story_text_a:
In 1936, archaeology professor and adventurer Dr. Jones, nicknamed "Indiana Jones" or "Indy", discovers a temple dotted with traps in the Peruvian jungle and steals a golden idol. Leaving the temple, his French rival Belloq waits for him with warriors of the natives and takes the figure back, Indy escapes at the last second with a seaplane.
Back at his university, he and Brody, the university curator, receive a visit from two representatives of American military intelligence. They instruct Indy to secure the Ark of the Covenant before it falls into Hitler's hands, who also sends for it. There are many myths surrounding the Ark, so an army with the Ark at its head is said to be invincible.
After initial skepticism, Indy takes the job. First, he needs the head of Re's staff, a kind of amulet that can help him locate the Ark's whereabouts. It's owned by Marion Ravenwood, the daughter of Indy's former mentor and his estranged love, who lives as a bar owner in Nepal. Indy flies there, but Marion resents him for ditching her years ago, and doesn't hand him the head piece. As soon as Indy leaves her bar, the Nazi thugs appear around Gestapo Major Toht, who also covets the head. Before Toht can torture Marion, Indy shows up and a fight breaks out, leading to a fire. The head falls into the flame, and when Toht tries to take it, the blazing metal burns into his hand. He escapes and Indy is able to defeat the remaining attackers, but Marion's bar burns down.
With the rescued head piece, the two of them will travel to Cairo. With Belloc's help, the Nazis under Colonel Dietrich have found the ancient city of Tanis and are digging for the Ark. Indy's old friend Sallah has insight into the Germans' excavation work. The Nazis, however, are on their trail. Marion is kidnapped and apparently killed in an explosion, while Indy and Sallah escape multiple assassination attempts. Sallah tells that the Nazis are using a replica of the head to dig for a hall called the "Fountain of Souls" where the Ark is supposed to be located. Indy has the inscription of his headpiece translated and learns that the staff for the headpiece must be six kadams long. But on the back of the headpiece, it says that you must wear a kadam in honor of the Hebrew god. Since the Nazis with the burn scar on Toht's hand only have the front of the headpiece, they miscalculated the length and dug in the wrong place.
After reuniting with Indy Belloq in a bar, Sallah helps him into the so-called card room, a hall with a model of Tanis and a hole in the ceiling. Indy puts a stick of the right length, with the headpiece at the top, in a certain spot, and as the sun shines through the ceiling opening at the right angle, the crystal in the center of the headpiece concentrates the sun's rays and illuminates in the model of the city the building where the box is supposed to be.
With some workers at night, Indy finds the opening to the "Fountain of Souls" and the box, but they are surprised by Belloq and Dietrich. They transport the crate and lock Indy and Marion in the building, the floor of which is covered with hundreds of snakes. Indy finds an exit and pursues Dietrich's wagon column on horseback. After a chase, he can take the truck with the trunk. Sallah arranges for him, Marion and the box to board a cargo ship, but it is picked up on the high seas by a German submarine. Dietrich and Belloq take over the cargo and put Marion on the sub, but Indy manages to sneak aboard before it sinks.
On an island north of Crete, the submarine, commanded by Oskar Schomburg, is stuck in a camouflaged submarine harbor. Inside the island, Belloq and Dietrich want to open the box. Indy tries to free Marion by threatening to destroy the crate with a tank fist. But Belloq realizes that Indy is bluffing and can't destroy this precious historical artifact, and has him arrested. In the evening, Belloq celebrates a ritual in which, in addition to Dietrich and Toht, numerous soldiers also participate, as well as Indy and Marion, who are tied to a pole. Belloq, in the garb of a high priest, utters an incantation, and two soldiers lift the lid of the ark. This, however, contains only the dust of the shattered tablets of the Law of Moses. Suddenly, all the electrical appliances explode, and supernatural, ghostly lights float out of the box and surround those present. Indy begs Marion not to look under any circumstances. Finally, lightning strikes the box and melts everyone in it except Indy and Marion, who survive the inferno with their eyes closed. Finally, the lid of the ark is hurled upward by a huge pillar of fire, landing back on the ark and closing it.
Back home, Indy and Brody will be denied any further access to the federal vault. Government officials assure them that the box is currently being investigated by "absolute specialists". In reality, however, the box is stored in a wooden box labeled "Top Secret" and housed in a huge government storage facility with thousands of other similar wooden boxes. Finally, Indy and Marion are reunited.
story_text_b: Amelia Earhart was an American aviation pioneer and an exceptional woman. The first woman to fly across the Atlantic, she was one of the most famous and admired figures of her time.

story_text_a:
Young Alfred "Al" Yankovic is interested in parodying songs, which his father disapproves of, to the point of destroying the accordion his mother had secretly bought him. Years later, he tries to join bands as an accordionist, but is constantly rejected. While listening to "My Sharona" on the radio and preparing a mortadella sandwich, Al is inspired to write "My Bologna" (for the Bologna sausage).
Her first hits are "I Love Rocky Road", performed with her roommates, and "Another One Rides the Bus", a parody of Queen's "Another One Bites the Dust", with the band's bassist, John Deacon, present. With these hits Al gets a record deal, and his debut album goes multi-platinum, with the original artists experiencing a "Yankovic hit" in record sales and Al being courted by Oprah Winfrey.
Later, under the influence of LSD that radio DJ Dr. Demento mixed it with guacamole, Al comes up with a new original song, which becomes his next hit, "Eat It". On the other hand, Madonna, in search of the "Yankovic hit", begins a relationship with Al to convince him to parody her song "Like a Virgin", although he insists that he only wants to write original songs.
Just before a major show, Al learns that Michael Jackson took "Eat It" and parodied it as "Beat It", which angers him because he thinks people will assume that "Eat It" is actually a parody of "Beat It". Drunk, he suffers a car accident and is rushed to the hospital, where he comes up with "Like a Surgeon". He premieres the song at a show that same night, while still gravely wounded, but when he is reminded that "Eat It" is the last song of the show, he gets drunk again, insults the crowd, and is arrested.
Once released, Al confesses to Madonna that he fears he has disappointed everyone who cared about him and that she is the only one he has left. Suddenly, Madonna is captured by agents of Pablo Escobar, who is a big fan of Al and uses the kidnapping to force him to play at his fortieth birthday party. Al flies to Colombia and breaks into Escobar's compound, where he confronts the drug kingpin. After refusing to play him a song, he gets involved in a shootout and kills Escobar and his mercenaries, freeing Madonna, who tries to convince him to quit music and help her take over Escobar's drug empire, but Al rejects her.
Al returns home to work in his father's factory, as this had always wanted; but his father admits that he always believed that Al did not belong in that world and that, secretly, had supported the path he had taken, all the time. He reveals to his son that he grew up in an Amish community and was excommunicated for playing the accordion, which led him to prevent Al from making the same mistake. Then, Al sings a song by his father, "Amish Paradise", on stage, earning him a major award in 1985, before being murdered on stage by one of Madonna's henchmen.
story_text_b:
# General presentation
In an industrial town, a man with no history, Henry Spencer, is forced to care for his premature and monstrous newborn child alone after his wife leaves the marital home. To escape his oppressive daily life, marked by the cries of the baby, he takes refuge in a parallel world where the  Lady of the radiator  resides.
# Detailed synopsis
Eraserhead begins with a sequence in space. The camera zooms in on a planet where there is a small cabin in which a man disfigured by burns (Jack Fisk) pulls levers. One of the levers triggers the fall of an umbilical cord into a puddle. Gradually emerging from the pool, the light becomes more and more intense until it fades to white.
Henry Spencer (Jack Nance) is a nervous-looking printer on vacation. The young man walks to his apartment, through a semi-industrial, semi-port neighborhood, derelict buildings, vacant lots and dreary streets. His next-door neighbor informs him that he is invited to the parents of his girlfriend, Mary X (Charlotte Stewart), who had not contacted him for a long time. Henry thought she'd ended their relationship.
The meal at the in-laws' house takes place in an atmosphere prone to malaise. Mary X's mother (Jeanne Bates) genuinely stalks Henry while Mary's father (Allen Joseph) is a character totally disconnected from the tense situation around the table. After attempting to cut up a chicken that died and leaked a black liquid, Henry learns that he is the father of Mary's premature child. He is therefore obliged to marry her.
Mary and the baby move into Henry's one-room apartment. The child is seen for the first time, a baby with the appearance of a fetus of lamb and hideously deformed, who never ceases to groan. These sobs will get the better of Mary, who, unable to sleep, leaves Henry and leaves him alone with the little creature.
This departure is followed by a series of the strangest events, including meeting the Lady in the Radiator, a blonde woman with grotesquely bloated cheeks in the Betty Boop style, who sings and lives on the small stage of a music-hall hidden in the radiator in Henry's bedroom. He will then have a sexual relationship with his neighbor, the  pretty girl across the hall  (Beautiful Girl Across the Hall).
The title Eraserhead takes on its full meaning during the last quarter of the film. Henry's head then detaches from his body and plunges into a pool of blood, falling from the sky to land in an alley where it opens. A young boy (Thomas Coulson) finds the head and takes it to a pencil factory where Paul (Darwin Joston), a receptionist, calls his boss (Neil Moran) by pressing the button of a bell. The furious boss enters the room but immediately changes his mood when he sees what the boy has brought them. The head is taken to another room where a pencil-making machine operator (Hal Landon Jr.) takes a sample of Henry's brain and applies it to the tip of a pencil. He tests this "gum" which proves effective, and the young boy is paid by the boss of the factory. The image of Henry in his bed later suggests that this whole sequence was just a dream.
A little later, Henry sees through his window two men fighting in the street. He tries to go see his pretty neighbor across the hall, but she's with another man. The baby is seized with a sarcastic laugh, so Henry takes a pair of scissors and cuts the bandages in which the child is wrapped. It soon becomes apparent that they are directly targeting the creature's vital organs. As the baby screams in pain, Henry plunges the scissors into her lungs. The electrical system in the apartment goes out and the lights start blinking and then they go out. A giant child's head appears in the room. Henry returns to the small stage of the music hall where the radiator lady welcomes him tenderly into her arms. The stage is flooded with light and a white noise makes a crescendo. Then everything goes dark and silent for a few seconds before the end credits.

story_text_a:
In 1874, the U.S. government encroaches on the lands of the Lakota people. Mattotaupa, an Oglala Lakota man, gambles with Red Fox, a White criminal, in a saloon. When seeing he has gold, Red Fox demands to know its origin. Mattotaupa refuses, and Red Fox murders him. Mattotaupa's son, the young and fierce warrior Tokei-ihto who distrusts the Whites and never drinks their "Firewater", witnesses the murder.
Two years later, Tokei-ihto is the war chieftain of the Oglala's Bear Band and one of Crazy Horse's commanders in the Great Sioux War. He raids a resupply column sent to a U.S. Army fort, but brings the commander's daughter Katie Smith to her father unharmed, requesting to negotiate peace. Major Smith turns him down, and one of his officers tries to shoot the chieftain, who then surprises the soldiers and single-handedly destroys their munitions depot.
The warriors return to their camp victorious. Red Fox arrives, offering a peace treaty. Tokei-ihto is sent to negotiate. Smith demands they settle in a reservation. When Tokei-ihto rejects the offer, he is imprisoned. The Bear Band are brutally forced to resettle.
After several months, the war has ended. Red Fox enters Tokei-ihto's cell, trying to force him to reveal the location of the gold mine. Katie Smith and her friend Adams stop him before he begins to torture the captive. They recommend that after being released, he should take his people to Canada. The chieftain accepts the government's terms and returns to the reservation.
Tokei-ihto ventures to the sacred caves of the Great She-Bear, the Band's Totem animal, which are also the gold's source, to seek the blessing of the spirits to their departure. Red Fox's henchman Pitt goes after him, hoping to find gold. He stumbles upon a she-bear which kills him, though not before he fatally wounds her with a gunshot. Tokei-ihto finds the she-bear's cub. He takes it back to the tribe.
The Bear Band leave. They raid an army column, and General George Crook offers a $200 reward on the chieftain's head. Red Fox, still seeking the gold, sets after them with a large group of ruffians. They gain on the Lakota as they cross the Missouri River. Red Fox agrees to let the people move on undisturbed if Tokei-ihto would remain behind. The chieftain agrees. After a prolonged fight, he manages to kill Red Fox. The band settle on the other bank, finding refuge.
story_text_b:
Mark Dixon is a police detective who was just demoted over his too-frequent use of violence. Because his own father was a criminal, he hates them even more than is acceptable to the force.
At a floating crap game in New York City run by gangster Tommy Scalise, the beautiful Morgan Taylor decides to leave for the night, with or without the man, Ken Paine, who brought her there.  Effusive Texas tycoon Morrison offers to escort her home. This upsets Scalise, as Morrison is up $19,000 on his bank. Morrison says he is in town all week and "you'll get it back another night," but Paine tells Morgan she has to stay. She realizes he only brought her to the game so Morrison would follow, and is now determined to leave.
Paine slaps Morgan, whereupon Morrison starts a fistfight with Paine. Morrison is knocked out, but when the police arrive he has been stabbed to death. Dixon is one of the officers on the scene. He interrogates Scalise, whom he arrested two years earlier for murder but who was acquitted.
Scalise tells several lies about the crime, and implicates Paine. Dixon goes to Paine's apartment and questions him, but Paine becomes angry and starts a fight. Defending himself, Dixon does not know that a war injury has left Paine with a metal plate in his skull. When Paine falls, he hits his head and dies.
After his recent reprimand, Dixon does not dare report what has happened. Borrowing Paine's coat and putting a bandage on his own face where Paine had one, he lays a false trail suggesting that Paine has left town. Back at Paine's apartment he is almost seen by Morgan's father, cab driver Jiggs Taylor, who arrives and (having found out that Paine had slapped his daughter) noisily threatens him from outside his door, then leaves when there is no answer. Dixon then takes the body and dumps it in the river. It is soon found and, moving to cover himself, Dixon suggests that Scalise murdered Paine as well as Morrison.
As the case develops the detectives talk to Morgan and Jiggs Taylor. It is revealed that Morgan is Paine's estranged wife; the night of the murder is the first time she has seen him in months. She and Dixon begin to fall in love. In spite of Dixon's insisting that Scalise is the killer, Jiggs had been seen at Paine's apartment and is arrested. Dixon cannot bear to tell Morgan the truth, but he arranges to pay for a top lawyer for Jiggs, one who has never lost a murder case. For unspecified reasons the lawyer refuses a retainer.
After a fruitless confrontation with Scalise, Dixon writes a letter, addressing the envelope to Inspector Foley and marking it "to be opened in the event of my death." He then arranges to meet with Scalise again, fully expecting to be murdered but reasoning that at least this time Scalise will be held responsible. Scalise has anticipated this, too, and has realized what happened to Paine. He refuses to kill Dixon, who is shot in his arm instead. Then one of Scalise's men arrives with the news that the police have gotten the truth about Morrison out of another gang member. As the gang attempts escape in a car elevator, Dixon manages to delay them by stalling it until the police arrive.
Back at the 16th Precinct, Foley - extremely proud of Dixon's work trapping Scalise - returns Dixon's letter to him, unopened, but Dixon tells him to read it. Foley arrests Dixon. Morgan is present, looking forward to starting a life with Dixon. Perplexed, she asks why he is now being taken into custody; Dixon asks Foley to show her the letter. Even knowing the truth her love for Dixon is undaunted. She confidently declares that he will not be punished for the accidental death.

story_text_a:
The books switches from character to character, following Italian soldiers in Beirut, flashbacks of their lives before they came to the city, their Lebanese sweethearts, Lebanese Christian and Shi'ite militants, and a group of French nuns. If anyone could be called the protagonist of the story, it would be Angelo, a confused Italian soldier who abandoned his studies of mathematics in order to enlist as a conscript in the Italian army and see war first-hand. Angelo's interest in Mathematics is reflective of Fallaci's lover, the Greek politician and rebel Alexandros Panagoulis, who also studied mathematics at the Athens Polytechnion and attempted to prove mathematical theorems in his own blood whilst in jail.
But the real inspirer and leading actor of the novel is "Charlie", to which the author devotes many pages and between the lines attributed the success of the Italian contingent which left Lebanon unscathed. Charlie, a character of course inspired by Captain Corrado Cantatore (multi decorated just for his Lebanese exploits). Cantatore arrived in Lebanon many years before the Italian contingent, as a volunteer in the UN and was probably recruited by the famous Colonel Stefano Giovannone of Italian intelligence. Cantatore grew with Giovannone and when Giovannone left Lebanon, Cantatore  had already woven his network that so impressed Oriana Fallaci and assured the safety to the Italians. The commanding Officer of the Italian Contingent, General Franco Angioni, before taking command of the expeditionary unit had served as Chief of Operations of the Army Staff, in charge of the Italian Military  personnel serving in United Nations organizations (UNIFIL and UNTSO)  in Middle East. Angioni was therefore aware of the peculiar capacity of the Captain Cantatore, and just landed off the ship in the Beirut harbor had given him the task of liaising with all Lebanese factions, under the cover of the press information officer. Cantatore received and accompanied all the journalists who visited the contingent and was the officer who spent more time overall with Oriana Fallaci who, struck by the extraordinary quality of the Captain, decided to spend the last night of the Italian Contingent in Lebanon in the office of Captain Cantatore (so called "Arab Bureau") with him. One last curiosity is that the code name "Charlie - Charlie" was born from the extraction of aeronautics of Cantatore (he was a pilot of fix wings and attack helicopters): at the arrival of the Italian Contingent, when Angioni asked to choose a Radio call sign distinct from those used in his headquarters (Condor, Eagle, Ruby, etc.). was natural for Cantatore take his initials, just CC, which was designed "Charlie - Charlie" in the NATO phonetic alphabet in use among the pilots and control towers. Cantatore, when returned from Lebanon disappeared from the scene, he was great friend of Oriana Fallaci, it seems, he has continued to work for the' Italian intelligence.
Angelo finds war not as he expected, and he is shocked at the irrationality and barbarity of the civil war engulfing Beirut. Whilst on guard duty, he meets Ninette, a beautiful Christian Lebanese woman with whom he cannot communicate as she pretends not to speak French for reasons unknown to Angelo. Still, they are attracted to each other and they begin a relationship. Angelo is tormented by the fact that their relationship is primarily physical, and also on his growing reliance on Ninette.
While expecting a visit from Ninette, Hizbollah bombs the American marine barracks as well as French paratroopers barracks. Angelo is ordered to photograph the rescue efforts of Italian soldiers, but he is too horrified by the carnage to accomplish the task. On the way back to purchases Ninette an anchor shaped cross with the Virgin Mary inscribed on it to apologize for missing their rendez-vous.
Subplots are developed between a group of Italian soldiers billeted in a Catholic monastery and the French nuns, as well as the negotiations between Italian officers and Shi'ite militia leaders.
Angelo's friend Gino, a gentle poet, is severely wounded by Khalid Passepartout, a vicious child soldier in the service of the Shi'ite militia "the Sons of God." Gino loses his fingers, and can no longer write poetry. Angelo vows revenge, and during an encounter with Ninette he leaves early to visit Gino in the hospital and tells her that he cannot spend Christmas with her due to Gino's condition. He admits to her that friendship is more important than love to him, and this hurts Ninette who expresses to him in a letter, written in perfect French, that she can no longer see him. Angleo realizes how much he loves Ninette and vainly searches for her throughout the city.
French paratroopers vacating a tower in the center of Beirut causes fighting to break out between Amal, a Shi'ite militia and mainly Christian government forces. In the turmoil Passpartout sees Ninette, who he sees in the street after she goes to the Italian post to see if Angelo is all right, and gives her his Kalashnikov, as he wants to run away. After being chastised by his officer and pedophilic lover, Rashid, he returns to Ninette demanding that his gun be returned and accusing her of theft. Despite warnings from passers-by that she will be killed if she returns the gun as she is a Christian, she returns the gun and Passepartout shoots her shouting "Christian! Whore! Spy!" Ninette is buried in a mass grave.
Angelo's officer finds out the news, and tells Angelo who is shattered. Angelo again vows revenge, and whilst on guard duty he encounters Passepartout who is wearing Gino's bersaglieri helmet. Through a discussion, Angelo forgives Passepartout for killing his friend as he is only a child, but then rather than running away Passepartout attempts to sell Angelo an anchor shaped cross with the Virgin Mary on it. Angelo recognizes that this was the cross that he had given Ninette. In a fit of rage Angelo realizes that Passepartout killed not only his friend, but his lover, and Angelo kills Passepartout.
Rashid finds out that an Italian killed his lover, Passepartout, and vows vengeance. He plans a suicided bombing against the Italian's boats as they plan to leave. The Italian commanders struggle to strike a deal with the Shi'ite militia to avert catastrophe. Angelo discovers by chance in a magazine that Ninette was really an elegant Lebanese woman named Natalia Narakat who had been married to an assassinated political leader, who looked quite a bit like Angelo which is what attracted her to him in the first place. In the interview she states that the meaning of life is contained in the word "in sha Allah"-- "as God wills"—there is no rationality, no way to predict the future, just a series of events that are all interlocking but completely incomprehensible when viewed above from human eyes. Angelo is deeply moved and abandons his quest to formulate life in mathematical terms.
The French nuns who quartered the Italian troops are raped and murdered by Shi'ite militiamen, who desecrate their church. The novel ends with the Italians departing after striking a deal with a Shi'ite cleric for their safety in exchange for supplies. The Shi'ite promise to give the alcohol and pork to Christian Lebanese, but instead they destroy it. In the final scene Angelo looks across the prow of the boat and sees Rashid's motorboat speeding towards the Italian convoy.
story_text_b:
The story opens on the morning of Sunday, October 23, 1983, when two vehicles loaded with 5,400 kilograms of explosives each destroy the headquarters of the American 1st Battalion 8th Marines (causing two hundred and forty-one dead and sixty wounded) and that of the 3e compagnie du 1er régiment de chasseurs parachutistes (causing fifty-eight dead and fifteen wounded) in Beirut. The command of the Italian contingent is astonished, and there are several minutes in which there is a fear that another truck may be directed against the Italian contingent. The Italian contingent had, however, come to know, through some informants in Charlie's pay (who organized a sort of "Arab office" on the basis of the one organized by Lawrence of Arabia during the First World War) of the preparation of the attacks, and had informed the allied commanders who, however, had ignored the warning, it will be found later that disagreements within the Islamist groups "stopped" the third truck. Some Italian soldiers who arrive at the scene of the attack find themselves faced with an unimaginable horror: dead soldiers, beheaded, mutilated, crushed and even a little girl who, due to the displacement of air from the explosion, was thrown into the exhaust of a toilet and reduced "to a human sausage".
Immediately after the attention is focused on the Italian contingent, in particular on some soldiers, almost all indicated by a nickname.
Through episodes of their lives and the narration of what happens in the various locations of the contingent, all the characters around whom the events of the novel will unfold are introduced. At the Contingent Command, under the leadership of the "Condor", the soldiers of the command department are housed; in a basement there is Charlie's "Arab office" that manages relations with Arab informants and negotiations with the local people, such as the powerful imam Zandra Sadr. The Rubino base, headquarters of the contingent of paratroopers commanded by Falco, is instead in an abandoned convent; the return of the nuns who previously inhabited it causes many problems of coexistence between nuns and soldiers, until the relations do not extend and even some officers (such as Armando from the Golden Hands and Falco himself) will let themselves be involved in more or less explicit sentimental relationships with the nuns. Sierra Mike is home to the Navy's San Marco Battalion, commanded by Sandokan an officer so named for his pirate-like appearance and bellicose attitude. As events unfold, he undergoes a great transformation in his personality from a fierce warmonger to a quiet pacifist, like his father. The Italian contingent is completed by the snipers guarding the Palestinian refugee camps and the soldiers of the logistics battalion. Characters outside the Italian contingent are also introduced, such as Ninette, a young and attractive woman with purple eyes with whom the Italian soldier Angelo, the protagonist of the novel, will live a very tormented relationship, and disturbing people such as Khalid "Passepartout", teenage street Amal, a prostitute and Islamic fundamentalist, Rashid, Passepartout's protector as well as a fierce fundamentalist, and Captain Gassàn, a former Maronite Christian medical student who became an officer of the Lebanese Regular Army to avenge the death of his father.
The protagonists live personal anguish and conduct research that can not lead to anything concrete: the search for the formula of Angelo's life, the secret disappointment of Charlie for having always been a winner, the blind obedience of Zucchero and the sadness for the loss of the ancient chivalric values of Crazy Horse.
The third act opens on 25 December 1983, when the French contingent leaves "the tower", an important position that could bring strong tactical advantages to one or the other faction. The Italians, the sub-organization for Christmas leave, can only keep it until 5:00. Once the tower is abandoned, the battle breaks out between the Shiite militiamen (the Amal) and the government army. The description of the battle is very long and detailed, and also reveals the great abilities of the Fallaci and his knowledge of the war environment. When it ends, while an Italian soldier goes to bury a Shia girl victim of the clashes, the Muslim forces in the regular army begin to side with their co-religionists. From here begins a chain of events that will lead irretrievably to the death sentence of the Italian force. Angelo kills Khalid "Passepartout", who had killed Ninette and maimed a close friend of Charlie's with a fragmentation hand grenade Rdg 8: it becomes clear that the goal of a quiet re-embarkation of the contingent will be unattainable. The illogic of the gesture is underlined by the fact that just as Angelo shoots at Passepartout, the shrapnel from a bomb searches his body: Passepartout would have died anyway, examining his body, however, Rashid, an important leader of the Amal and Passepartout's lover-protector, notices a bullet hole. The last weeks narrated are in fact tense and unbearable; especially the last, when it has now been decided to abandon Lebanon, which sees a desperate negotiation between Charlie and Zandra Sadr to guarantee Italian troops a safe return to the homeland. The Italians leave, not without hesitation, in the hands of the Arabs almost all the food reserves they had brought and the field hospital. All alcohol and pork, as condemned by the Koran, are burned, the rest looted and medical equipment looted. Rashid, mad at the loss of Passepartout, climbs aboard a speedboat loaded with explosives and heads for one of the three ships taking the soldiers back to Italy.

story_text_a: Roy Clayton, an FBI agent, and his colleague Max Archer are investigating Islamic terror cells that are plotting attacks in the West. The agents suspect Samir Horn, whose identity is still unclear: whether he is one of the main terrorists or an American infiltrator.
story_text_b:
Samir Horn (Don Cheadle) is an American ex-soldier and devout Muslim whose specialty is the manufacture of explosive devices with Centec plastic explosive to radical Islamic factions, Horn sells a powerful explosive used by radical Islamists for their attacks against the United States.
Horn is actually a CIA infiltrator whose mission is unknown to the FBI and who seeks to track down the leaders of these Islamic terrorist factions, especially Nathir, the leader who leads them.
To make the mission more credible, Horn is detained in a Yemeni prison where Omar (Saïd Taghmaoui) is imprisoned and gains his trust when he is rescued by his friends from outside. Then Horn gets into a world full of radicalized Islamic ideals and mistrust where he contacts the group of "Nathir" who carry out attacks in Spain and France; for this Horn to make credible his conviction by this group of terrorists blows up an embassy of the United States under construction causing several deaths (in reality a screen of apparent deaths) then earning Horn his complete trust being able to meet Nathir, the leader of the terrorists.
However in the FBI there is an informant who keeps Omar up to date as the FBI investigations evolve, the search actions are headed by agents Alex Clayton (Guy Pearce) and Max Archer (Neal McDonough) who are desperately looking for Horn believing that he is a genuine radical Islamic terrorist.
The terrorists are planning for Thanksgiving a masterstroke with about 30 Islamic American citizens who will serve as suicide martyrs and who will board crowded buses of people to blow them up with themselves.

story_text_a:
Matko Destanov, a small-time Romani smuggler and profiteer, lives with his teenage son Zare in a ramshackle house by the Danube River in eastern Serbia near the Bulgarian border.  He has plans to steal a whole train of smuggled fuel. To obtain a loan that would subsidize the heist, he visits Grga Pitić, a wheelchair-using old gangster, who is an old friend of Zarije Destanov, Matko's father and Zare's grandfather. Matko plots the details of the job with an ally named Dadan, a rich, fun-living, drug-snorting gangster who has a harem, juggles grenades, and cheats at gambling. However, Dadan double-crosses him and glitches up the deal by giving Matko a drink that is drugged, and carrying out the job while Matko is unconscious.  Matko is unable to repay his loan, so Dadan makes a deal whereby he would forgive the debt if Zare marries Afrodita, Dadan's dwarf sister. However, Zare (17) is in love with Ida (26), a barmaid who works in an establishment run by her Roma grandmother Sujka, and Afrodita is waiting for the man of her dreams. Dadan coerces Afrodita into marrying by dunking her in a well, while Zare first learns of the scheme to marry him off from Ida, who has overheard Dadan and Matko plotting it in the restaurant where she works. Meanwhile, Zare retrieves Zarije from the hospital where he is being kept, with the aid of a gypsy band. Grga Pitić is having problems of his own, as he wants his grandsons, including the 2.00m giant Grga Veliki, to get married.
The two reluctantly endure the wedding ceremony held at Matko's house, which Dadan refuses to postpone despite the sudden apparent death of Zarije. They were not supposed to have a wedding while in mourning, but Dadan decides to delay the death announcement, so Matko and Zare hide Zarije's body in the attic, packed in ice. Ida and Sujka provide the catering for the wedding, and Ida is upset at seeing her beloved married to someone else. However, the bride runs away mid-ceremony, pursued by Dadan, Matko and Dadan's criminal cronies. Meanwhile, Grga Veliki is driving his father and brother to Matko's house so that they may visit Zarije's grave (Grga Pitić and Zarije  old friends). The fleeing bride stumbles across Grga Veliki, and the couple fall instantly in love. Grga Pitić arrives on the scene, after his wheelchair had fallen out the back of the truck and rolled downhill, and he is delighted that Grga Veliki has found his mate. The old gangster forces Dadan, who had once worked for him, to accept the match.
The groom conspires with Sujka and Ida to bring Dadan down a peg, and rigs the outhouse so that the seat will come apart. While the preparations for the wedding ceremony of Afrodita and Grga Veliki are being conducted, Matko and Dadan pass the time by playing dice, with Dadan cheating. Sujka comes in during the game, and serves the unsuspecting Dadan a drink spiked with a laxative. Grga Pitić apparently dies, and Dadan and Matko hide his body in the attic, where Zarije's body is also hidden. However, the two corpses soon both come back to life; they were not dead after all. They are surprised to find themselves together, as they had not seen each other for 25 years and each had thought the other was dead. During the ceremony, Dadan starts to feel uncomfortable and rushes into the outhouse, only to fall into the manure. His harem and cronies desert him, and as he tries to clean himself off on a goose, only Matko remains loyal, and he provides Dadan with a shower from the garden hose. Zare grabs the wedding official at gunpoint and orders him to solemnize his marriage with his sweetheart, Ida, and the two sail off together on a riverboat set for Bulgaria with a fistful of cash stashed in his grandfather's accordion, the blessing of their respective grandparents and, as witnesses, a black cat and a white cat.
story_text_b:
Sonny Hooper (Burt Reynolds) is the stunt coordinator on the action film The Spy Who Laughed at Danger, directed by Roger Deal (Robert Klein) and starring Adam West (playing himself). Sonny's antics and wisecracks are a trial for the egotistical director and his officious but cowardly assistant, Tony (Alfie Wise). Years of numerous "gags" and his use of alcohol and painkillers are beginning to take their toll. Sonny lives with his girlfriend Gwen Doyle (Sally Field), whose father Jocko (Brian Keith) is a retired stuntman.
Sonny is coerced by a friend into performing at a charity show, where he meets Delmore "Ski" Shidski (Jan-Michael Vincent), a newcomer who makes a spectacular entrance. They become friends after a barroom brawl, and Sonny invites Ski to work with him on the film. They begin a friendly rivalry in which the dangerous stunts escalate. After a freefall from a record 224 ft (68 m), Sonny quietly consults with his doctor, who warns him that one more bad fall could render him quadriplegic.
Roger decides to change the film's ending, adding a climactic earthquake complete with many explosions, fires and car crashes. Sonny and Ski would race through the carnage to a nearby gorge, where the bridge explodes before they can cross it. Roger suggests they rappel down one side of the gorge and up the other to safety, but Ski proposes jumping a car over the gorge, with Hooper adding that a rocket car can make the 335-foot (102 m) jump.  Roger loves the idea, ignoring the warnings that Sonny and Ski might not survive the landing even if the car lands on its wheels. Max Berns, the movie's producer and a longtime friend of Sonny's, warns Roger that the film is already over budget and they can't afford the $100,000 Hooper wants to perform the rocket car jump. Roger tells Max he wants the rocket car ending and to make cuts elsewhere. Tony is sent to talk Hooper down from his high price, but fails.
Meanwhile, Jocko suffers a stroke, but denies the gravity of his condition. Seeing Jocko in the hospital motivates Sonny to promise Gwen that he will quit the business after the film wraps.  Then, Sonny's assistant and best friend Cully (James Best) reveals the rocket car stunt and Sonny's secret visit to his doctor to a horrified Gwen.  Sonny later tells Roger that he is backing out of the gag, but Max convinces him to reconsider, as no qualified stuntman is available, or willing, to replace him and Ski cannot do it alone. Having no other choice, and even after Gwen threatens to leave him, Sonny goes through with the gag.
Sonny and Ski perform the first part of the gag perfectly. As they arrive at the now-demolished bridge, they find that the rocket pressure is below the minimum needed to make the jump, but they attempt it anyway.  The rocket car clears the gorge, but overshoots the prepared landing area and lands hard on the far side. Ski emerges from the car on his own, but the impact is more of a shock to Sonny's system. Gwen tearfully pushes her way through the gathering crowd as the chief engineer extracts Sonny from the car. Sonny slowly comes out of his daze and takes Gwen in his arms.
As Sonny, Ski, Gwen, Cully and Jocko view the bridge lying in the river and the gorge the rocket car had jumped, Roger comes up to them and tries to apologize for all the grief he gave him during filming, but he comes off as trying to justify himself. Sonny's response is to knock Roger out with a single punch. He, Gwen, Ski, Cully and Jocko then triumphantly walk off the set.

story_text_a:
# Content
Successful child psychiatrist Dr. Malcolm Crowe is being honored by the city of Philadelphia for his service. While celebrating with his wife, the couple is surprised by an intruder in the bedroom. Turns out it's a former patient of Crowe's, Vincent Grey, whom he hadn't been able to help as a child overcome his fears that haunt him to this day. The desperate, deranged man shoots Dr. Crowe and then kills himself.
The following year, Dr. Crowe cares for nine-year-old Cole, who strongly reminds him of his former patient Grey, which is why the case excites him. Cole seems to be plagued by great fears that he doesn't confide in anyone. He is teased and shunned by his classmates as a "psycho". However, he pretends to his mother that he will be accepted in school. Still, Cole's mother is desperate because of his fears. Even Dr. Crowe doesn't seem to be able to help the boy at first. When Cole is invited to a birthday party, he is bullied by other children and, locked in a small room, experiences something that leaves him deeply traumatized and unconscious. At the hospital, the psychologist visits his little patient and promises not to leave him alone. Cole finally tells him his secret: "I see dead people. They're mad. They don't know they're dead.
At first, Dr. Crowe doesn't believe him and diagnoses him delusional, but then he has doubts, and as he revisits the case of his former patient Vincent Grey, he notices strange voices on an old tape recording he made during a session with this boy. He realizes that Cole told him the truth and that his former patient must have seen or heard Vincent Tote, too. He advises Cole not to be afraid of the dead, but to listen to them and try to help them. Cole first succeeds in the case of little Kyra, who has been gradually poisoned by her own mother. Cole helps the dead girl uncover the murder case for the survivors while also protecting Kira's younger sister as a possible next victim from her mother. From then on, his life changes for the better. It becomes clear that the people Cole sees have all died violently and need his help to end their lives.
Ever since Dr. Crowe was shot, he's been estranged from his wife. The two do not speak to each other, not even on their wedding day, when Crowe meets his wife late at a restaurant and she leaves upon his arrival. Dr. Crowe is deeply troubled by this, partly because he thinks he is watching his wife gradually fall in love with a coworker and start a new relationship. Cole advises him to talk to his wife when she has just fallen asleep. Conversely, the psychologist suggests that the boy should also confide in an important person. Cole tells his mother that he can see dead people and that his grandmother sometimes visits him. At first, the mother doesn't believe her son, but when Cole tells her secrets that only she and the dead grandmother can know, she shrugs Cole in her shocked but happy arms.
After Dr. Crowe's wife falls asleep while watching her wedding video, her husband tries to talk to her again; she reacts to him, half-asleeply asking him why he left her. Crowe is confused, claiming he didn't leave her after all, when his wedding ring falls from her hands to the ground. It makes him realize that he's been dead himself since Grey shot him that night. Only Cole could see him, just like the other dead men. He also realizes that his wife is grieving for him. He finally accepts his death and leaves his sleeping widow. He considers his duty to help Cole, to make up for his failure to help Grey, fulfilled.
# Form
The plot of the story is divided into two parallel storylines, which are linked in many places. The one storyline tells Cole's story as it unfolds since his first encounter with Malcolm Crowe. The other plot line is, without the viewer noticing it at first, of Malcolm's story from the night he was shot by his former patient. Both storylines are told from a personal point of view. Since the narrative is neutral and like that of an observer, an authoritarian narrator's attitude is to be excluded. This parallel between the storylines is maintained until the end, because after Cole tells his mother that he can see ghosts, Malcolm opens up to reality and suddenly realizes that he himself is a ghost that his wife cannot see. The mother and the wife serve in this parabolic narrative as a projection for the main characters to come to self-knowledge and thus to change. Both main characters need each other in this quest for knowledge and arrive at the solution by entering on each other.
story_text_b: The two friends Folcacchio and Gulfardo are on their way as messengers to deliver a message to the Bishop of Volterra. On the journey, the two meet a young peasant woman, the blonde Gemmata. Folcacchio sleeps with her and then falls in love. In order to be able to be intimate with her once again, the friends of Gemmata's husband play a story: In the stable, a mare would turn into his wife. Now that Folcacchio is intimate with Gemmata, her husband believes the young man is only doing it with a horse. The word is out. Torello, nicknamed "the stallion" because of his enormous penis, also sleeps with Gemmata. Folcacchio does not envy him. While Torello has his fun, Folcacchio and Gulfardo move on and meet the Spaniard Matias. He shows them that there are gold coins hidden in a monastery. While the friends want to use the money to build an irrigation canal, Matias wants the money alone. After tricking him, they return to Gemmata's court, where Folacchio once again amuses himself with the "naked mare".

story_text_a:
The film takes place in the summer of 1941, after the events of A Christmas Story, which took place in December 1940. It has several plot lines, one each for 10-year-old Ralphie, his father, and his mother, followed by a recurring subplot involving him and his dad on a fishing trip, that proves frequently fruitless until a single night when all fish are caught. This also feeds a needless obsession in Ralphie's 7-year-old brother Randy, much to Mrs. Parker's nerve.
# Ralphie's plot
Ralphie's plot for most of the film is to find a top tough enough to knock that of a bully's out of a chalk circle in a game of "Kill". Scut Farkus, the 13-year-old main bully, was demoted following the events of A Christmas Story, with a new head bully, Lug Ditka, taking his place and ruling over the school. Despite his firm standing, Ralphie's tops are always defeated by Lug's top Mariah, prompting Ralphie to look for outside sources that also backfire, such as a top bought from an Eastern shop that is painted with roses, giving Lug all the mocking material. During the Parker family's visit to the world fair, Ralphie gets a top from a gypsy stand called "Wolf" just as powerful as Mariah, allowing Ralphie to challenge him again. However, at the climax of the challenge, both Mariah and Wolf end up disappearing into the sewer, never to be seen again; as a result, the game ends on a lose-lose draw.
# Mrs. Parker's plot
Mrs. Parker's plot revolves around attempting to start a collection of celebrity dishes, one per each dish night, at the Orpheum Theatre run by Leopold Doppler. She acquires the first dish, a Ronald Colman gravy boat, though she accumulates more as Doppler announces the other dishes are unavailable due to 'misshipment'. The frustration of accumulating the gravy boats combined with the events throughout the movie get Mrs. Parker over the edge, resulting her in throwing the gravy boat she won at the theater in Doppler's head. All other housewives, encouraged by Mrs. Parker's act, also start raining down the surplus gravy boats towards Doppler, enraged at the frustration and the apparent fraudulent scheme. Mrs. Parker is arrested for the act, though with a relieved smile on her face.
# Mr. Parker's plot
Mr. Parker's plot revolves around his odds with the Parker's hillbilly neighbors, the Bumpuses (or Bumpi, as the Parkers tend to refer them in plural), especially due to their loud overplaying of hillbilly music, obnoxious behavior and the constant harassment on Mr. Parker by the Bumpuses' forty-three Bloodhounds named Big Red. The escalation turns into war when the Bumpuses inaugurate an outhouse bathroom, which Parker clearly perceives as a health code violation. When Mr. Parker attempts forcing the Bumpuses to demolish the outhouse, they respond by having Big Dickie, the largest of the Bumpus family, destroy their house's porch as a show of force. Parker attempts unsuccessfully to torment the Bumpuses with music, which they mistake for Parker calling a night party, prompting him to hurriedly escape to the fishing trip with Ralphie. Mr. Parker does a second attempt, this time with a sound effects record disk simulating a federal bust, but by the time he unleashes the sound disk, the Bumpuses have long moved away. Mr. Parker interprets this as a defeat, and the act earns the ire of the woken-up neighborhood, who strongly suggest to bring the Bumpuses back and be rid of Parker.
story_text_b:
A prominent New England doctor has been murdered and his young nephew Felix is suspected of the murder.
Casual prostitute Angela Crispini hires private investigator Tom O'Toole to look for evidence that could exonerate Felix. She tells O'Toole that Felix is innocent and everyone knows the real culprit. O'Toole is in love with Crispini. His relationship suffers, and there are arguments.
O'Toole finds out that Crispini has been dating the prosecutor for two years, who is determined to make Felix a scapegoat. Besides, he's gonna find out that Jerry did the murder.
Crispini tells the prosecutor that many prominent locals are involved in the drug trade.
O'Toole convinces Jerry to tell the judge in charge everything. You go to Judge O'Toole in the car, Jerry on his motorcycle. On the way, Jerry drives on the wrong side of the road, gets run over by a truck, and gets killed. Crispini himself tells the judge about the events, after which Felix is released. O'Toole pressures the judge to prosecute the corrupt celebrities, but the judge refuses. Later, he sees Crispini visiting the judge privately.

story_text_a:
It is set in Jamaica in the mid-19th century and tells the prehistory of Edward Rochester, the protagonist of the novel Jane Eyre.
Antoinette Cosway grows up on the island as the heiress of a large plantation. Her mother becomes mentally unstable; her disabled brother dies. The plantation runs into financial difficulties, so Cosway marries Englishman Edward Rochester. She falls in love with him, but in time the couple become estranged. Cosway becomes mentally ill and is confined to her husband's mansion in England. This is the starting point for the plot of the novel Jane Eyre, in which Antoinette Cosway is presented only as a supporting character.
story_text_b: Antoniette, a young landowner in Jamaica in the 1840s, marries an English lord to avoid losing her lands. Everything seems to be going well between the two of them, but the woman is hiding a secret about her childhood and her mother. To complicate matters, Amelie, a young, mixed-race servant born to a Jamaican mother, will do anything to drive a wedge between them.

story_text_a:
# Hang up the phone
At the beginning of the 20th century, in a luxurious mansion lost in a corner of greenery, two women engaged in consensual sadomasochistic saphic games.
# Detailed summary
Evelyn studied lepidopterology with Cynthia, who frequently lectures on her studies. The former is in love with the latter, who employs her as a maid in his home, where she is subject to high expectations of behavior and standards of cleanliness. When Evelyn did not finish her chores to Cynthia's satisfaction, she punished her. It turns out that Cynthia is faltering more and more in her dominance and that Evelyn has orchestrated the role of her boss and lover by writing the instructions to follow for specific scenes in which the couple plays the same way every day.
While Evelyn achieves sexual arousal during these scenes, Cynthia acts only to satisfy the young woman's desires. In order to please Evelyn, Cynthia decides to ask a carpenter to build a bed with a drawer in order to lock her up all night as a punishment, but due to Evelyn's dissatisfaction with the time of making the bed, the project fails. A solution is found when Evelyn demands that Cynthia lock her in a crate for the night as further punishment. Although bitter, Cynthia agrees but is faced with a back pain at the time of lifting the chest into the bedroom, realizing that she is beginning to age.
As time passes, tensions in the couple begin to be felt due to Evelyn's unfulfilled expectations, accused by Cynthia of polishing the boots of another lecturer, which is considered a betrayal. Then, to express her sadness, Cynthia demands that Evelyn bake her own birthday cake, which she eats by placing her feet on Evelyn's face, lying on the floor, who is not enjoying herself. But the two women reconciled, and Evelyn agreed to put less emphasis on her sexual needs. The end of the film, however, shows the couple returning to the same game of household chores.
story_text_b: As Trevor (Jason Connery) drifts through Texas he is still haunted by the evils of the war he recently returned from and a promise he failed to keep. When a stranger offers a ride, Trevor finds himself battling the brutal homegrown evil of the Broderick family at Hoboken Hollow, a remote West Texas ranch that many have visited but few ever leave.

story_text_a: The story revolves around Martin Clément, born Marvin Bijou, who escapes from his hometown and his family. He's going to tell his story through a play that's going to be a big hit. But at what price, I don't know.
story_text_b: I was in Baltimore in 1954. The United States is entering a new era, and the Kurtzman family is about to go through a lot of changes, too. Ben, the youngest son, has always lived in an exclusively Jewish neighborhood. He then falls in love with Sylvia, the only black student in his high school, against the advice of her father, because of Ben's skin color (white). Meanwhile, Ben's older brother, Van, is fascinated by the beautiful and aristocratic Dubbie. As for the father, he's trying to save his little music hall.

story_text_a: Gwen married, against her father Sam Burnett's wishes, the Torito Indian and lives with his tribe. After being kidnapped by a hostile Indian tribe, she escapes and is taken to safety by Cowboy Johnny. Johnny's looking for Gwen's father, to whom he intends to turn her over. In the meantime, however, her husband, Torito, took her home. Johnny and Burnett try to convince the couple to move to Burnett's ranch; while Torito refuses, Gwen follows her father there. Johnny accompanies her and realizes that Gwen really loves her husband. He returns to Torito and tries to persuade him to follow his wife. Meanwhile, the Indians, led by their hostage, attack Burnett's ranch. All the inhabitants except Gwen are killed in the ultimately futile defense, the latter becomes a victim of another abduction. Johnny and Torito team up, and they can finally free Gwen.
story_text_b:
The content of the novel can be characterized by the phrase Sex, Drugs n Jazz.
The two main characters, Dean Moriarty and the narrator Sal Paradise, embark on various journeys across the United States and Mexico to indulge in the high, the women and the jazz  while listening as hipsters not to mainstream jazz, but to the new, harder bebop.
The two of them step on, jump on freight trains, ride Greyhound buses, truck gears or stolen cars across the North American continent and back, from New York City, via Chicago, Denver, California to New Orleans and finally to Mexico. Of particular interest are the deviations from the norm that become apparent in US society in the late 1940s and early 1950s, the outlook of young outsiders and their observational perspective on the rest of society.
Joyce Johnson, with whom Kerouac had a relationship between 1957 and 1958, recalled the basic scheme of the novel at the time of Mark Twain's novel The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn. Sal can be equated with Twain's character Tom Sawyer, as both live in comfort with their bourgeois aunts. Dean would thus be a counterpart to Huck Finn, especially since both are outlaws who make a great impression on a middle-class boy and with whom they travel. However, the raft was replaced by more modern vehicles.
The novel is strongly autobiographical, and many of the characters can be identified with people in Kerouac's life. Shortly before his death, Kerouac planned a complete edition of his work, on the cover of which he would name the real people who corresponded to his characters. The character Dean Moriarty in On the Road is Neal Cassady, Carlo Marx is Allen Ginsberg, Old Bull Lee is William S. Burroughs, Tom Saybrook is John Clellon Holmes, Elmo Hassel is Herbert Huncke, the narrator Sal Paradise is Kerouac himself. However, this total expenditure was no longer realized during his lifetime. It wasn't until 2007 that the original scroll with the real names was published. A German translation of the original by Ulrich Blumenbach was published in 2010.

story_text_a:
The film depicts a romantic relationship between two people belonging to different communities who more or less directly oppose their relationship.
In Glasgow, Scotland, Casim, a young disc jockey, dreams of starting his own nightclub. Her parents, Pakistani immigrants, are arranging her marriage to a Pakistani cousin who'll be arriving in Scotland in a few weeks.
Casim's encounter with Roisin, his sister Tahara's music teacher at a Catholic high school, disrupted the path his family and the Pakistani community in Glasgow had planned for him. But Roisin, a Catholic, is also judged by her own community...
story_text_b:
The film opens with a call for people to come out and participate in protests demanding the release of Alexei Navalny, the film's narrator and scriptwriter, who was detained after arriving in Russia following treatment and rehabilitation in Germany in connection with his poisoning in 2020. Alexei Navalny then goes on to tell the story of the making of the film, saying that the film is an in-depth look into the psychological portrait of Vladimir Putin.
The film mainly focuses on the building of the Residence at Cape Idokopas, a dacha located near the town of Gelendzhik in Krasnodar Krai, which Navalny calls "the largest private house in Russia", citing documents regarding its construction, some of which are then presented to the audience for viewing. According to The Straits Times, these documents included itemised lists of purchased furniture and samples of the building's floor plans, which were handed over to the Anti-Corruption Foundation by a subcontractor involved with its construction. Allegedly, all vehicles entering the compound are subject to inspections at several checkpoints, and workers are strictly forbidden from carrying mobile phones with a camera. Besides the complex itself, the restricted area also includes an underground ice palace and two helipads, an arboretum and greenhouse measuring 2,500 square metres (27,000 sq ft), a church, an amphitheatre, a teahouse and an 80-metre (260 ft) bridge leading to the compound, which crosses a ravine. Due to its location on a steep bank, a special tunnel was dug to provide access to the nearby beach, which contains a tasting room overlooking the Black Sea. The area of the palace complex is 68 hectares (170 acres), with 7,000 hectares (17,000 acres) of land surrounding the palace being designated as a closed territory under the jurisdiction of the Federal Security Service. According to the film, all fishing activities within a radius of two kilometres from the Residence at Cape Idokopas is banned and the airspace over the palace complex is closed to all aircraft. The film also shows 3D renders of the palace interior and exterior made using the floorplan, leaked photos and after inquiring with the furniture brands. The film goes on to focus on the businesses located within the complex, a luxury winery, vineyards and an oyster farm, showing inconsistencies between their estimated values and reported productions and revenues. It establishes how the (changing) ownerships conceal an interconnected network of managers as well as "donors" that supply money. The network includes former associates (e.g. Vladimir Kolbin, son of a childhood friend of Putin) or relatives of Putin (e.g. Mikhail Shelomov of JSC Accept), but also state-owned companies such as Transneft through shady "leasing" services. Huge sums are funneled into the compound in what Navalny calls the "biggest bribe" and Putin's "slush fund".

story_text_a:
1886: In London's Soho district, Adolf Verloc runs a small, not-so-successful shop selling pornographic products and nipples. He lives with his wife, Winnie, and their mentally handicapped brother, Stevie, in a small apartment behind the store. What his wife doesn't know is that he provides reports on the anarchist circles he's in for good money to an embassy. That's the message he'll be quoted for one day. The new secretary, Vladimir, is asking Verloc for more than just reports. He's asking Verloc to carry out a bombing at the Greenwich Observatory. The public outcry over this attack on science would change the lax attitude of the British police towards the anarchists, who also threaten the security of his country.
Torn from his civilian life by this assignment, Verloc makes his preparations. He sends Stevie, on the grounds that the city is too exciting for his mood, to one of his anarchist friends in the countryside and begins - much to the delight of his wife - to take him on his walks. With the professor, another anarchist, he gets an explosive device. Stevie, who trusts him unconditionally and considers him a "good" person, is supposed to bring him to the observatory, but he stumbles, the bomb explodes and tears him apart.
Chief Inspector Heat, who is in charge of the police investigation, quickly tracks him down through a piece of coat with Verloc's address on it. Verloc is no stranger to Scotland Yard. He'd given the police a tip or two before. But Heat is booed back by his superiors. They want to use the knowledge of the Vladimir-Verloc connection to get Vladimir to pull his agents out of England. Verloc's friends in the anarchist group think he's the victim of the explosion.
Verloc, meanwhile, expects to have to flee abroad after the failed assassination attempt, and withdraws all his money from the bank. Heat's looking for him off the books. Winnie overhears the inspector's conversation with her husband, learns of her brother's death and Verloc's guilt in it. When he tries to play down Stevie's death as an unfortunate accident and accuses her of putting the police on his trail, she strangles him.
Excited, she leaves the apartment after the murder, where she meets Ossipon, another comrade from Verloc's anarchist circle. She asks him for help, which her Ossipon, who is in love with her, agrees to. They plan to flee to the continent, but when he learns of Verloc's money, he takes it, jumps off the oncoming train at the last moment, and abandons them. Later, he learns from the newspaper that a woman, after leaving her wedding ring on board, has jumped from the ship into the English Channel.
Note: The plot summary follows the chronology, the novel is not structured chronologically and an omniscient narrator changes the narrative perspective several times.
story_text_b: In an unspecified future, a young woman, Elizabeth Hansen, wakes up inside a cryogenic capsule identified as Omicron 267, but due to amnesia has no memory of why she is there or who she is. The situation worsens when the oxygen begins to run out, and in order to survive, Elizabeth must dig into her memory while simultaneously searching for a way to escape. The story takes a turn when the woman in the course of dialogues with MILO (Medical Interface Liaison Officer), the artificial intelligence that oversees all operations, realizes what reality is: her identity, in fact, with her surprise and anguish, is that of a clone of the scientist Elizabeth Hansen, who travels on a spaceship with others like her to a distant planet 14 light years from Earth and who has been put into hyper-sleep because the trip lasts 34 years, so as to escape a virus that is ending the life of man on Earth. He discovers that his awakening was due to a processor overheating.

story_text_a: The twins Rachel and Theo have to travel to Auckland to visit relatives after their mother's death. At first, everything seems normal except for a few earthquakes. The next day, the son of the relatives shows the twins the region and the volcanoes. Theo also meets the important Mr. Jones. Meanwhile, Rachel discovers the lake house, which stands overgrown and dilapidated on Lake Pupuke. The men who live there, who call themselves the Wilberforces, behave very strangely towards Rachel. Later it becomes clear that the Wilberforces are the creatures who want to kill the twins. The reasons are still unknown. The next day, Theo and Mr. Jones are having a conversation. Meanwhile, Rachel is nearly strangled by a Wilberforce. It's becoming clear that Mr. Jones is different, too. He's trying to destroy the Wilberforces with twins. Only twins have the gift of destroying the Wilberforces with fire stones. They must both be thrown into the crater of Rangitoto at the same time, says Jones. The twins finally manage to destroy the Wilberforces. Mr. Jones is going to die.
story_text_b: The film follows the adventures of two teenage twins, Theo and Rachel, as they confront the dark forces lurking beneath the volcanoes of Auckland.

story_text_a:
The novel begins in 1857 and sees Rougon in conflict with the emperor forced to resign as premier before he can be dismissed.
This puts the plans and dreams of Rougon's friends in limbo, as they relied on his political influence to obtain various personal favors.
His greatest ally and his greatest opponent, however, is Clorinde Balbi, an Italian woman of dubious origins and devious intentions.
Clorinde, who desires power as much as Rougon but who, being a woman, is forced to act behind the scenes, falls in love with Eugène but Rougon refuses to marry her because he believes that two dominant personalities like theirs would lead to mutual destruction.
Eugène thus encourages her to marry M. Delestang, a very rich man who can however be easily handled, while he will take as a wife a nullity that cannot hinder his ambitions.
Meanwhile, Rougon learns of a plot to assassinate the emperor, but decides not to take part.
Consequently, after Felice Orsini's failed attempt in 1858, Eugène was promoted by the emperor to Minister of the Interior with the power to maintain peace and national security at all costs.
Rougon uses this opportunity to punish his political opponents, anti-imperialists, and reward friends who had remained loyal to him by entrusting them with honors, offices and political commitments.
Due to his influence, Delestang is elected Minister of Agriculture and Trade.
But as Rougon's power expands his friends, despite his attempts to satisfy their personal demands, begin to abandon him because they feel that he hasn't done enough for them and what he has done either hasn't been good enough or has had disastrous consequences so that it hasn't been of help to anyone.
Moreover, they consider him ungrateful given all the work they claim to have done to succeed in reinstating him as Minister.
In the end Rougon is involved in several big scandals based on the favors he has propagated to his group and at the center of all this conflict there is Clorinde. In fact, the woman's power is now greater than that of Rougon and her influence is at a higher level and on an international scale having become the emperor's mistress.
Clorinde, having now the upper hand, is able to punish Rougon for his refusal to marry her.
To quell political and personal opposition, Rougon decides to tender his resignation to the emperor, confident that it will not be accepted.
However, they are accepted and Delestang is elected Minister of the Interior.
The novel ends in 1862 when the Emperor re-admits Rougon to his service as Minister without Portfolio, giving him unprecedented power in the wake of Italian unification.
Ostensibly the task of the office would be to reconfigure the country along more liberal lines, but in reality Rougon has a free hand to crush resistance, reduce opposition and control the press.
story_text_b: Thomas Crown (Pierce Brosnan) is a billionaire adventurous businessman who enjoys challenges, such as crashing an expensive yacht or betting a hundred thousand dollars on a golf stroke simply because he thinks he can emulate the reputed golfer Arnold Palmer. Crown steals a painting (San Giorgio Maggiore during twilight) by Monet valued at $100 million; the artwork's insurers send in investigator Catherine Banning (Rene Russo) to help the police solve the crime. From the beginning, Banning suspected Crown was behind the crime. The elaborate cat-and-mouse game that develops gives Crown exactly what he's been looking for: Banning's love.

story_text_a:
Joe Pendleton, a boxer, crashes his small plane on a pleasure flight. Angel 7013 believes that Joe will not survive the crash, and assumes  to spare him pain  his soul even before the crash. In the afterlife, it turns out Joe's death was a mistake. Without the angel's intervention, he would have survived and had another 50 years to live. The angel's superior, Mr. Jordan, orders Joe to return to his body, but in the meantime, it has been burned in the crematorium by order of Max Corkle, Joe's boxing manager. Now Joe, who does not want to be cheated of his 50 years of life, is to be provided with a new body. Mr. Jordan explains that the body is just a shell, but through his soul, Joe will remain the same as he was. Since Joe wants to continue as a boxer, it should be a physically fit specimen.
After a few unusable specimens, Jordan Joe shows the body of Mr. Bruce Farnsworth, a banker who has just been drowned in his bathtub by his wife, Julia, and his secretary, Tony Abbott. Joe's reluctant to take over the body. However, when he sees the murderous couple's dismissive treatment of the lovely Miss Bette Logan, the daughter of a Farnsworth client wrongfully imprisoned for fraud, he chooses the body. From now on, the audience and Joe himself will continue to see the real Joe, the characters in the film perceive him as Farnsworth.
Pendleton in Farnsworth's body pays off all the investors and manages to get Miss Logan's father out of jail. He tells his manager, Max, that he's really Joe. To prove it, he plays a saxophone in the bad way the real Joe did. Max trains him, and after a while, he can beat the current heavyweight champion, Ralph (K.O.) I want to challenge Murdock. Mr. Jordan warns Joe that there could be a conflict if he, in the guise of Farnsworth, wins the title that Pendleton was supposed to win. Meanwhile, Julia and Secretary Abbott plan another assassination attempt on their donor Farnsworth, though they remain baffled as to how he survived their previous assassination attempt. Joe as Farnsworth gets shot by Abbott. Joe returns to the spirit world and learns from Mr. Jordan that the Farnsworth body has been hidden in a freezer in the basement.
From now on, Julia and Abbott claim Farnsworth went into hiding. Max doesn't believe this and calls the police, but they don't believe his talk about angels and body changes. During an interrogation at the Farnsworth house by Inspector Williams, Joe uses telepathic influence to get Max to turn on the radio. The announcer announces that Murdock collapsed in the world championship match against Lou Gilbert without anyone touching him. Jordan finds out that Murdock was shot by betting fraudsters so that the fight would go to his opponent. Joe takes on the body of Murdock, whom he knows and respects, and in that body wins the fight. Now that Joe has a saxophone as Murdock again, Max knows that Joe is now performing in Murdock's body. Joe tells Max where Farnsworth's body is hidden, prompting the police to find the body in the freezer a short time later. Julia and Abbott will be arrested. Still Murdock, he fires Murdock's corrupt manager and hires Max.
Mr. Jordan explains to Joe that this is his destiny, that he can now live as Murdock. He heals the gunshot wound and makes his memories of his previous life as Joe and his encounters with the angels disappear. Miss Logan appears, sees Murdock, and feels that they've seen each other before. She remembers Joe as Farnsworth telling her shortly before his murder that she should be kind to a boxer she might soon meet who would remind her of him. As the two walk away together, Jordan smiles into himself.
story_text_b:
On May 11, 1941, boxer and amateur pilot Joe Pendleton (Robert Montgomery), affectionately known as "the Flying Pug", flies his small aircraft to his next fight in New York, but suffers a serious accident when a control wire breaks. His soul is "rescued" by 7013 (Edward Everett Horton), an unofficial angel who surmised that Joe could not have survived. Joe's representative, Max "Pop" Corkle (James Gleason), cremated his body. In a place beyond life, the records show that his death was a mistake; he is supposed to live another 50 years. The superior angel, Mr. Jordan (Claude Rains), confirms this situation, but since there is no longer a body, Joe will have to take a recently dead corpse. Mr. Jordan explains that a body is just something that wears out, like a coat; but on the inside, Joe would still be the same. Joe insists that he be someone in good physical shape, because he wants to continue his boxing career.
After Joe discards several "candidates", Mr. Jordan takes him to see the body of a dishonest, big-time investor and wealthy banker named Bruce Farnsworth, who has just been drugged and drowned in a bathtub by his wife Julia (Rita Johnson) and his secretary, Tony Abbott (John Emery). Joe is reluctant to take a life so different from his own, but when he sees the pair of killers mockingly reprimanding Miss Logan (Evelyn Keyes), the daughter of a financier to whom he has been selling worthless Farnsworth Bank bonds, he changes his mind and agrees to take Farnsworth's body.
Since he's Farnsworth, Joe reimburses all the investors, including Miss Logan's father. He sends for Corkle and convinces him that he is Joe (by playing his saxophone as badly as he did before). With Farnsworth's money to pave the way, Corkle trains him and arranges a final fight with the reigning heavyweight champion, but Mr. Jordan returns to warn Joe that, although he's destined to be the champion, it can't happen that way. Joe only has enough time to tell Miss Logan, with whom he has fallen in love, that if a stranger (especially if he is a boxer) approaches him, give him a chance. Then his secretary shoots him. The body is hidden and Joe returns to a spiritual existence.
Accompanied by Mr. Jordan, Joe finds that his substitute in the fight for the championship is a clean and honest boxer named Murdoch, whom Joe knows and respects. Discovering that he forgot his lucky saxophone, Joe runs back to the Farnsworth mansion to find that everyone believes Farnsworth has "disappeared". Corkle hires a private investigator to find him. Corkle explains about Joe, Mr. Jordan and the body-shifter, but naturally the police detective (Donald MacBride) thinks he's nuts. Joe mentally directs eccentric Corkle to turn on the radio broadcasting the fight and hears that Murdoch has fallen untouched. Mr. Jordan reveals that the boxer has been shot by the punters because he refused to lose the fight. Joe takes Murdoch's body and wins the title. Back at the mansion, Corkle hears a radio announcer mention a saxophone left in the ring and realizes that Joe has taken over Murdoch's body.
Corkle runs to the dressing rooms. There, Joe passes him a lot of information from Mr. Jordan about Farnsworth's body being in a refrigerator in the mansion's basement. Corkle tells the detective, who quickly arrests Miss Farnsworth and the secretary. Like Murdoch, Joe fires his former dishonest representative and hires Corkle. Mr. Jordan reveals to Joe that this is his destiny; that he can be Murdoch and live his life.
Healing the gunshot wound and at the same time removing Joe's memory of his past life, Mr. Jordan waits nearby until Miss Logan arrives. She wants to see Corkle, but finds Murdoch instead. The couple feels like they've met before. The two of them leave together, as Mr. Jordan smiles and says, "See you later, champ".

story_text_a:
The film takes place shortly after the landing of Allied troops in Sicily on July 10, 1943. When a small village hears the news, they are at first shocked. The fascists have left the village and there is still no sign of the Allies, resulting in a time of power vacuum, a chance for a utopia. The villagers make plans for a life without army and war, in freedom and peace.
The main character is the intellectual Giuseppe, who has just graduated and, despite his young age, is already considered a leader by part of the village community. The small village community is very diverse, divided into homeowners and farmers, communists and Catholics, the Mafia and people who mourn Mussolini  and each group has its own ideas and notions that are presented to Giuseppe. But Giuseppe really wants to enjoy his life and love after graduation. The seductive Anne and the passionate Pina have done it to him, but who conquers his heart?
story_text_b: The film, inspired by the youthful experience of the director's father, tells the short but intense period between the fall of the fascist regime and the arrival of the Americans in a country of Sicily. The film aims to be halfway between the historical novel and a more personal and intimate tale, inspired by the tales of Zagarrio's father and a veiled metaphor for the conflict in the Middle East

story_text_a:
It is set in an anonymous, desolate, isolated small town in Hungary during Communist times.
The film starts with János Valuska, a young newspaper-delivery man, conducting a performance with drunken bar patrons about the total eclipse of the sun, which disturbs, then silences the animals. It finishes with the grand return of the warm sunlight.
János is devoted to his uncle György Eszter, a composer and musicologist, who is like a father to him. György records his observations about the imperfection and compromise of the musical scale, as defined by Andreas Werckmeister. György proposes changes to the natural scale to make its harmonies more natural.
János goes to the post office to pick up his newspapers for delivery. The workers are unsettled by the ominous signs of the circus' arrival and are disturbed by the cloud that settles over each town it visits.
A “circus” built around a huge stuffed smelly whale and its star performer, "The Prince", who is never seen, come to town in the silence and darkness of night. János sees them arrive and philosophizes about God and the whale.
