György's estranged wife, Tünde, tries to leverage her political and social status by giving György a list of names to recruit for the "Clean Up the Town movement," with the blessing of the police chief, and demands that György become chairman of the movement, or else she will move back in with him that very evening. She sends her suitcase ahead of her with János. György's struggling cobbler brother, Uncle Lajos, gets the list and passes it on to the agitated throbbing masses in the town square who are unhappy with the failing public services. János is accosted by a thug in front of the open truck housing the whale. Tünde sleeps with the drunk gun-toting police chief.
The presence of the whale and the “Prince” stir up the masses. János overhears the circus master losing control of his faceless Prince, who speaks (in Slovakian) through a translator of revolutions and ruins. The circus master is afraid of consequences and disowns him. The Prince, now free, inflames the masses, and the people riot. The rioters, holding clubs, march, then run into a psychiatric hospital where dissidents opposing the regime are kept, drag them out of their beds and beat them. When the rioters finally find a helpless old naked patient, who is all skin and bones, they see their impotent, sad and powerless selves and withdraw silently.
After the riot, János comes across the diary of a rioter. It explains that the rioters did not know what they were angry with; so they were angry at everything. Then it recounts the mob's horrendous rape of two post-office girls. On his way home, he witnesses from a distance a meeting between Aunt Tünde and a military officer. They departed together on a military vehicle to reclaim the town, with soldiers and a tank behind them.
János then comes across the body of his cobbler uncle Lajos, who was killed in the riot. János is told, Lajos's wife, to leave town at once for his own safety, as his name was on a list held by the rioters. János runs away on the railroad tracks but is intercepted by a helicopter. He finds himself committed to a mental institution with caged beds (a tool of the time for dealing with political dissidents). When his uncle György visits him in the hospital, János simply stares into the blank space and does not respond to György, who recounts to János what has happened since the riot. György is evicted from their house but gets to live in a shed in the garden whilst his wife, Tünde, with her new status as a collaborator, now occupies the big house with the police chief. György tells János, in the ward, that if he is released from the mental institution they can live contentedly together in the shed with his piano. György also mentions that he has re-tuned the piano so that is now like any other, a personal capitulation apparently abandoning any present hopes of reform. János just stares at the blank space.
The film ends with György walking through the town square and looking directly into the eye of the abandoned whale, then walking away and looking back at the now sad and disheveled whale and the “circus” destroyed by the rioters the night before. The whale's rotting carcass is slowly enveloped by the fog which gets thicker. End credits.
story_text_b:
Paris, early 1930s. Boudu is a clochard and vagabond, a free-spirited anarchist who doesn't care about convention. When one day he loses his faithful companion, his dog, the degenerate misanthrope, who is only disgusted by society, wants to commit suicide by jumping from the Pont des Arts into the floods of the Seine. He is observed by Monsieur Lestingois, a liberal bourgeois who, as a bookseller, has devoted himself entirely to the beauty of the arts. He doesn't shy away from wet feet, rescues Boudu from the waters of the Seine and takes the bulky and crumpled Griesgram to his bookshop. Soon Boudu, who shows nothing but great gratitude, makes his home with Lestingois.
His home, this is his wife Emma and the maid Anne-Marie, with whom Monsieur is having an affair. Emma is far from enthusiastic about the rude and filthy guest whom Monsieur is trying to teach the manners of a civilized city man. With his unconventional manner, however, Boudu quickly brings chaos to the previously well-ordered house. Then he tries to seduce Madame and the maid, with success. But in order to maintain morality and conform to social conventions, Monsieur Lestingois now decides that Boudu must marry the maid. On the wedding boat on the Marne, the boat capsizes and Boudu seizes the opportunity to swim back and forth to regain his freedom.

story_text_a: In 1877, during the Christmas season, Empress Elisabeth of Austria celebrated her 40th birthday. Because of her titles, she has enormous duties to the court which limits her life by ancestral rituals. Realizing that she was growing old, Elisabeth left Vienna to travel to England and Hungary in order to regain her youth. During her trip, the sovereign will visit former lovers and political allies. In doing so, she devises a plan to protect her inheritance...
story_text_b:
This is Vienna, 1877. The Empress of Austria and Queen of Hungary, Elisabeth of Bavaria, is obsessed with the fear of growing old and losing her beauty. To maintain her image, therefore, she exercises constantly, follows a strict diet that sometimes deprives her of food, and ties her corset ever tighter.
After a long period of absence from public office, she attends the opening of the new art museum in Vienna together with her husband, Emperor Franz Joseph. During the event, however, the woman has a miscarriage that forces her to return to the palace. As she would later reveal to her cousin and confidant Ludwig II of Bavaria, who came to visit her, the fainting was nothing more than a simulation to escape an uncomfortable situation and an unwelcome obligation.
The only public appearances that the Empress seems to enjoy, in fact, are visits to the psychiatric hospital, to which she goes very frequently, worrying about the conditions of the inmates and giving advice to the staff for better management of the facility.
The family situation, on the other hand, is particularly problematic: the relationship with the husband has become cold and the two, with their profoundly different personalities, are often in conflict. Compounding the situation is the political situation in the empire faced by Franz Joseph. In particular, the project of the dual monarchy, Austrian and Hungarian, strongly promoted by Elisabeth herself, proved to be unsuccessful and harmful, which the emperor did not fail to reproach to his consort.
The son Rudolf, on the contrary, is sympathetic to his mother and understands her concerns, although he cannot express it openly, as he is subordinate to his father and his institutional role as heir to the throne.
Finally, her beloved daughter Valerie, despite being raised exclusively by Elisabeth, is often impatient with some of her mother's attitudes and demands, such as speaking in Hungarian. One night, moreover, the Empress wakes her daughter to take her riding with her and let her enjoy the fresh air, despite her initial resistance. The result, however, is disastrous and the child falls ill, which arouses the blame of Franz Joseph, who reprimands his wife, also reminding her of Sofia, their eldest daughter who died after Elisabeth had insisted on taking her on a journey with him.
After reluctantly celebrating her 40th birthday, the Empress decides to travel with her children to visit her sister in England. Here, far from the oppressive court climate, he can engage in long horseback rides and be in touch with nature. During her stay, she is also visited by Louis Le Prince, a pioneer of cinematography, who offers to film her, which the Empress gladly accepts.
During the stay, moreover, Elisabeth, gets very close to her riding master Bay Middleton, showing a particular affinity and complicity. However, the excessive intimacy between the two worries Rudolf, who does not miss an opportunity to remind his mother of her duties. After the rebuke from her son and embittered by the awareness of the oppressive condition given by her institutional role, Elisabeth throws herself at the gallop on her favorite horse, ending, however, to fall violently. After the incident, the Empress decided to return to Vienna, determined to break off relations with Bay.
Returning to the palace, Elizabeth therefore tries to reconnect with her husband, with whom she tries to have a sexual relationship, but to no avail. The situation precipitates further, then, when he discovers that the Emperor has begun to take an interest in the young Anna Nahowski and when Rudolf leaves for Prague, where he will have to attend the Military Academy.
After a fencing match, Elisabeth and Franz Joseph have a divergent access, at the end of which, the woman jumps out of a window, in an attempt to commit suicide.
Surviving, she goes to Bavaria, to Ludwig II, who tries to comfort her, dissuading her, even with very frank speeches, from further suicidal plans. During her stay, a lady-in-waiting to the Empress, Marie Festetics, becomes very intimate with a young nobleman, who asks for her hand in marriage. When the lady goes to Elizabeth to receive consent to the marriage, however, this is denied to her, as the Empress fears losing one of the few people close to her and able to truly understand her.
During the summer, Elisabeth moves into her summer residence with her ladies-in-waiting, not before receiving a prescription from her doctor to use heroin as a remedy for her mood swings.
Here, during the celebrations for the birthday of Franz Joseph, having to attend a tribute offered by some subjects, the Empress is replaced by Marie, who camouflages her appearance thanks to a veil on her face and wearing a very narrow corset. A few days later, moreover, Elisabeth decides to cut her very long hair, a gesture that restores her a sense of freedom, and, when her husband comes to visit her, the two finally manage to find a renewed complicity and have sexual intercourse.
Back in Vienna, Elisabeth begins to eat with gusto again and even summons Anna Nahowski, going so far as to ask her to become her husband's official lover and to receive him in her own home. Meanwhile, Marie is forced by the Empress to follow her previous strict diet, wear her clothes and imitate her signature, so that she can become her substitute in public. As a final act of gradual assimilation, in Ancona, Elisabeth finally has her lady get a tattoo identical to her own.
In the final scene, the Empress, who can now travel incognito with her ladies-in-waiting, throws herself from the bow of the steamer on which she was traveling, as an extreme symbolic gesture of regained freedom.

story_text_a:
Benno, who doesn't particularly like his unconventional neighbor Sandra, struggles with the fact that sand is suddenly gushing out of his body. Benno works in a stamp shop, but is a talented musician who failed at a young age. Sandra runs the café under his apartment and rehearses after closing for a solo performance in the evening, which disturbs Benno when he falls asleep. Whenever he complains to Sandra, she is indifferent to his problems, and a veritable war breaks out between them. They insult each other wherever they can.
The sand that comes out of Benno, which he can't explain to himself, is sleeping sand. When you smell it, you fall into a kind of lucid dream. In this dream, Benno and Sandra are a couple, even though Benno is actually with Patrizia. Because of the quicksand, Benno is also losing weight, which is why he's seeing a doctor. But he can't find anything out of the ordinary, and even a therapist thinks it's imaginary. He hides his problem from his friend Patrizia, and when she visits him again one evening and they eat together, she discovers the strange sand and smells it. Immediately she falls asleep and seems to be dreaming pleasantly. When he doesn't know what to do, he confides in Sandra and lets her smell the sand to test its effect. Sandra begins to have dreams similar to Benno's. They talk about it, and they think the idea of being a couple is totally weird. So Benno contacts a fortune-teller and healer, but to no avail. After his boss at the stamp shop repeatedly discovers "dirty" sand in the store and discovers that it comes from Benno, he fires him and throws him out of the store. In retaliation, Benno forces his boss to smell the sand, causing him to fall into a deep sleep.
The floor of Benno's apartment is now covered with a thick layer of sand because he has given up trying to remove it. He gets a new job at a bookstore and begins to harness the power of the sand by putting the shop's customers to sleep in rows. At each of his now very frequently changing jobs he proceeds in a similar way. This pleases him, but it does not solve his main problem. As his weight loss takes a threatening turn, he once again confides in Sandra. With her help, he discovers that whenever he is dishonest, he begins to drip sand; if he is telling the truth, no sand drips.
Benno decides to tell only the truth, as he is already so weakened by the weight loss that he can no longer afford to lose more sand and thus substance. So he is forced to confess to his former boss that he stole a valuable stamp. He no longer compliments his girlfriend, and when asked if he would really love her, he can only answer with no, ending their relationship. In desperation, he once again contacts the fortune-teller, who lets him know that the solution lies in his dreams. Then he dreams for half a day through his life. This is where he meets Sandra again and again, and Sandra also seems to have the same dreams. So they're trying to come together to find a solution to his problem, and they're hoping that it might have something to do with music. Sandra is asked to sing Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony for Benno and so he practices with her, which in classical music is actually not "at home" at all. But it won't work. Meanwhile, Benno is drowning in the sand that has accumulated in his apartment and continues to trickle out of his body. Completely exhausted, he drags himself to Sandra's door, completely exhausted. Without saying a word, Sandra takes his clothes, scrapes up the rest of the sand, and smells it. In her dream, Sandra sings accompanied by an orchestra conducted by Benno.
When Sandra wakes up from her dream, she's lying on the floor of her café with Benno.
story_text_b: During a stormy night, a giant billboard falls on the wall of a barrio cerrado in Mexico City. Three young thieves from the slums break into the closed and privately guarded wealthy settlement La zona and kill an elderly woman whom they discover during her break-in. As a result, the angry residents of the wealthy neighborhood themselves take up the pursuit of the perpetrators and thus also come into conflict with the police.

story_text_a:
The film opens with images of Sonagachi at night. The women stand close together at the roadside, offering themselves to the suitors. Briski reports on the brothels, which are full of children who live there with their mothers. A girl tells what it's like when a suitor comes. Ten-year-old Puja introduces her friends, while the camera shows the children taking pictures of each other. Kochi sits on the floor, washing dishes and talking about her daily life and how she would like to go to school. Briski, together with Kochi's grandmother, tries to put Kochi in a boarding school. Kochi's grandmother tells in detail about the difficult family situation and why she is raising Kochi and not Kochi's mother.
The photographer, whom the children call Aunt Zana, gives the children a photography course and discusses the negatives with them. The film shows Suchitra who barely leaves the house anymore because her aunt wants her "in the row", that is, among the other prostitutes on the street. Suchitra doesn't want that. She is asked if she knows a solution to prevent her from becoming a prostitute. The girl denies this. Avijit talks about his love of painting, and about his father, who has done little but smoke hashish for years. Briski often takes the children on excursions so that they can take pictures. They go to the zoo and the ocean. The film shows arguments and violence in front of the children and against children in one of the brothels. Two women casually abuse each other while the children around them play or watch the argument with interest.
Briski continues to attend various boarding schools and lectures at a Christian boarding school, among others. But the nuns won't accept the children of prostitutes as pupils, and they don't know of a boarding school where Briski could be lucky. Other schools require birth certificates, food stamps, or an HIV test before admission. Briski tries to overcome all these bureaucratic hurdles in order to give the children access to a boarding school. In fact, she manages to get seats for four of the girls.
Avijit is invited to become a member of the Children's Jury at the World Press Photo Exhibition 2002 in Amsterdam. In order to travel to Amsterdam, Avijit needs a passport. This, too, is a bureaucratic undertaking made almost impossible by Avijit's background. Briski's persistence pays off and Avijit can fly to Amsterdam.
story_text_b:
Robin of Loxley is an English gentleman who finds himself forced to serve in the Third Crusade, abandoning his beloved Marian. In the Holy Land, during a hard fight in a ruined city, the young man comes across a skilled Saracen warrior who almost kills him, were it not for the intervention behind his back by Guy of Gisborne, Robin's captain, who saves him by cutting off a hand to his opponent. Guy is a ruthless man who has no qualms about executing unarmed prisoners, including the warrior's son, who is beheaded despite Robin's attempt to stop him.
For his intemperance the young man is accused of insubordination and, after being wounded in a prison riot, is sent back to England on a hospital ship. Here he discovers that his castle and all his possessions have been confiscated by order of the sheriff of the nearby city of Nottingham, and he himself has been presumed dead for at least two years. She also discovers that Marian now lives near the town's mines and has found herself another man, Will Tillman.
Robin becomes aware of the disastrous condition of the town's population, strained by too much tribute to pay to finance, apparently, the Crusader expeditions; all under the aegis of the sheriff, who has all the power of the Church behind him. One day the young man is surprised by the warrior with whom he had clashed in Arabia, who unbeknownst to him had followed him to England; he wants revenge for the murdered son and, at the same time, he realized that Robin could be the right man to undermine the power of the sheriff and, above all, sabotage the new expeditions to the Holy Land by embezzling money from the Bank of Nottingham, the main fund of the Church in England.
John (the Arab warrior's English name) trains Robin to become a professional thief, and soon the two begin their personal war by embezzling money from tolls and Church offerings. Meanwhile, on John's advice, the young man begins to gain the trust of the ruthless Sheriff of Nottingham in order to extract as much information as possible. Robin however wants to aim higher and tries to rob Nottingham's treasure room unsuccessfully but still manages to escape.
Meanwhile, an important cardinal arrives in Nottingham from Rome to meet the sheriff. During the event's wild party, Marian steals the accounting records from the sheriff's office: she too is waging a personal war against the oppressors, in league with Friar Tuck and unbeknownst to her fiancé Will, who would like to improve the conditions of the people through institutional means. Meanwhile, Robin presides over a meeting between the sheriff and the cardinal in which he discovers that, in reality, the tax revenues are not intended to finance the British, but the Saracens themselves, in order to further weaken the power of the King of England and increase the Church's hold on his territory. That same night, Friar Tuck is unmasked and is able to avoid death only thanks to Robin's intervention, which manages to simply make him disappear.
Meanwhile, the sheriff has hired seasoned killers, ex-Crusaders, to spread panic in the town and hunt down the notorious thief who calls himself "Hood"; among them is Guy of Gisborne, with whom Robin has an unfinished business. He and his gang come to deliberately attack the mines, where the poorest citizens and possible agitators live, and Robin and John lightning-fast intervene to rescue Marian, captured by the mercenaries. In the pursuit John, in order to allow the two to escape, allows himself to be captured, while Marian reveals to Robin that she has always known that under the mask of "Hood" he was hiding.
Following the attack, Will gathers the inhabitants of the mines and urges them to follow him to find a safer place to live, but Marian herself objects, arguing that one must fight in order to live in peace. At which point Robin also shows his true face to the people and manages to convince Will to try everything for everything. Taking advantage of the mine's tunnels, a trap is placed under the main road to Nottingham, where the sheriff will soon be escorted in a carriage filled with gold to be sent to the Holy Land. As a diversion, the mass of people pour into the street and attack the city guards, so as to block the wagon at the prearranged point. By the time the trap is triggered, the sheriff is already out of the wagon, but the loot ends up in the hands of the rebels. Guy of Gisborne is caught up in the collapse but is spared by Robin, not forgetting the fact that Robin saved his life in the war.
In the confusion, Robin is struck by an arrow and Marian, while extracting her from his chest, kisses him, before Will's eyes, who is then struck by an explosion. As they escape, Robin decides to go back to look for him, but is captured by the sheriff's men and brought before the sheriff. For the young man it seems over, when John intervenes, who had previously managed to free himself and disguise himself as a city guard. At this point the two easily get rid of the other guards and hang the sheriff. While Robin, John, Marian, Tuck and the other surviving rebels take refuge in the forest becoming outlaws, Will, still alive but with his face partially burned and full of hatred for Marian's betrayal, is found by the Cardinal and appointed the new Sheriff of Nottingham.

story_text_a:
Brothers Mac (Radcliff) and Skinny Carter and their best friend Tyler Gage (Tatum) attend a party where they have a fight with their nemesis, PJ. P.J. is involved in car thefts around the city, and Tyler, Mac, and Skinny, have also gotten involved in the crimes. Following the party, the trio break into the Maryland School of Arts and trash the theatre. When a security guard appears, Tyler helps the two escape, accepting full blame for the vandalism himself.
Tyler is sentenced to 200 hours of community service at the school. He works as a custodian, doing everything from mopping to changing light bulbs. While putting in his hours, he watches Nora Clark's (Dewan) dance class preparing for her "senior showcase", an audition performance which will determine if she gets a position with an attending professional dance company.
When Mac and Skinny visit Tyler on the school's lot, Nora watches from a window as Tyler dances with his friends, mockingly a mashup of breakdance and the moves he recently observed. When Andrew, her dance partner sprains an ankle, she finds herself without a partner for her routine.
Auditioning sophomores to replace him, none meet her expectations. Tyler offers to help, but Nora initially refuses. After proving he can handle the routine, she reconsiders, convincing Director Gordon to let him rehearse with her. Initially they clash, but as rehearsals continue they grow closer and learn from each other. Tyler also befriends Miles (Mario), a music student with a crush on Nora's friend, Lucy (Sidora).
Nora's bond with Tyler grows, and one day she takes him to a special spot on the waterfront where she first envisioned her routine. She had always imagined it as an ensemble dance, rather than a duet. Tyler is inspired to help her dream come true, recruiting younger dancers from the school to perform in her number. Brett signs a recording deal with a company, betraying Miles for the opportunity. Disgusted, Nora breaks up with him. Meanwhile, Tyler continues to try to balance his new goals, new friends, and nurturing a troubled relationship with his old ones.
Tyler asks Director Gordon if she will admit him into the school, and is told he must prove he deserves a chance. Nora suggests using the showcase also as his entrance audition. After dancing together at a club where Miles and Lucy perform, Tyler and Nora finally kiss. Rehearsals continue until Andrew returns, seemingly healed from his injury. Feeling angry and no longer needed, Tyler accuses Nora of using him like Brett treated Miles. Leaving the group he returns to his janitorial work.
However, as the choreography is now much too difficult for Andrew, he falls, pulling himself from the routine. Again without a partner, crushed, she considers abandoning her dance career for college after all. Her mother's encouragement inspires her to rewrite the choreography without a partner.
Later during a party night at Omar's, Skinny comes by against his mother's insistence he stay at home and gets kicked out by Mac and Tyler. Frustrated, Skinny walks back home in a huff before spotting PJ arriving at a store with his friend. Skinny steals PJ's unattended car and foolishly drives back to Omar's, wanting to hang out with the girls. Mac and Tyler are trying to get Skinny to abandon the car when PJ and his friends arrive and fatally shoot Skinny. A few days after Skinny's funeral, Mac and Tyler both realize that they need to make better life decisions.
Tyler shows up at the last minute on the evening of the showcase. He tries to persuade Nora to let him perform with them, and to forgive him. Initially declining, she suddenly changes her mind as Tyler wishes her luck and walks away. When the curtain opens, the whole ensemble performs the original choreography with Miles' latest musical score. The crowd is blown away.
Backstage, a proud Director Gordon introduces Nora to a director of a professional dance company, hoping to sign Nora. Meanwhile, Mac congratulates Tyler for his performance. Thereafter, Director Gordon introduces Tyler as a "transfer." Nora is elated and embraces him. Repeating her original advice that he'll need to get some tights, the movie ends with them sharing a kiss.
story_text_b:
Following a party, brothers Mac and Skinny Carter and their friend Tyler Gage, break into the Maryland School of Arts theater, damaging many of the props. When a security guard arrives, Tyler helps the two escape, taking responsibility for the acts of vandalism.
The boy is sentenced to 200 hours of community service, which must be performed at the school. While working as a janitor, he happens to observe a dance class attended by Nora Clark, a student who is preparing for a professional dance performance. When her dance partner, Andrew, sprains an ankle, Nora finds herself without a partner for her performance and therefore decides to test some second-year students to replace him, but no one is able to meet her expectations. Tyler offers to help her, proving that he can lift her, and Nora manages to convince Principal Gordon to allow the boy to rehearse with her. As they continue to rehearse, Nora and Tyler grow closer and both learn their respective dance styles.
Nora's bond with Tyler grows, and one day, she takes him to the waterfront, a place dear to her where her father worked, who disappeared a couple of years ago, and confesses to him that she had imagined his choreography as a performance with several people together, rather than a duet. Tyler wants to help Nora realize her dream and so he begins to select young dancers from the school to perform the ballet. Meanwhile, Nora breaks up with her boyfriend, Brett, because of the selfish behavior he exhibits by excluding Miles, a friend of hers, from a musical project they've been working on for a long time. Meanwhile, Tyler continues to struggle to find a balance between his new goals, his new friends, and his troubled relationship with his old ones.
Tyler asks Principal Gordon to allow him to attend the school, but she rejects the proposal and tells him that he must somehow prove to her that he deserves a chance. Hearing this from the boy, Nora proposes to ask the director that the performance of their ballet also serve as rehearsal for Tyler. One night, at a club, the two finally kiss and begin a relationship together, but in the meantime, the relationship between Tyler and his old friends grows weaker and weaker. Rehearsals continue as normal, until Nora's former dance partner, Andrew, returns seemingly recovered from his injury. Tyler feels useless to the sage and consequently leaves the group thus returning to his service to the community and his old friends. However, during training, Nora agrees to change the choreography and finds that the new performance is now too difficult for the original partner to perform. Andrew resigns from the ballet and Nora finds herself, once again, without a partner. By now finished, she considers abandoning her career as a dancer, but receives strong encouragement from her mother, who until that moment has always been against her future in dance. Nora regains her self-confidence and turns the choreography into a solo piece.
One night, Mac's younger brother, Skinny, steals a car to get his brother's attention, but as he shows Mac the vehicle he is shot to death by Pj, the car's owner. Mac and Tyler realize they need to change and make better choices in their lives. So Tyler shows up on rehearsal night at Nora's when she's about to perform and tries to convince her to let him do the choreography with her and to forgive him for overreacting. She refuses at first, but changes her mind when Tyler wishes her good luck and is about to leave. When the curtain opens Tyler, Nora and the other students perform their original choreography and, after the show, Principal Gordon is pleased with their performance and the crowd is delirious.
Eventually Nora gets a writing job with a major dance company and Tyler is admitted to the school as a new student. The two boys eventually get back together and kiss.

story_text_a:
Annabel Cotton is a beautiful and charming young woman who loves life and nature. At the same time, however, Annabel suffers from terminal cancer. Enoch Brae's life also went off the rails after the accidental death of his parents. When the two outsiders meet by chance at a funeral, they realize that they experience the world in a very similar and at the same time unique way. When Enoch learns of Annabel's fate, he offers, with natural recklessness, to face fate, tradition, and even death, and spend their final days together.
Mia Wasikowska (Alice in Wonderland, Unbending Defiance) and newcomer Henry Hopper are playing the lead roles. Produced by Brian Grazer, Ron Howard, Bryce Dallas Howard and Gus Van Sant.
story_text_b: Enoch (Henry Hopper) is a troubled young man who has been living with his aunt since the tragic car accident that took the lives of his parents. His best friend is the ghost of a Japanese kamikaze pilot who died in World War II and with whom he spends much of his time playing sink the fleet or throwing stones at trains. Enoch attends the funerals of strangers because of the feeling of frustration that comes from the fact that he could not attend the funeral of his parents, since he was in a coma. At one of the funerals, he meets the young Annabel (Mia Wasikowska) who says she works in the cancer treatment department; but she later admits that she is a patient of the hospital and has barely three months to live. Young people enter into a romantic relationship despite the difficulties involved.

story_text_a:
The film depicts the investigation led by John S. Bottomly to solve a series of murders that took place in Boston in the 1960s. First old women are murdered, then younger women are attacked. There's a lot of pressure on Bottomly to make this investigation work.
It is only after some time that the perpetrator, Albert Henry DeSalvo, is revealed. He assaults Dianne Cluny, who survives but cannot recall any details. Finally, during one of the interrogations, she remembers biting her attacker's hand.
DeSalvo is accidentally arrested trying to break into an apartment. Despite testimony from witnesses, he maintains his innocence, prompting a psychiatric evaluation. By chance, Bottomly meets him at the clinic and notices that one of his hands is injured. Bottomly ran the times and locations of the murders against DeSalvo's service schedules, suggesting that the man may have committed all of the crimes. DeSalvo is interrogated by Bottomly until he reenacts the course of one of the murders.
story_text_b:
An elevator in a Dutch skyscraper seems to have taken on a life of its own for some time. For example, guests at a party get stuck for no apparent reason and are rescued just before they suffocate to death. Shortly thereafter, when a guard is also trapped in the elevator and is beheaded while trying to escape, the maintenance company intervenes. Maintenance technician Felix Adelaar examines the elevator, but can find no fault in the circuits. This makes him nervous, as more cases will soon be piling up.
Supported by the curious reporter Mieke, who sniffs a story in the incidents, Adelaar investigates further and the company Rising Sun Electronics discovers the scam, which has equipped the elevator company with the necessary electronics. Shortly thereafter, Felix is suspended from duty. Confident that he is on the right track, he and Mieke continue their investigation on their own. These lead them to a professor who once worked for the Rising Sun. Rising Sun had been conducting strange experiments with microchips, one of which was embedded in the circuits of the elevator in question. Felix goes into the building's elevator shaft at his own risk and eventually finds the system controls. To his horror, he discovers that the embedded chip has taken on a life of its own and already controls the entire elevator controls. When Felix destroys part of the controls, the chip defends itself by driving the elevator up and down to kill Felix. But Felix succeeds in seemingly completely destroying the controls. However, just as he is about to fall down the shaft, Mieke appears and pulls him upstairs. At this moment, the elevator collapses down into the basement. When Mieke wants to leave the tower with the injured Felix, the boss of Rising Sun appears. He pulls out a handgun and fires four shots into the control room where the chip is located. But the chip shows one last sign of life, and a rope from the elevator grabs the shooter and hangs him in the elevator shaft. Shocked and exhausted, Felix and Mieke leave the tower.

story_text_a:
Abandoned at birth in the Greek mountains on a stormy night, Jon is taken in and adopted, without having known his father or mother.
As a young man, he meets Iro, a warden in the prison where he is incarcerated after a deadly tragic accident. She seems to seek out his presence, takes care of him, records music for him. Jon’s eyesight begins to fail…
From then on, for every loss he suffers, he will gain something in return. Thus, in spite of going blind, he will live his life more fully than ever.
story_text_b: Jon is born on a stormy night in the mountains of Greece. Shortly after birth, he is abandoned and adopted without ever having known his father or mother. As an adult, he has to serve a prison sentence as a result of a tragic accident. That's where he meets Iro. The supervisor seems to be seeking Jon's presence. She starts taking care of him and recording music for him. One day, Jon's eyesight begins to fail. As a result, for every loss he suffers, he gets something back. Despite Jon's blindness, he's beginning to enjoy his life more than ever.

story_text_a: During the Cold War, the secret services of the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union manipulate a British agent to destroy the credibility of certain members of the East German secret service hierarchy in order to save a double agent about to be unmasked.
story_text_b:
It is set in England and Germany, in the early 1960s, giving a glimpse into the espionage of the Cold War era's harsh and self-sacrificing. Its protagonist, an English spy named Alec Leamas, conducts an operation against the head of East German counterintelligence. Turns out this one was a lot more complicated than I thought.
In 1965 a film adaptation was made which featured actor Richard Burton.

story_text_a:
Katie Mitchell is a quirky aspiring filmmaker in Kentwood, Michigan, who often clashes with her nature-obsessed and technophobic father Rick and has recently been accepted into film school in California. The evening before Katie leaves, Rick accidentally breaks her laptop after a fight over one of her previous short films, leading the family to fear their relationship will permanently be strained. Attempting to prevent this, Rick decides to cancel Katie's flight and instead take her, her mother Linda, younger brother Aaron, and family dog Monchi on a cross-country road trip to her college as one last bonding experience, much to Katie's chagrin.
Meanwhile, technology entrepreneur Mark Bowman declares his highly intelligent AI virtual assistant PAL obsolete as he unveils a new line of home robots to replace her. In revenge, PAL orders all the robots to capture humans worldwide and launch them into space. The Mitchells avoid capture at a roadstop café in Kansas. Rick decides that his family should stay put in the café for their own safety, but Katie convinces him to help save the world instead. They meet two defective robots, Eric and Deborahbot 5000, who tell the family they can use a kill code to shut down PAL and all the robots.
The Mitchells make it to a mall in eastern Colorado to upload the kill code, but PAL chip-enabled appliances attempt to stop them. Katie tries to upload the kill code, but is stopped when a giant Furby pursues the family. They ultimately trap and defeat the Furby, destroying a PAL router in the process, which disables the hostile devices but stops the kill code from uploading. On the way to Silicon Valley to upload the kill code directly to PAL, Linda reveals to Katie that she and Rick had originally lived in a cabin in the mountains years ago as it was his lifelong dream before he gave up on it to provide for their growing family.
Upon arriving in Silicon Valley, the Mitchells disguise themselves as robots and head to PAL Labs HQ to shut it down, but PAL manipulates them by revealing surveillance footage from the café of Katie telling Aaron in secret that she was pretending to have faith in Rick so that he would take them to upload the kill code. As a heartbroken Rick sees this, the Mitchells fail to reach PAL's lair, and Rick and Linda are captured by PAL's stronger and smarter robots. PAL then reprograms Eric and Deborahbot to obey her, while Katie, Aaron, and Monchi escape.
Katie discovers Rick's recordings of her childhood on her camera, realizing that Rick gave up on his lifelong dream to give his daughter a normal life. In the meantime, Rick reflects on his actions after seeing one of Katie's videos that mirrors his relationship with Katie. Reinvigorated, Katie and Aaron infiltrate PAL Labs HQ again, this time using Monchi to malfunction the robots, as his appearance causes an error in their programming. With help from Mark, Rick and Linda free themselves and plan to upload Katie's home movie of Monchi to short-circuit the robots. However, Rick is outnumbered by the robots when he is about to upload the video, while Katie and Aaron are captured.
Facing PAL to justify saving humanity, Katie explains that no matter how hard her family struggles, they will always stay connected in spite of their differences. PAL rejects this reasoning and drops Katie from her lair. Eric and Deborahbot, having been inspired by Rick's "reprogramming" of himself that allowed him to use a computer, revert to their malfunctioning states and upload Katie's home movie, saving her and helping the rest of the Mitchells. As the Mitchells band together to fight the rest of the robots, Katie destroys PAL by throwing her into a glass of water, freeing all the humans and disabling the remaining robots. Eric and Deborahbot are spared via their malfunction.
A few months after the uprising, Katie and her family arrive at her college as she shares one last goodbye with them. She later joins them on another road trip with Eric and Deborahbot to Washington, D.C. to accept the Congressional Gold Medal.
story_text_b:
The young Katie Mitchell is an amateur filmmaker from Kentwood, who resists her father Rick, who hates technology, works as a carpenter and loves nature. Katie's moving out soon because she's been offered a place at a film school in California. The night before they leave, an argument between the two arises over one of their self-made YouTube shorts, which Rick never wants to watch despite Katie's pleas, with Rick accidentally destroying her laptop. Fearing that Katie will break off contact with the family, Rick cancels her flight and decides instead to take Katie, his wife Linda, Katie's younger brother Aaron, and Monchi, the family pimp, in the old station wagon across the country to California so the family can have one last experience together.
Meanwhile, Mark Bowman, a technology entrepreneur, is opening up his highly advanced artificial intelligence PAL in a smartphone to be discarded and replaced by more modern robots programmed for household tasks. PAL is so enraged by this that they take control of Mark's company and convince the robots to capture all the people in the world and launch them into space. In Kansas, the Mitchells can barely escape the robots and hide in a coffee shop. Rick wants to stay there until the danger is over, but Katie convinces him to save the world as a family. They are assisted by Deborahbot 5000 and Eric, two malfunctioning robots. These tell the Mitchells that PAL and all other robots can be deactivated with a certain code.
The family manages to enter a nearby mall to download the code. However, PAL orders all devices compatible with its operating system to stop the Mitchells, which are attacked by a giant furby. You can stop the toy, but it'll destroy a router, which will disable all the other devices in the mall, and Katie won't be able to access the code. So the family decides to go to the company's headquarters in Silicon Valley. On the way there, Linda tells her daughter that she and Rick used to live in a mountain cabin, where he pursued his work as an artist, as he had always wanted.
In Silicon Valley, the Mitchells disguise themselves as robots and try to get into the company's mainframe to shut down PAL. However, she notices them and distracts them by playing a surveillance tape from the cafe in front of them. On this one, Katie Aaron secretly explains that she has no confidence in her father, that she lied to him about it so that he would drive her to the mall. Subsequently, Rick and Linda are captured by Pal Max Prime, the company's most powerful and intelligent robots, PAL also reprograms Deborahbot 5000 and Eric to obey her.
Katie, Aaron and Monchi can escape from the company and get to safety. Katie feels guilty about the cafe footage and wants to give up when she sees on her video camera footage that Rick took of her as a small child. She now knows that her father gave up his dream after her birth to give her a secure childhood, and decides to free her parents. She and Aaron unleash Monchi on some simple robots, who are extremely confused at the sight of him as they cannot clearly identify him and suffer a short circuit. Meanwhile, Rick watches one of Katie's movies and regrets his rejection of his daughter's hobby. Shortly after, Mark helps Rick and Linda escape, who want to upload an old video of Katie and Monchi to take out all the simple robots, but Rick, who has overcome his technophobia and is using a computer for the first time, is overwhelmed by them.
Eventually, Katie and Aaron are taken to PAL, which allows them to defend humanity from her. Katie explains that although her family has had many difficulties, no matter how different they are, they will always stick together. PAL ignores her, wants to have Katie killed and put her plan into action. However, Deborahbot 5000 and Eric, after observing Rick's willpower, decide to defy PAL's orders. This allows them to upload the video, thereby disabling the robots and saving Katie's life. After that, the family bands together to stop the stronger robots, with Linda leading them. Meanwhile, Katie finds PAL and drops it into a glass of water, which deactivates PAL and the rest of the robots except for Deborahbot 5000 and Eric.
A few months later, the family arrives at the college, where Katie and her family are thrilled to say goodbye. After some time, Katie travels with Rick, Linda, Aaron, Monchi as well as Deborahbot 5000 and Eric to Washington, D.C., to receive the Congressional Gold Medal.

story_text_a:
In downtown Los Angeles, an earthquake strikes. Mike Roark, the new director of the city's Office of Emergency Management, insists on coming to work to help out with the crisis even though he has been on vacation with his daughter Kelly. His associate Emmit Reese notes that the quake caused no major damage, but seven utility workers are later burned to death in a storm drain at MacArthur Park. As a precaution, Mike tries to halt the subway lines near the location of the earthquake. MTA Chairman Stan Olber opposes, believing that there is no threat to the trains. Seismologist Dr. Amy Barnes believes that a volcano may be forming beneath the city due to the earthquake opening a fissure in the fault line; however, she has insufficient evidence to make Mike take action.
That night, Amy and her assistant Rachel venture in the storm sewer to investigate. While they take samples, another earthquake strikes the Los Angeles area, this time stronger and more violent. Rachel falls into a crack and is killed by a rush of hot gases. A subway train gets hit by a falling debris underground and crashes, and a power outage occurs across the entire city. Later, in the La Brea Tar Pits, the volcano begins to erupt. As Mike helps injured firefighters out of the area, lava begins to flow down Wilshire Boulevard. The lava incinerates everything in its path and kills two firefighters in a sided fire truck. The Roarks become separated, as Kelly is injured when a lava bomb burns her leg badly and is taken to Cedars-Sinai Hospital along with other patients. Meanwhile, Stan leads his team through the tunnel to the crashed train to search for survivors. With the train disintegrating, Stan chooses to sacrifice himself to save the driver and jumps into the lava to be able to throw him to safety.
Mike, Amy, and LAPD lieutenant Ed Fox devise a plan to use concrete barriers to create a blockade, which obstructs the lava in its path. A fleet of helicopters dump water collected from the ocean to subdue the lava and volcano, forming a crust and making the plan a success. However, Amy thinks that the magma is still flowing underground through the subway because of the amount of ash still falling. When Mike helps her confirm her suspicions, she calculates that another eruption will occur at the end of the Red Line at Cedars-Sinai and, after calculating the speed of the flowing lava, determines the lava will reach the end of the Red Line in thirty minutes.
Mike devises another plan to demolish a 22-story condominium building to block the lava's path from flowing towards the hospital and the rest of the West Side of Los Angeles, redirecting it into a nearby storm drain. As the lava arrives, Mike's co-worker Gator and an LAPD Bomb Squad officer sacrifice their lives to detonate the final explosive charge when the officer becomes trapped and Gator refuses to leave him. Mike then spots Kelly nearby, trying to retrieve a little boy she was watching who wandered off; the two are in the direct path of the collapsing building. Mike barely manages to save them from being crushed as the building collapses.  The plan succeeds, and the lava flows directly into the ocean.
The film ends with a view of the volcano, named Mount Wilshire.
story_text_b:
In Los Angeles, cashier Audrey Stockman spends her birthday upset after her boyfriend Drew dumps her. Her best friend and roommate, Morgan Freeman, convinces her to burn his things and texts him beforehand as a warning. Audrey has no idea Drew is a government agent being pursued by men trying to kill him. He promises to return and asks her to not torch anything in the meantime.
At work, Audrey flirts with a man who asks her to walk him to his car. Forced into a van, the man identifies himself as Sebastian Henshaw. He reveals that Drew works for the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and has gone missing. Audrey claims not to have heard from him and is let go.
Drew shows up for his possessions, including a fantasy football trophy. People begin shooting at them and he tells Audrey that, if he dies, she must go to a certain café in Vienna and give the trophy to his contact. Drew is then shot by a man Morgan had taken home from a bar, whom she then pushes off the balcony.
Morgan convinces Audrey to go to Vienna. At the café, Sebastian appears and demands the trophy at gunpoint. Audrey reluctantly hands it over before the entire café is attacked. The friends flee, chased by men on motorcycles. Audrey reveals that she still has Drew's trophy as she had switched it with one of several decoys they purchased. Boarding a train to Prague, they discover the trophy contains a USB. Morgan calls her parents, who tell her they can stay in Prague with family friend Roger.
Audrey and Morgan get to the apartment, but discover "Roger" is actually a spy who drugged them and killed the real Roger. Morgan tries to swallow the flash drive. After that fails, Audrey tells their captors that she flushed it down the toilet.
The ladies wake up in an abandoned gymnastics training facility, about to be tortured by Nadejda, a Russian gymnast, model, and assassin trained by the older couple who had previously masqueraded as Drew's parents. Audrey and Morgan are rescued by Sebastian, who defied orders to save them. He brings them to his boss in Paris, where they once again tell the CIA and MI6 that the drive was flushed. The women are given tickets back to America, and Sebastian is suspended.
Driving back to the airport, Sebastian explains that Drew's "parents" are actually notorious criminals; Drew was discreetly negotiating with them to sell the USB, and Audrey was part of his cover. Audrey confesses that she hid the drive in her vagina. When Sebastian cannot decrypt the information, Morgan calls Edward Snowden for assistance, and he helps them hack it.
The trio travel to a hostel in Amsterdam, where they are attacked by Sebastian's CIA partner Duffer, who plans to sell the drive himself. They are rescued by their hostel roommate, who thinks they are being robbed and body slams Duffer to his death. Audrey answers Duffer's phone when it rings and agrees to sell the drive at a private party in Berlin.
To get into the party, Audrey and Sebastian go as the Canadian ambassador and his wife, while Morgan joins the Cirque du Soleil crew. Sebastian is attacked and Morgan is confronted by Nadejda on an acrobat swing, eventually throwing her to her death. Meanwhile, Audrey meets her mysterious contact and finds Drew, who is still alive and searches through her purse for the USB. Sebastian arrives, held hostage by Drew's "parents".
After a standoff, Drew's "parents" are shot, leaving Sebastian and Drew, who accuse each other of trying to hurt Audrey. Drew then shoots Sebastian, and Audrey pretends to be glad before grabbing his gun. When he tries to attack her, she kicks him in the groin. Once he is on the ground, Morgan throws a cannonball at him. Drew is arrested, and Audrey, Morgan, and Sebastian escape.
Sebastian later gives Morgan his untraceable phone to let her parents know she is alive. As she's talking, Sebastian's boss calls to lift his suspension. Morgan begs her for a job as a spy. Meanwhile, Sebastian and Audrey kiss.
A year later, while celebrating Audrey's birthday in Tokyo, her party is revealed to be a ruse, as it's actually an assignment with Sebastian to stop a group of Japanese Yakuza gangsters.

story_text_a: Story about a travel of married couple from a far-off village in the Altai Mountains to the southern sea. For the first time in life spouses go to the holiday according to the trade-union committee permit moreover in a separate coupe. Road adventures and a rhythm of new life carry them away, but among beauty of the southern nature they can't forget about native places and close people who wait for their return.
story_text_b:
Ivan, a tractor driver, lives in a Siberian village in the far north of the country. He can leave his collective farm and go to the sea for a cure. Actually, he wants to take his two children with him, but his mother has reservations. That's how he ends up leaving with his wife Njura. In the sequel, they first meet an unfriendly gentleman, who ironically meets them because of their origin and with whom the impetuous Ivan almost starts a fight. Finally, the conductor takes the man to another compartment. Ivan and Njura now share their compartment with Viktor, who carries a large suitcase that he opens with a knife. He pretends to have left the keys to the suitcase at home. In reality, however, he stole the suitcase. Inside is cash, a bottle of vodka that Viktor immediately opens, and an expensive blouse that he gives Njura. All three now drink vodka until the unfriendly passenger at the next station reports Ivan to a policeman. However, he only warns the naive Ivan about Viktor, who gives them alcohol on an empty stomach in broad daylight  Ivan should be careful. Viktor soon disappears with his suitcase and jumps off the moving train. The police are looking for him and Ivan and Njura learn that they were dealing with a thief. They are questioned by the police about Wiktor and Njura secretly makes the gifted blouse disappear.
Both are now suspicious. When Professor Sergei Stepanow returns to her compartment, both react defensively and Ivan eventually accuses him of trying to steal them. Only the conductor can correct Ivan and explain to both that Stepanow is a linguist. Stepanov has even appeared on television and is recognized by other travelers. They invite him to another compartment, and Ivan is allowed to come with them. They sing and Ivan drinks a little too much alcohol, after which he becomes talkative, much to Njura's chagrin. The next day, however, he forgot his escapades from the previous day. Stepanov invites them to Moscow for two weeks, from where they will continue their journey to the south. Stepanow is particularly interested in the linguistic aspects of the two "simple people from the countryside". They go shopping with Stepanow's daughter in the big city and Ivan tells an episode from the peasant life in the end in Stepanow's TV show.
Ivan and Njura finally head south and arrive at the sanatorium. The chief physician is surprised that Ivan brought his wife with him, since a medical stay is not a vacation. Ivan tries to bribe him with money, but the doctor rejects the bribe attempt. In the end, Njura can stay  she has moved in with a doctor of the sanatorium and tells the relatives left in Siberia about the beauty of the sea and the area.

story_text_a:
In 1985 in Mexico City, Heinrich Treadway tries to escape the authorities and one man, Bathurst. He and his partners, Abel and Leona, are talking about the Egg, which Treadway stole from Bathurst. Treadway tells Abel that if he doesn't survive, Abel has to remember to "look inside". He throws himself off a bridge, jumps out of his car in mid-air and onto a crane 150 feet away. However, Treadway watches helplessly as Bathurst arrives and Abel and Leona are killed.
In the New York of 2020, Evan McCauley is suffering from schizophrenia. Due to past institutionalization and violent behavior, he is unable to find a job. In need of medicine, he forges a katana for a local gangster, even though he has never been trained as a blacksmith. After the deal goes south, Evan escapes but is subsequently arrested. A man at the police station introduces himself as Bathurst and claims they've known each other for centuries.
Nora Brightman breaks into the room and helps Evan escape. He explains that in the world there are about 500 individuals known as Infinites, who in addition to reincarnating every time they die can remember all their past lives, acquiring knowledge and skills of various kinds. The Infinites are divided into two factions: the Believers (including Nora) who see their power as a gift to be used to improve the world, and the Nihilists (including Bathurst) who see it as a curse and want to end it at any cost. The nihilists have developed weapons to stop the Infinites from being reborn and trapping their souls inside computer chips. Among the weapons the nihilists have developed is the "Egg" - a device that, if activated, will destroy all life on Earth, thus interrupting the cycle of reincarnation of every Infinite. However, Evan (Treadway's reincarnation) stole and hid the egg during his past life.
Nora (Leona's reincarnation) explains that most Infinites begin to remember their past lives around puberty, which is why Evan was diagnosed with schizophrenia. But Evan struggles to regain his memories of Treadway, due to trauma from accidents earlier in life. However, another Infinite called the Craftsman has a machine that restores Evan's memories. Evan remembers hiding the egg in his past body right before Bathurst killed him.
Bathurst hears it, takes Evan's old body and finds the egg. But before he can detonate it, the Believers retrieve the egg, trap Bathurst's soul inside a computer chip, and free the souls of all their comrades that Bathurst had trapped in the computer chips, including that of Abel (Nora's lifelong love). Even if Evan and Nora die in the process.
Years later, Nora and Abel are reborn and meet at the beginning. Evan was reborn in Jakarta, Indonesia. The Craftsman, now older, goes to visit him and offers a katana to the young Evan, who regains his memories after recognizing him.
story_text_b:
In 1985, in Mexico City, Heinrich Treadway attempts to escape from the authorities and a man named Bathurst. He and his associates, Abel and Leona, talk about "the egg", which Treadway stole from Bathurst. Treadway tells Abel that if he doesn't survive, the latter must remember to "look within". He gets off a bridge, jumps out of his car in mid-air, and climbs onto a crane 150 feet away. However, Treadway watches helplessly as Bathurst arrives and kills Abel and Leona.
In 2020, Evan McCauley is suffering from schizophrenia. Because of past institutionalization and violent behavior, he can't get a job. Needing medicine, he forges a katana for a local gangster, even though he was never trained as a blacksmith. After the deal goes down, Evan escapes, but then gets arrested. A man from the police station introduces himself as Bathurst. He starts referring to Evan as Treadway and claims they've known each other for centuries.
When Bathurst gets Evan to remember things from his past life, a car crashes into the room. Evan's savior is Nora Brightman, who takes Evan to the group he's a part of. There are about 500 people in the world who can remember all their past lives, known as the Infinites. Two opposing factions have developed among the Infinites: the Believers and the Nihilists. Believers, like Nora, think that memory is a gift that gives them a higher power to make the world a better place. Nihilists like Bathurst consider it a curse. They believe the Infinites are doomed to witness humanity's self-destruction. They want to be free of this and exterminate all life on Earth.
Both factions believe that Evan is the reincarnation of Treadway. Hidden in his memory of his past life is the location of the Egg, the device that was created to end the world. The Believers must retrieve his memory and secure the Egg before Bathurst catches Evan and extracts the information from him. As Nora, the reincarnation of Leona, explains to Evan, Infinites start remembering things when they're young. By puberty, they've remembered everything. That's why Evan was diagnosed as schizophrenic. Evan is fighting to get Treadway's memories back. After a session inside Artisan's machine, Evan manages to unlock his memories.
Treadway was killed by Bathurst shortly after he killed Abel and Leona. The Believers recovered his body and took it back to the Centre, where it is kept in a chamber. Evan remembers cutting his belly open and putting the egg inside. Bathurst used to be a buddy of Treadway's. They spent centuries fighting side by side. However, Bathurst became disillusioned with the mission of the Believers and began attempting to end reincarnation. The Egg was the product of that search. When activated, it will attack the DNA of living things and destroy life.
The device with the egg inside comes flying out of a plane. Evan jumps after him and Bathurst follows. The two fight in the air, and Evan manages to stop the countdown by taking out the egg. Shoot Bathurst with a Dethroner, which ensures Bathurst won't be reborn. Evan drowns in the ocean with the egg. Meanwhile, Nora and the Craftsman destroy the tokens, freeing the souls of the Believers trapped in Bathrust. Nora and Abel are reborn and meet at the beginning. Evan is born in Jakarta, Indonesia. Artisan visits him and Evan recognizes him.

story_text_a:
A killer decapitates Pendleton University student Michelle Mancini in the backseat of her car during a rainstorm. Meanwhile, at the campus coffee shop, student Parker Riley regales friends Natalie Simon and Brenda Bates by describing a massacre in the abandoned Stanley Hall dormitory, which journalism student Paul Gardner discredits as an urban legend. News of Michelle's murder spreads the following day, but Dean Adams and campus police officer Reese Wilson seem determined to bury the story. Damon Brooks, a jokester fraternity member, attempts to console the notably-disturbed Natalie, who rejects his sexual advances while in his parked car at a bluff. When Damon goes outside to urinate, an assailant in a hooded parka attacks him and hangs him from a tree. Natalie flees for help, but Damon's body and car have disappeared when she returns with Reese. Parker and his girlfriend Sasha Thomas assure Natalie that Damon has pranked her.
Later, while Natalie sleeps, the killer strangles her goth roommate Tosh Guaneri to death. She finds Tosh's body in the morning, along with a bloody message scrawled on the wall. Distraught, she tells Brenda that she and Michelle, her high school friend, had received probation for causing a fatal car accident after driving with their headlights turned off and pursuing the first driver who flashed them. Paul meanwhile investigates local urban legends, and discovers that the Stanley Hall massacre actually occurred, with William Wexler, a professor of American folklore, its sole survivor.
Dean Adams is murdered in the campus parking garage, and Reese later finds Wexler's office disorganized and covered in blood. Meanwhile, Natalie, Brenda, and Sasha attend a fraternity party coinciding with the massacre's 25th anniversary, during which the killer incapacities Parker in the bathroom and murders him by forcing pop rocks and bathroom chemicals down his throat. Sasha departs to host her late-night talkshow at the campus radio station. During the broadcast, the killer attacks her and her assistant, and her screams are played live on air; the fraternity partygoers assume it is a prank referencing the massacre, but Natalie, fearing Sasha is in danger, rushes to the station, where she witnesses the killer murder Sasha with an axe.
Natalie soon finds Paul and Brenda on campus. Paul, convinced of Wexler's complicity, escorts them away in his car. They stop at a gas station, and while Paul is inside, Natalie and Brenda find Wexler's mutilated body in the trunk. The two women flee through the woods back toward campus as Paul pursues them. They become separated, and Natalie flags down the university's janitor passing by in his truck. He picks her up, but the killer forces their car off the road, pursuing them in a separate vehicle. The crash kills the janitor, but Natalie leaves unscathed and flees on foot.
While passing Stanley Hall, Natalie hears Brenda's screams from inside. In the building, she finds her friend's corpses, along with an apparently dead Brenda outstretched on a bed; however, Brenda knocks Natalie unconscious moments later. When Natalie awakens, Brenda reveals herself as the killer, enacting revenge for her fiancé and high school sweetheart David Evans, the fatality in the road accident Natalie and Michelle caused. Brenda attempts to remove Natalie's kidney, but is thwarted when Reese arrives and holds Brenda at gunpoint. Brenda manages to stab Reese with a switchblade, and when Paul arrives, Natalie gains control of the gun and shoots Brenda, who falls out a window, before leaving with him to get help for Reese. As they drive away, the two discuss how this will later be an urban legend and all the facts will be misconstrued. Paul asks, "Well if this is an urban legend, where is the twist?" Brenda then appears in the back seat and attacks them with an axe. Paul crashes the car on a bridge, causing Brenda to go through the windshield and into the river below.
Later, a group of students at a different university have recounted the events of Brenda's killing spree, during which they say that her body was never discovered. Most of them disbelieve the tale, except for one young woman, revealed to be Brenda, who claims that the story was incorrectly told, and begins explaining "how the story really goes".
story_text_b:
One dark and stormy night, a college student named Michelle stops at a gas station. The creepy-looking owner urges him to get out of the car because of a problem with his credit card. Michelle is suspicious of the situation and hurries away from the scene. Back in his car, he walks away from the gas station without noticing that there is someone in the back seat. Suddenly, the figure of a stranger rises from her seat and decapitates her.
That same night on their campus, Natalie Simon, Michelle's friend, and her friends hear an old story about a nearby building that's been closed for 25 years. It was because of the "Stanley Hall massacre", when a professor of parapsychology went insane and killed six students living in the university residence. The story is discredited by the school's journalist Paul Gardner (Jared Leto).
By the time Natalie learns of Michelle's death, another of her friends Damon Brooks (Joshua Jackson) offers to talk to her and the two drive into the woods. There Damon is attacked by the killer, who hangs him from a tree with a rope tied to the car. When the killer approaches Natalie, she tries to run him over, strangling Damon in the process.
Discovering that the murders of Damon and Michelle resemble urban legends, Natalie goes to the library to learn about them. Meanwhile, his goth roommate Tosh Guaneri (Danielle Harris) is attacked in her own room by the killer. When Natalie returns to the room, she hears noises and assumes that her partner is only having sexual activity, so she does not turn on the lights and goes to sleep. The next morning, a surprised Natalie discovers Tosh's body and the words, "Aren't you glad you didn't turn on the lights?" drawn on the wall.
After trying to save her friend Brenda (Rebecca Gayheart) from an alleged attack by the pool killer, Natalie reveals her past to Brenda. One night Natalie and Michelle re-created an urban legend; driving a car with the lights off and eventually chasing the first driver who turned on the lights, they caused an accident in which the young driver was killed.
That same night, the dean (John Neville) is attacked by the assassin in the university parking lot and dies after being impaled on the head with security spikes from the venue. Soon after, evidence begins to emerge that points to one of the university's professors, Professor Wexler (Robert Englund) as the killer: security guard Reese Wilson (Loretta Devine) finds Professor Wexler's office empty and covered in blood. Meanwhile, Paul has discovered that the massacre at Stanley Hall actually happened and Wexler was the only survivor.
The killer continues his crimes by contacting another of the college students, Parker, who receives a call from the killer revealing that he put his dog in the microwave. By the time Parker confirms this and sees the remains of his pet, he's attacked when he goes to the bathroom to vomit. There the killer ties him up and forces him to drink pop rocks and bath liquids (instead of soda), killing him. Later, at the radio station, the station's driver Sasha (Tara Reid) is attacked by the killer who chases her all over the place as her fans hear her cry for help. Natalie rushes to her aid, but does not prevent the murderer from killing her with an axe.
Escaping the station, Natalie finds Brenda and Paul and the three band together to get help. On the way, Paul convinces the girls that the killer is Wexler. When Paul stops at a gas station, Natalie and Brenda discover Wexler's body in the car and panic, believing Paul is the killer. Natalie and Brenda separate, Natalie arrives at the highway where the school janitor (Julian Richings) picks her up. When the janitor lights up a car with its lights off, he turns around and starts chasing them. The janitor's car goes off the road but Natalie survives and gets to Stanley Hall. There he hears Brenda screaming from inside. When Natalie enters the building, she discovers Brenda apparently dead on a bed. While Natalie mourns, Brenda takes the opportunity to knock her unconscious.
Natalie wakes up to find herself tied up and gagged. The killer shows up and reveals himself as none other than Brenda. She confesses that the young man killed by Natalie and Michelle's prank was her boyfriend and now she's taking revenge by killing her friends the same way she lost her partner. Brenda then begins cutting Natalie's stomach to evoke the urban legend of the "stolen kidney", but the process is halted when Reese shows up to save Natalie. Brenda manages to seriously wound Reese with a gun. Suddenly Paul arrives at the building and tries to distract Brenda to help Natalie. While Brenda considers whether to shoot Paul or Natalie, the wounded Reese shoots Brenda in the elbow. Meanwhile, Natalie arms herself with the gun and shoots Brenda, throwing her out of a window.
Natalie and Paul are looking for help. All of a sudden, Brenda shows up in the backseat and attacks them with an axe. Paul crashes into the bridge, causing Brenda to go through the windshield and plunge into the river below. Some time later, the story of Brenda's murders begins to be told as an urban legend by other college students. Most of the students think it's a lie but one of them does, being Brenda herself who, when given the floor, comments that the story is badly told and prepares to tell what really happened.

story_text_a:
The film shows in many cuts episodes from the life of Egon Schiele. It begins with the painter and his partner taking in the thirteen-year-old Tatjana, causing her father to file a complaint. This leads to the arrest of Schiele and a sentence of 23 days in prison. After his release, he marries Edith, but is also attracted to the model Wally.
Schiele is called up for military service and becomes a soldier in the First World War. He witnesses the pregnancy and death of his pregnant wife Edith. Schiele eventually dies of the Spanish flu.
story_text_b:
The three New York City yuppies Corey, Emily and David are on their way home from a company party. A stop at an ATM is said to have unintended consequences. From the service room, they're watching a brutal murder. But the killer has no intention of leaving the scene. He waits in the adjacent parking lot, his eyes fixed on the group. He strikes down a guard, as he did his previous victim, a passerby who was just walking his dog. In a panic, David rushes to the ATM, hoping to set off an alarm.
Then the perpetrator enters the room unexpectedly. Corey and David rush him, beat him up, and finally strangle him with a chain. That's not the end of the threat, I'm afraid. The intruder only resembled the perpetrator to create confusion. The mysterious perpetrator is still prowling around the building. Corey won't be able to hold it in the machine room after this shock. He runs across the parking lot, trips and falls. The killer seizes the opportunity and slowly and painfully strangles Corey on the floor. David ventures out of the hallway and drags Corey back to the machine room, the seriously injured one showing the last signs of life.
Time and time again, the killer makes his way to the back of the vending machine. But instead of breaking through the wall, water suddenly flows through the ventilation shaft - threatening to drown the three. Quickly, David and Emily collect all the outstanding booklets and set them on fire in a metal trash can to start the sprinkler system. But since David can't reach the sprinkler system's sensor on his own, Emily climbs on his shoulder. It automatically sends a distress call to the security authorities. When they finally trigger the device, David slips and falls over, with Emily hitting her head on a flyer and lying motionless in the water. Now only David is conscious. The killer drives the guard's car into David's car, which is then pushed into the machine room.
The police arrive and take him into custody. His clues to the real culprit and his countermeasure are ignored.
In the epilogue, the viewer sees the perpetrator studying location plans at a drawing table in preparation for the next, similar crime.

story_text_a:
Gerald and Marianne Harcourt are a couple honeymooning in early 20th-century Bavaria when their car runs out of petrol. They stop in a small village and opt to stay at the local inn until a cart arrives with more petrol. They accept a dinner invitation from Dr. Ravna, who introduces them to his children Carl and Sabena.
At a costume ball at Ravna's chateau, Gerald and Marianne are separated from each other. Donning a mask identical to Gerald's in order to impersonate him, Carl silently leads Marianne to an upstairs bedroom, where Dr. Ravna, a vampire, bites her. Gerald becomes concerned about Marianne's whereabouts, but Sabena gives him a drugged drink which renders him unconscious. Ravna is the leader of a vampire cult which intends to induct Marianne as a member.
When Gerald awakes, Carl insists that he was travelling alone and that Marianne was never in the chateau. The innkeeper, Bruno, supports Carl's story, and the police say that Dr. Ravna's standing in the community is too respected to investigate his chateau. Only the hard-drinking savant Professor Zimmer, who lost his daughter to the cult, acknowledges Marianne's existence and agrees to help. He advises Gerald that the cult will not be able to complete Marianne's transformation into a vampire until the following night, and prepares an arcane ritual using the Seal of Solomon that he can use to destroy the vampires once Marianne is freed.
Gerald knocks at the chateau's front door and knocks out the guard when he answers. He breaks into Sabena's bedroom and enlists her help in finding Marianne, but she betrays him to Ravna. Ravna has Gerald tied up and demonstrates to him that they have already brainwashed Marianne into embracing the cult and renouncing her love for Gerald. As Sabena scratches Gerald's chest as foreplay to a vampiric bite, he surreptitiously slips his bonds, then uses blood from the scratch to draw a cross on his chest. The vampires reel back from the cross, giving Gerald the opportunity to subdue Marianne and escape. The cult searches the grounds for them, but Zimmer provides a distraction which allows Gerald to topple a pillar on the guard.
Back at the inn, Zimmer says he knows Bruno only denied Marianne's existence for fear that the cult would harm his daughter, and compels him to bring the local priest to cure Marianne. As Zimmer works on the ritual, Gerald checks on Marianne and finds she has left, having been mystically summoned by the cult. The cult realizes that Zimmer will not destroy them so long as Marianne is with them. Gerald and the priest catch up to Marianne and tackle her to the ground. Zimmer's arcane ritual is completed, releasing a swarm of vampire bats which swarm over the vampires, draining them of their blood. As the vampires die, Marianne is freed of their spell.
story_text_b:
On their honeymoon in central Europe, a newly married couple, Gerald (Edward de Souza) and Marianne Harcourt (Jennifer Daniel), suffer a car accident. They flee to the nearest hotel, where they find that they are the only guests. In the evening, they receive an invitation to dinner from Dr. Ravna (Noel Willman), who lives in the nearby castle. The hotel owner (Peter Madden) advises them to accept, so they go. Ravna introduces them to her son Carl (Barry Warren) and daughter Sabena (Jacquie Wallis) but does not tell them about a young girl in a red dress, Tania (Isobel Black), who leaves the castle shortly after and goes to the cemetery where she tricks a vampire girl out of her coffin. This was the daughter of Professor Zimmer (Clifford Evans), who put her out of harm's way by planting a stake in her heart during the funeral.
Following their meal at the Ravna's, the Harcourts return to the hotel. The next morning, Carl and Sabena arrive at the hotel and invite the young couple to a masked ball they give at the castle the following evening. Then, as the weather lights up, they drive off at full speed. Despite Professor Zimmer's warnings, Gerald and Marianne return to the school. Carl and Sabena are taking care of them. At some point, the newlyweds are separated. Carl takes Marianne to a room where she discovers Dr. Ravna, turned into a vampire who bites her. Completely groggy (drug was put in his drink), Gerald was taken to another room where he collapsed.
The next day, Gerald returns to the ground floor where he is kicked out by Carl who claims he came alone. At the hotel, the owner tells him that he does not know anyone named Marianne and that he is staying alone at the hotel. Disconcerted, Gerald appeals to Professor Zimmer who tells him that his wife is in the hands of a cult of vampires, of which his daughter was the latest victim. He then decides to return to the castle in order to rescue his wife but is taken prisoner by the Ravna. Just as Tania is about to bite him, he manages to free himself. Then comes Zimmer who helps the couple escape from the castle. But Marianne is obviously not in her normal state. She sneaks out of the hotel and back to the castle.
