In his laboratory, Zimmer then cast a series of incantations. That's when thousands of bats attack the castle and kill the vampires by draining their blood. Marianne is safe.

story_text_a: Wren, a sarcastic teenager, is invited by a boy to celebrate Halloween at his house but is forced to watch over her little brother during the night. The latter suddenly disappears during the candy hunt. Wren has to find him before their mother gets back from the party.
story_text_b: In Cleveland, Ohio, Wren DeSantis and his friend April are invited to a Halloween party by the school's most popular boy Aaron Riley, but on the same night she is also forced to babysit her younger brother Albert by his widowed mother, Joy so that she can go out and have fun with her new 26-year-old boyfriend. After spending the evening trick-or-treating around town, she loses sight of him in a haunted house, the night turning into a hunt for the little brother before his mother finds out.

story_text_a:
A 15-year-old drifter named Gary asks Joe, the boss of a Texan tree-poisoning crew, for a job, and impresses him with his industriousness. The next day, Gary brings his alcoholic father, Wade, to work, but Wade's poor attitude and laziness get them fired. Joe witnesses Wade beat Gary and take his money. Gary later goes to Joe's house to ask for his job. Joe agrees, and Gary begins working for him, hiding his money from Wade.
Willie Russell, a criminal with whom Joe has a long-standing feud, shoots and wounds Joe as he leaves a friend's house. Later, Gary meets Willie and asks for a ride home; when Willie makes lewd comments about Gary's younger sister, Dorothy, Gary beats him up. Later, Wade beats to death a homeless man, stealing his liquor. Willie confronts Joe at a bar and asks where Gary lives in order to seek revenge. Joe does not answer and, when Willie presses him, beats him up. Joe tells the bartender to call the police before fleeing to a brothel but leaves after getting spooked by a guard dog. He goes home, gets his dog and returns to the brothel, setting it on the guard dog, and has a prostitute give him oral sex. He leaves with his dog, who has killed the guard dog. Two police officers stop him at gunpoint, and Joe challenges them to a fight. Joe is arrested but released.
Wade asks Gary for money, but Gary denies having any. Wade finds food in the cupboard and questions how he can afford food. They get into an argument that ends with Wade pulling a knife. He leaves but threatens to return and find Gary's money. Gary visits Joe, who tells him that he served 29 months for assaulting police officers. Gary agrees to help Joe look for his missing dog. After spending hours together and bonding, they find the dog and Joe gives Gary his lighter as a keepsake. Joe finds Wade walking and offers him a ride. They do not get far before Wade insults Gary and accuses Joe of not paying him. Joe grabs him by the collar and threatens to hurt him if anything happens to Gary.
Later on, Gary tells Joe that he has enough money to buy his truck, and Joe takes him to the dealership where he has bought a new one. Joe tells Gary to keep the money he was going to use to buy Joe's truck and use it to obtain insurance. When he questions what insurance is, Joe promises to help him with it. As Joe drives home, a patrol cop stops him and tries to make him take a breathalyzer, but Joe refuses and drives away. After an altercation, Joe beats up the officer. A senior officer, a friend of Joe's and a fellow ex-con, visit Joe and says the patrol cop had it coming but warns him to keep his nose clean.
Gary arrives at Joe's house, his face bruised, and asks to borrow his truck. Gary reveals that Wade beat him up, stole his truck, and left with Dorothy, intent on pimping her out to Willie and his goon. They go after Wade. Meanwhile, Willie pays Wade $60, and prepares to rape Dorothy first. Joe arrives and subdues Willie, and Gary leaves with Dorothy for help. Willie begs an unmoved Joe for his life, but as Joe prepares to kill him, one of Willie's thugs shoots him in the side and accidentally shoots Willie as well. Joe kills the thug then finishes Willie off before limping towards Wade, who is standing on a nearby bridge. He tries to shoot him, but misses. He attempts to shoot Wade again, but finds he is out of bullets. Wade asks Joe if he is his friend, and when Joe doesn't answer, leaps to his death. Joe then collapses and looks at the gaping wound in his side. Gary arrives with the sheriff and embraces Joe as he dies. He then looks down and sees his father's body.
Later, it is shown that an untold amount of time has passed, Gary is seen driving Joe's car with Joe's dog. He arrives at a job interview to replant the woods Joe and his crew had originally torn down.
story_text_b: In a small, remote Texas town, Joe (Nicolas Cage), a man in his late 50's, owns a modest logging business and employs a few poor people with whom he has developed cordial friendships. He got out of prison, where he ended up for violence against police officers, but he remains on probation, which makes him very dependent on the possible effects of his bloody moods and forces him to control them. One day, a teenager comes to him, starts working, and shows a special willingness. Unfortunately, the young man's father is a deeply alcoholic, violent, unscrupulous individual, occasionally murderous. He makes the acquaintance of a small local gangster who has been in trouble with Joe for a long time; this encounter will unintentionally accelerate events and make them more and more tragic.

story_text_a:
In 2063, astrophysicists on a climate-change-ravaged Earth find a habitable planet. A scouting mission is sent, although the roughly 86-year flight means that the launch crew astronauts' grandchildren will be the ones who reach the planet. To help the crew cope with spending their remaining lives mostly in flight, the original 30 are bred through IVF and kept in isolation from the rest of the world. To extend their time in flight, they are launched on the Humanitas spaceship as pre-teens, with a single adult, senior program commander Richard, to guide them through the journey's early stage. The plan is for IVF to be performed when the crew turns 24, to be repeated on those offspring when they turn 24.
During the tenth year of the flight, Christopher and Zac discover a chemical is added to the grown teenagers' food that suppresses the sex drive and pleasure response, keeping them docile and manageable. The pair stops taking the chemical, and their surging hormones drive them to become competitive, careless, and anxious to engage in sexual relations, particularly with crewmate Sela who has trained as chief medical officer.
During a repair effort outside the Humanitas to address a failed Earth communication system, chief officer Richard is killed and a fire damages more ship systems. Christopher is voted the new chief officer, which upsets Zac, who then tells the others to stop ingesting the chemical. The mission descends into madness as many of the young men and women revert to their most primal state.
Zac tells the others an alien killed Richard, and he will protect them, letting them eat all the (closely conserved) food they want. He convinces all but five to follow him rather than Christopher. Christopher and Sela, who have become a couple, find and repair a video disk that reveals Zac killed Richard and precipitated the further systems damage by turning on the electricity to the communications array while Richard was working on it. They show the others, but Zac convinces many that an alien is inhabiting one of them, and his followers murder anyone Zac targets.
Christopher inadvertently leads Zac to a weapons cache for their grandchildren to use on the planet. Christopher, Sela, and Phoebe are the only holdouts. Phoebe is killed as the pack searches for Christopher and Sela. The pair tricks Zac into being ejected into space, and peace returns to Humanitas. Sela is voted chief officer. The crew permanently forgoes the suppression chemical and learn to manage their emotions. They fall in love and have children naturally rather than via the planned IVF.
Decades later, Humanitas and its multi-generational crew arrive at the planet, which appears from orbit to be as Earth-like as hoped.
story_text_b:
# Summary
The plot begins in November 2026, a few months before the start of the 2027 presidential election. The main character, Paul Raison, a civil servant in the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Budget, in his forties, works in the office of Minister Bruno Juge, with whom he also has friendly ties. The political climate is marked by terrorist attacks, which at first spare human lives. These are extremely sophisticated and involve significant military means, without it being easily possible to assess the underlying motives of the authors.
Paul's father, Edouard Raison, is a former member of the Secret Service.
Paul had a long-distance relationship with his wife, Prudence, who was also a civil servant. Paul has a practicing Catholic sister, Cécile, who is married to an unemployed notary, Hervé. The couple live in Arras and openly vote for the National Rally. Finally, Paul has a younger brother, Aurélien, who works as an art restorer for the Ministry of Culture and is married to an obnoxious woman named Indy.
# Characters

story_text_a: Southern Marcus Hubbard made a fortune during the Civil War. He returns to his fellow citizens their contempt for him. Yet, he fails to teach his children to learn from his experience....
story_text_b:
Enriched during the Civil War, Southerner Marcus Hubbard repays the contempt of his fellow citizens with hatred, but he can't stop his children from learning his lesson all too well.
This bourgeois drama set in the deep South can be considered as a sort of even more unpleasant antecedent of Little Foxes, another play by Hellman herself.

story_text_a:
Former Ohio State quarterback and rookie FBI agent Johnny Utah assists experienced agent Angelo Pappas in investigating a string of bank robberies by the "Ex-Presidents": a gang of robbers who wear rubber masks of former presidents Ronald Reagan, Jimmy Carter, Richard Nixon and Lyndon B. Johnson. Rather than robbing the vault, they only demand the cash the tellers have in their drawers, and are gone within ninety seconds.
Pursuing Pappas's theory that the criminals are surfers, Utah goes undercover to infiltrate the surfing community. He fabricates a personal family tragedy to persuade orphaned surfer and restaurant waitress Tyler to teach him to surf, after she saves him from drowning during his first attempt at surfing. Through her, he meets Bodhi, the charismatic leader of a gang of surfers consisting of Roach, Grommet, and Nathaniel. The group are initially wary of Utah, but accept him when Bodhi recognizes him as a former college football star who quit the sport due to a knee injury. As he masters surfing, Utah finds himself increasingly drawn to the surfers' adrenaline-charged lifestyle, Bodhi's philosophies, and Tyler. Following a clue retrieved by analyzing toxins found in the hair of one of the bank robbers, Utah and Pappas lead an FBI raid on another gang of surfers, resulting in the deaths of two of them. The raid inadvertently ruins a DEA undercover operation, as those surfers were wanted for separate charges regarding drug dealing, but they are determined not to be the Ex-Presidents.
Watching Bodhi's group surfing, Utah begins to suspect that they are the Ex-Presidents, noting how close a group they are and the way one of them moons other surfers in the same manner one of the robbers does when leaving a bank. Utah and Pappas stake out a bank and the Ex-Presidents appear. While wearing a Reagan mask, Bodhi leads Utah on a foot chase through the neighborhood, which ends when Utah's old knee injury flares up after jumping into a flood control channel. Despite still having a clear shot, the injured Utah is unwilling to kill Bodhi and allows him to escape, repeatedly shooting into the air instead.
At a campfire that night, it is confirmed that Bodhi and his gang are the Ex-Presidents. Tyler discovers Utah's FBI badge and angrily terminates their relationship after briefly holding him at gunpoint. Shortly afterwards, Bodhi coerces Utah into skydiving with the group. After the jump, Bodhi reveals that he knows Utah is an FBI agent and has arranged for his friend Rosie, a non-surfing thug, to hold Tyler hostage. Utah is blackmailed into participating in the Ex-Presidents' last bank robbery of the summer. As a result, Grommet is killed, along with an off-duty cop and a bank guard who attempt to foil the robbery. Outraged by Grommet's death, Bodhi knocks out Utah and leaves the scene.
Defying their superior, who arrests Utah for the armed robbery, Pappas and Utah head to the airport where Bodhi, Roach, and Nathaniel are about to leave for Mexico. During a shootout, Pappas and Nathaniel are killed and Roach is seriously wounded. With Roach aboard, Bodhi forces Utah onto the plane at gunpoint. Once airborne and over their intended drop zone, Bodhi and Roach put on their parachutes and jump from the plane, leaving Utah to take the blame. With no other parachutes available, Utah jumps from the plane with Bodhi's gun and intercepts him. After landing safely, Utah's knee gives out again, allowing Bodhi to escape Utah's grasp. Bodhi meets with Rosie and releases Tyler. Roach dies of his wounds, and Bodhi and Rosie leave with the money, with Tyler and Johnny watching on.
Nine months later, Utah tracks Bodhi to Bells Beach in Victoria, Australia where a record storm is producing lethal waves. This is an event Bodhi had talked about experiencing, calling it the "50-Year Storm". Utah attempts to bring Bodhi into custody, but Bodhi refuses. During a brawl in the surf, Utah manages to handcuff himself to Bodhi, who begs Utah to release him so he can ride the once-in-a-lifetime wave. Knowing Bodhi will not come back alive, Utah releases him, bids him farewell, and sees him step towards the wave. While the authorities watch Bodhi surf to his death, Utah walks away, throwing his FBI badge into the ocean.
story_text_b:
A gang of four robbers have been attacking banks in Los Angeles County for more than three years: their characteristic is to have their faces hidden by rubber masks depicting four former presidents (Johnson, Nixon, Carter, Reagan); The FBI, which has never been able to trace their true identity, is on their trail, but without having any concrete elements. Special Agent Johnny Utah, an ambitious young man who has just graduated from college, joins forces with Angelo Pappas, an elderly professional and Vietnam veteran, who has a theory: the "rapist-ex-presidents" are surfers who finance their free life with robberies  that they target only in the summer  so that they can move around the world during the winter, looking for locations with the best weather and waves. The theory is supported by two elements: the first consists of the samples of earth and sand found at the scene of the crime, but without ever being taken into account by the investigators and their superiors; the second consists of the security camera recording of the buttocks shown in jest by one of the robbers, which highlights the strong difference in tanning with the typical back of surfers or beach goers.
Johnny follows his partner's theory and infiltrates the world of surfing; after buying an unsuitable board and risking drowning, he is rescued by Tyler, a young but very experienced surfer, from whom he manages to learn the rudiments of surfing and later, thanks to his past as an American football champion, he has the opportunity to participate in a game on the beach where he will meet Bodhi, a character who enjoys great respect in that world. Bodhi, short for Bodhisattva, is defined by Tyler, his former companion, as a "seeker", that is, one who is in perpetual search for the perfect wave, and Johnny begins to associate with him and to appreciate his spirit; this appreciation is reciprocated by Bodhi, who appreciates his new friend's courage and passion.
Johnny continues to investigate and at one point believes that he has identified the robbers in a group of suspicious surfers with whom he has a fight, from which he is saved only thanks to the help of Bodhi.
After locating the surfers' home, Johnny and Angelo, with the cooperation of the special team, break into the building. Soon the situation escalates into a shootout with casualties and injuries. At the end of the shooting the two agents discover with great disappointment that the gang was indeed involved in dirty business, but had nothing to do with the robberies: it was in fact a group of dealers already known to the police, to the point that among them there was also an infiltrated agent of the narcotics team. So they find themselves not only having to start over on their investigations, but also getting a beating for blowing up the narcotics operation, which was waiting to arrest the group so they could discover their drug supply channels.
The former presidents, meanwhile, continue undisturbed in their activities, until the moment when Johnny believes that he recognizes from the attitudes of his friends the same as the robbers; so the next day he stands with Angelo in front of the bank that he believes will be attacked. The hunch turns out to be right, but after Bodhi sets fire to a gas station, causing a devastating explosion, 3 of the robbers manage to escape in a car, while Bodhi is pursued on foot by Johnny, who during the escape hurts his knee and falls. While on the ground, however, he recognizes the friend behind the mask and, despite having him in his sights, hesitates to shoot him, thus allowing him to escape.
His cover blown, Johnny fights with Tyler (with whom he has since started a relationship), as she has discovered he is a cop, and the two separate. Later Johnny is lured into a trap by Bodhi, who forces him, after a parachute jump, to participate in a robbery along with the other former presidents, under the threat of having Tyler killed by an accomplice; in the robbery one of the four is killed, and even an off-duty policeman finds death in the shooting: Johnny is then arrested, and Angelo insists on taking him into custody personally. Johnny confides that the robbers are leaving from the nearby airport, where the two meet them.
Johnny tries to negotiate, but the situation escalates into a shootout in which Angelo and a second robber are killed and a third is seriously injured. Once in the air, the two criminals launch themselves with the only parachutes available: Johnny, desperate because he does not know the fate of the girl, throws himself into the void managing to cling to Bodhi; once the three passengers have reached the ground, the robber Roach also dies, while Johnny, still injured in the knee, can not continue the pursuit of Bodhi, who leaves with the money; however, he obtains the release of Tyler, with whom he is in love; she forgives him for having lied about his identity.
A year later Johnny arrives in Bells Beach, Australia: he seems to be a very changed man in appearance and attitude, and on the beach, during a violent tidal wave, he meets Bodhi, who has come to that place to ride the waves in the so-called "fifty-year storm", a key event that he had previously told Johnny about and that the latter knew he would not miss. After a brief struggle the officer manages to handcuff the friend awaiting the arrival of the Australian police, but Bodhi begs him to let him go, as he would never be able to survive in a cage. The friend, sensing what will happen, opens the handcuffs and lets him crown the last dream of a lifetime, walking away and throwing away his badge because he also has nothing to ask from his profession: he thus ends that part of his life to open another, perhaps dedicated to his passion for surfing, which he says he practices every day since he met him.
The film closes with footage of Bodhi who, soon after being released by Johnny, attempts to ride a giant wave that inevitably overwhelms him, hinting at his end.

story_text_a:
Aladdin, a young thief living in the desert kingdom of Agrabah along with his monkey, Abu, helps and befriends the enterprising Princess Jasmine: she barely adjusts to the law that requires her to marry a prince not for love, but for political strategy, only to be relegated to a secondary role in running the city. The girl, however, does not reveal who she is, preferring to pose as her maid.
Meanwhile Jafar, the Grand Vizier, eager to gain power, seeks, along with his parrot Iago, to gain possession of a magic lamp, hidden inside the Cave of Wonders along with other priceless treasures, to take the place of the rightful Sultan. Both are told that only one person is worthy of entering: "the diamond in the rough", whom Jafar identifies as Aladdin. In fact, when the boy sneaks into the royal palace to return Jasmine's bracelet, the guards imprison him, by order of Jafar, who then frees him, telling him that he can make him rich enough to impress the princess, as long as he brings him the magic lamp, which he so desires. The young man accepts and is led by Jafar himself to the location of the Cave of Wonders, where he also learns that the Grand Vizier himself had in the past been a highwayman.
In the cave, Aladdin finds a flying carpet and the lamp, which he manages to catch. Breaking the rule of not touching anything but the object they're there for, Abu grabs a ruby and soon after the cave begins to collapse. At that point, the two, aided by the carpet, escape and manage to reach the exit, where they hand the lamp to Jafar, who, immediately, pushes both Aladdin and Abu into the depths of the earth. As he closes the cave behind him, the Grand Vizier reaches for the long-awaited lamp, which he had placed by his side, but only then does he realize that the monkey had managed to snatch it from him when, shortly before, he had jumped on it.
Trapped, Aladdin touches the lamp, which releases the genie that lives within him and grants him three wishes. In order not to waste the first, the young man, with a cunning trick, manages to trick him into getting them out of the cave, and, once outside, asks him to assume the identity of a prince to court Jasmine, promising to use his last wish to free him from slavery. Once he assumes the identity of "Prince Ali Ababwa", Aladdin returns to Agrabah accompanied by a large procession, but the princess is not impressed.
After a party thrown by the Sultan to celebrate his arrival, Aladdin takes Jasmine for a ride on the magic carpet, while the Genie goes out with his maid, Dalia. But when the princess deduces his true identity, the young man manages to convince her that, when they had met that time, he had disguised himself as a farmer just to get to know the city, which he was about to reach in official form. However, Jafar discovers his true identity, captures him, and threatens him to reveal where he put the lamp. Aladdin refuses and the Grand Vizier throws him into the sea from the tower. Abu and the carpet, who had seen the scene, arrive with the lamp, which the young man manages to rub before losing consciousness underwater, and the Genie saves him by extracting his second wish (necessary by regulation). Aladdin, after speaking with Jasmine, reveals Jafar's evil plots, who is arrested by the Sultan. The sovereign, grateful for Aladdin's honesty, offers him the hand of his daughter. The young man, fearing he will lose Jasmine if the truth comes out, reluctantly breaks his promise and refuses to release the Genie, upsetting him.
Meanwhile, Iago steals the keys to the prisons and frees Jafar, who manages to snatch the lamp from Aladdin through the streets of Agrabah (while returning to his old hideout to reflect) and becomes the new master of the Genie. At this point, he uses his first two wishes to become Sultan and the most powerful sorcerer in the world, thus banishing Aladdin and Abu to a frozen wasteland at the edge of the earth, and threatens to kill Dalia and the Sultan unless Jasmine agrees to marry him. However, the Genie sends the carpet to retrieve Aladdin.
As the wedding ceremony between Jafar and Jasmine proceeds, the latter, before saying "Yes. He sees from afar that Aladdin is returning to the palace, so with deception, he manages to steal the lamp from Jafar and escape on the magic carpet with Aladdin, but the Vizier does not want to surrender.
After a brief chase, Iago, transformed into a large bird by Jafar's magic, once again steals the lamp, but then loses it when the Sultan arrives. But Jafar, through a new spell, defeats the heroes, destroying the carpet. However, Aladdin, having realized that the evil sorcerer's weakness is his unbridled thirst for power, mocks him, making him understand that, even though he is now the Sultan and the most powerful sorcerer in the world, he is still inferior to the Genie, the most powerful being in the Universe. At that point, blinded by greed, Jafar uses his last wish, asking the Genie to become a being even more powerful than himself, unaware that, having not specified what kind of being he wants to become, he will be chained forever to his lamp, transformed in turn into the Genie. Realizing the ruse too late, Jafar is thus defeated and is sucked into his lamp, along with Iago.
With Agrabah back to normal, the Genie sends Jafar's lamp into the Cave of Wonders and repairs the carpet. He advises Aladdin to use his third wish to regain his royal title so the law will allow him to be with Jasmine or to cancel the part of the law that requires a princess to marry a prince. The young man, however, decides to keep his promise and releases the genie. The Sultan declares that Jasmine will be the next ruler and, to appease the love of the two young people, he tells her that he could change the law to allow her to marry whoever she wants. The Genie sets off to explore the world as a sailor together with Dalia (with whom he will have two children), while Jasmine reaches Aladdin (who was trying to get away so as not to be seen again) and the two exchange a kiss. After a while, they get married and start their new life together.
story_text_b:
On a fishing boat, a fisherman decides to tell his children the story of "Aladdin, Princess Jasmine and the Magic Lamp" as they travel to the kingdom of Agrabah.
Aladdin (Mena Massoud) is a kind-hearted young thief who lives in the Arab city of Agrabah with his pet monkey Abu. One day he rescues and befriends Princess Jasmine (Naomi Scott), who has snuck out of the palace to explore the city, tired of her over-protected life. Meanwhile, the Grand Vizier, Jafar (Marwan Kenzari), is planning to overthrow Jasmine's father (Navid Negahban) as the Sultan. He and his pet red macaw, Iago, search for a magical oil lamp hidden in the Cave of Wonders that will grant him his wishes. However, only one person is worthy of entering: "the diamond in the rough", and Jafar decides that this is Aladdin. As night falls while trying to return to Jasmine a gold bracelet that belonged to her mother, Aladdin is quickly captured by the guards and sent to the dungeon, and subsequently, is sent to the desert to meet with Jafar, who convinces him to retrieve the lamp. Inside the cave, Aladdin finds a magic carpet and obtains the lamp. He hands it to Jafar, who betrays him and throws him back into the cave, though Abu manages to steal the lamp just in time.
Trapped in the cave, Aladdin rubs the lamp to clean a bit of the dust that falls on him and ends up accidentally and unintentionally invoking the Genie (Will Smith) of the lamp, a powerful omnipotent being who possesses different magical abilities, where also the Genie explains to him that as Aladdin was the one who summoned him from his lamp after a long time locked in it, he has the power to grant him only three wishes that he wants, however these wishes also have certain limitations and restrictions, among them: he can not make someone fall in love with a person and can not resurrect the dead. Subsequently, Aladdin with the help of his monkey Abu, manages to trick the Genie into helping them out of the Cave of Wonders without spending any of the three available wishes. After leaving the cave, Aladdin uses as his first official wish to become a prince to impress Jasmine and at the same time promises to use his third and final wish to free the Genie from the bondage of his lamp.
Aladdin enters Agrabah as the "Prince Ali of Ababwa", who arrives in an extravagant show (including Abu, whom the Genie has transformed into an elephant), but Jasmine is not impressed, believing herself to be just another suitor. The latter two are reunited when Aladdin takes her for a ride on the magic carpet to show her the world he wants to see, while the Genie dates Jasmine's maid, Dalia (Nasim Pedrad). When Jasmine deduces Aladdin's true identity, he convinces her that he is actually a prince and only dresses as a peasant to get to know the citizens firsthand. Jafar, discovers Aladdin's identity and throws him into the sea, but the Genie rescues him from drowning at the bottom of the ocean by sacrificing Aladdin's second wish. They expose Jafar, who is arrested. After the sultan offers Aladdin the position of heir, Aladdin, fearing to lose Jasmine if he reveals the truth, says he needs the Genie with him now and refuses to release him, but the Genie mentions to Aladdin that he is not being true to himself, but is letting his hunger for power cloud his judgment.
Iago helps free Jafar and he steals the magic lamp from Aladdin and becomes the new master of the Genie. Using his first two wishes, Jafar becomes Sultan and then the most powerful sorcerer in the world, trapping the guards and Jasmine's pet tiger, Rajah. He then exposes Aladdin's truth to Jasmine, then banishes him and Abu to a frozen desert. With Aladdin out of the way, Jafar threatens to kill Jasmine's father unless she agrees to marry him, but with no other alternative, Jasmine agrees on the condition that they release her father. At the ceremony, Aladdin and Abu manage to return to Agrabah after being rescued by the magic carpet, while Jasmine manages to steal Jafar's lamp. Enraged, Jafar transforms Iago into a ruc to pursue them and manages to catch them and retrieve the lamp once again.
With almost all hope lost, Aladdin begins to taunt Jafar just for being the second to be after the Genie, in such a situation, Aladdin manages to trick him so that Jafar without knowing his true intentions uses his last wish to become the most powerful Genie in the universe. However, due to the great ambiguity of the desire, the Genie is free to interpret it whenever he wishes and turns Jafar into a Genie. When the wish is granted, Jafar boasts that he is now the most powerful Genie in the universe, but realizing that Genii are not free beings as he believed, he is now doomed to remain locked in a lamp without a master and Jafar is trapped inside his magic lamp, dragging Iago with him, so that the Genie takes Jafar's lamp and banishes him to the Cave of Wonders, from which he can never come out again. With the threat over, Aladdin fulfills his promise and uses his last wish to free the genie from his lamp and turn him human, on the other hand, the sultan declares that Jasmine will be the next ruler and tells him that Aladdin is a good person and Jasmine meets him by giving him a kiss of true love.
Meanwhile, the Genie marries Dalia and goes off to explore the world with her, revealing his identity as the man from the beginning of the story.

story_text_a: Earth, in the near future. On an October night, the sky suddenly turns opaque and the stars seem to have disappeared. Humanity soon realizes that it is surrounded by a barrier, which posterity will call  Spin, outside of which time passes a hundred million times faster than on Earth. The transformation of the Sun into a red giant is only a matter of decades, condemning the planet to certain destruction. Tyler Dupree, Jason Lawton and his twin sister Diane witnessed the stars disappear. Jason will now have only one goal: to find out who built this barrier and for what purpose. A quest as blind as it is determined, in which Tyler and Diane will play a decisive role.
story_text_b:
A small community of humans and robots coexist on a daily basis on a large space station that is freely orbiting in space. In it, as in any existing community, there is always friction and therefore, the story tells how this type of situation occurs.
The timeline focuses on the era of the 1970s.

story_text_a:
In 1970, eleven-year-old Margaret Simon is informed by her parents Barbara and Herb and paternal grandmother Sylvia that the family of three is moving from New York City to a New Jersey suburb, as Herb has received a promotion. Margaret is upset about moving away from her friends and Sylvia. She soon begins to communicate with God about her concerns, anxieties, and hopes.
Upon moving to New Jersey, Margaret is quickly befriended by her neighbor and soon-to-be classmate Nancy Wheeler. She welcomes her into her friend group that also consists of two other girls, Gretchen Potter and Janie Loomis.
At the beginning of the school year, Margaret's teacher, Mr. Benedict, gives the class a year-long research assignment. When he learns Margaret dislikes religious holidays, she explains that since her mother is a Christian and her father is Jewish, her family does not observe the holidays and has left it up to Margaret to decide on her own religious identity as she grows older.
Prompted by her school assignment, Margaret asks her mother why she has never met her maternal grandparents. Barbara reveals that she is estranged from her devoutly Christian parents Paul and Mary, who disowned her upon her marriage to a Jewish man. On a weekend visit to New York City, Margaret asks Sylvia to take her to temple, which Sylvia gladly does. Meanwhile, Barbara attempts to fit in with the PTA and signs up for multiple committees, which draws her away from her hobby of painting and teaching art.
Margaret and her new friends anticipate the milestones of puberty, such as wearing a bra and having their first kisses. At classmate Norman Fischer's birthday party, Margaret enjoys her first kiss with Philip Leroy, a popular boy in her class, during a game of spin the bottle. She also attends respective church masses with Janie and Nancy. After viewing a video about menstruation at school, the girls become excited about starting their periods. Margaret grows impatient when other girls get their periods before her, including Gretchen and Nancy.
One night while out with Nancy and her family in New York City, Margaret learns Nancy lied about getting her period earlier when she actually does get her period. At school, Margaret is assigned a group project with Laura Danker, a classmate who is ostracized by her peers (including Nancy) for being taller and more developed. While working together in the library, Margaret brings up rumors about Laura letting boys "feel her up", upsetting her and causing her to storm out. Margaret feels guilty for shaming her, while questioning her friendship with Nancy.
For spring break, Margaret wants to visit Sylvia while she is vacationing in Florida, but these plans are interrupted when Paul and Mary reach out to Barbara and say they want to visit and meet Margaret. Upon learning of the cancellation, Sylvia decides to show up at the Simon house with a friend from Florida on the same day of Paul and Mary's visit.
After dinner, when Paul and Mary question Margaret about possibly attending Sunday school, Sylvia retorts that Margaret went to temple with her and has already chosen to become Jewish, sparking an argument between the parents and grandparents. Margaret yells at the adults, proclaiming that she does not care about religion and does not even believe in God.
Margaret hands in her research paper to Mr. Benedict, wherein she expresses her disillusionment with religion. Soon, she reconciles with her parents and Sylvia. At the end of the school year, Margaret thanks Mr. Benedict for being a good teacher. She also befriends Laura and asks her to dance, with Janie joining them shortly afterwards. Barbara, who has since returned to teaching painting, tells Nancy's mother Jan, the PTA president, that she will no longer volunteer for PTA committees.
Before leaving for summer camp, Margaret talks to Nancy's older brother Evan's friend Moose Freed, a neighborhood boy who mows her family's lawn and whom Margaret has a crush on, and the two agree to spend time together when she returns. At home, she discovers her first period has arrived and excitedly tells her mother, who is thrilled for her. Margaret then resumes her communication with God.
story_text_b:
Former American football champion Paul Crewe, in the midst of a self-injury crisis after the end of his career, ends up in prison for drunkenly stealing and destroying his girlfriend's expensive car. His existential crisis is due to remorse for agreeing to let go of his team for money. Knowing of his professional background, the prison director wants him to coach the sentry team, but Crewe - under pressure from Captain Knauer - refuses.
The warden's resentment of his early rejections causes his imprisonment to worsen, to the point where Paul is forced to agree to captain a tight-knit team of inmates for a match against the team of surveillance guards. The outcome of the game seems obvious: the guards have been training regularly for a long time and are in great shape, while the prisoners are rebellious and individualistic.
Paul manages, however, with a lot of effort, to create a team spirit that manifests itself during the meeting, where the prisoners put the guards in serious difficulty. The director is determined to give the guard team a clear victory, and during the break, he blackmails Paul into favoring his opponents. Without him, the prisoners have no hope: he initially suffers blackmail, then redeems himself and with a burst of pride leads his team to victory.

story_text_a:
One day, a king determines that he will be able to cope with any occurrence if he has the answers to three critical questions:
Many educated men attempted to answer the king's questions, but they all came up with different answers. The king decided that he needed to ask a wise hermit in a nearby village. The hermit would only see common folk, however, so the king disguised himself as a peasant and left his guards behind to see the hermit. The hermit was digging flower beds when the king arrived. The king asked his questions, but the hermit went on digging rather laboriously. The king offered to dig for him for a while. After digging for some time, the king again asked his questions. Before the hermit could answer, a man emerged from the woods. He was bleeding from a terrible stomach wound. The king tended to him, and they stayed the night in the hermit's hut. By the next day, the wounded man was doing better but was incredulous at the help he had received. The man confessed that he knew who the king was and that the king had executed his brother and seized his property. He had come to kill the king, but the guards wounded him in the stomach. The man pledged allegiance to the king, asked for forgiveness and  went on his way. The king asked the hermit again for his answers, and the hermit responded that he had just had his questions answered:
story_text_b:
An emperor once thought that if he knew the answer to three questions, he would always have everything under control. These were:
In order to obtain the answers, he announced that he would give a large reward to anyone who could give them; but it was in vain, since no one gave him any satisfactory ones. So the emperor decided to visit a wise hermit, who actually, instead of giving him the answers, helped the emperor find and understand them for himself.

story_text_a:
The story is set in the late 1920s to early 1930s in the city of Toledo. Tristana is a young woman who, following the death of her mother, becomes a ward of notorious nobleman don Lope Garrido. Despite his advancing age, Don Lope refuses to change his playboy lifestyle, while maintaining strong yet increasingly-antiquated attitudes about honor, chivalry, and women. Claiming to defend the weak from corrupt institutions (while expressing support for leftist politics), Don Lope nonetheless preys on his new ward, entranced by her beauty and innocence. He thus treats her as wife as well as daughter from the age of 19, unbeknownst to the outside world.
While Tristana initially accepts the arrangement, by age 21 she starts finding her voice, to demand to study music, art and other subjects with which she wishes to become independent, chafing under Don Lope, who thinks women are untrustworthy and should be kept at home. While sneaking out of the house against Lope's wishes, she meets Horacio, a young artist from Catalonia. The two fall in love and Horacio asks her to come live with him in Barcelona, but she remains apprehensive because of the Don's inescapable presence. Horacio confronts Don Lope outside his apartment, Lope slaps him and challenges him to a duel, and Hoarcio responds by simply punching him in the face. He and Tristana leave the following day.
Five years later, Tristana returns, having suddenly fallen ill. She demands to be remanded to Don Lope's house so she can die there. Tristana survives but loses a leg in the process, which changes her prospects. She breaks up with Horacio and seemingly reinstates the previous relationship with Don Lope, but is now much more independent and openly defiant. Don Lope, whose health problems have only worsened, suddenly inherits money from his sister, which Tristana covets. She agrees to have a marriage of convenience with Lope in order to, as a local priest describes, "correct a previously sinful situation," but makes it clear she has no desire for a romantic or sexual relationship, taking up the housemaid's deaf-mute son Saturno as a lover.
One night, Lope suffers a heart attack in bed. Tristana pretends to get help until he's fallen unconscious, and finishes him off by opening the window to the winter cold. The film ends with a montage of scenes playing back in reverse, ending at the moment Don Lope first seduced Tristana.
story_text_b:
Tristana, according to the last wishes of her deceased mother, is entrusted to the disgraceful guardian Don Lope, a middle-class, anti-clerical, squattrine and much older man who, conquered by the beauty of the young orphan and taking advantage of his position of power and the weakness of the girl, does not hesitate to turn her increasingly soft attentions, making her his mistress and imprisoning her in fact in a relationship that allows him to assume the role of now husband now guardian, according to convenience.
Lope falls madly in love with Tristana to whom, however, jealous of the beauty of the young companion, imposes a suffocating relationship: The honest woman stays at home all year round, plays them. Tristana develops a hidden hatred for Lope, whom she despises and would like to abandon, especially after falling in love with Horacio, a bohemian painter with whom she flees to another city. But after two years, Tristana is forced to return to her former tutor, gravely ill, tormented by a cancer that is devouring her knee: the disease will quickly worsen to the point of making amputation inevitable. Shortly before Tristana's return, Lope had inherited a large sum of money from his hated deceased sister, considered a bigot, which from now on will allow him to live comfortably.
Taking advantage of Tristana's weakness due to the illness before and the infirmity after, Lope takes with him the still beloved companion who, leaving Horacio, resigns herself to live with the elderly guardian and whom she will later marry. But the amputation changes Tristana's character, making her more and more determined to stop her husband's eager attentions, betraying him with the deaf young gardener Saturn. Lope, constantly rejected and humiliated by his wife, this time imprisoned himself in a relationship that makes him suffer every day, will soon die of a heart attack. Tristana, to her husband's desperate requests on his deathbed to call the doctor, will pretend to do so and let him die and thus be rid of him once and for all.

story_text_a: The Old Man in the film is a Cuban fisherman who has gone 84 days without a catch. His only friend is a 14-year-old boy named Manolin, who has been barred by his father from accompanying the Old Man out to sea. On the Old Man's 85th day out, he finally hooks a huge marlin, which he then tries to haul in from far out past shore. For three days and nights he battles the fish, which is portrayed in the film (as it had been in Hemingway's novella) as a trial of mental and physical courage that becomes the ultimate test for him of his worth as a man.
story_text_b: In 1951, Marcus left his native New Jersey to study at a conservative university in Ohio, where he faced sexual repression and anti-Semitism.

story_text_a: Jack Worthing (Colin Firth) has a double life: on the one hand he has a model and respectable life in the countryside with Cecily (Reese Witherspoon) and on the other lives a very different one in London, where he is an extravagant man who likes to attract attention with his friend Algy (Rupert Everett).
story_text_b:
In Iraq, a U.S. Army bomb squad, specialized in neutralizing all types of explosive devices, ventures into one of Iraq's many war-torn cities. Each of the soldiers is prepared for any type of danger situation and deals in his own way with the possible danger, stress and fear of a surprise attack, in a place where any object or vehicle could prove a threat to the American soldiers.
Sergeant Will James is the squad leader of an artillery unit, consisting of Sergeant Sanborn and Private Eldridge, which was previously commanded by his colleague Thompson, who died following the explosion of an Iraqi ordnance. The three face numerous missions and face many dangers together, united by the deep bond of soldiers in battle, sometimes even clashing with each other because of the character of James, brave but brazen and reckless of dangers, as opposed to that of the two comrades, much more cautious and rational.
A few days before his discharge, Sanborn and James rescue Eldridge from two Iraqi guerrillas who had stunned and kidnapped him, but in the rescue James accidentally injures him in the leg. The young soldier will return to the United States to receive treatment before the end of the duty shift harboring great anger towards his squad leader, guilty according to him of not having thought of the safety of his team and of having wanted to indulge his adrenaline thirst, now degenerated into madness.
Two days before the end of their shift, Sanborn and James miraculously survive the explosion of a bomb attached to an Iraqi man, and reflect on their lives and the fact that what separates life from death is an invisible thread, and that every time they go on a mission, they "roll a die and see how it ends".
Upon returning home, Sergeant James finds his wife and a few months old son, but everyday life is no longer for him: he realizes that he is unsuitable for civilian life.
The film closes with the image of James, with a seemingly contented look, preparing to defuse a bomb, in full firefighter gear, during the first of his new 365-day tour of duty in Iraq.

story_text_a: While attending Oxford University in 1914, the young American Thomas Stearns Eliot became acquainted with the aristocratic Vivienne Haigh-Wood. The two marry shortly after, but it is only in the marriage that Tom discovers his wife's dark side: Viv suffers from an extreme hormonal imbalance that causes wild mood swings and unpredictable behavior. Eliot's poetry career takes off, but Viv's behavior becomes increasingly difficult to manage, and the painful choice of institutionalization ultimately becomes the only solution.
story_text_b:
With contributions from over 50 politicians, scientists, and environmental activists, including former Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, physicist Stephen Hawking, Nobel Prize winner Wangari Maathai, journalist Armand Betscher, and Paul Hawken, the film documents the grave problems facing the planet's life systems. Global warming, deforestation, mass species extinction, and depletion of the oceans' habitats are all addressed. The film's premise is that the future of humanity is in jeopardy.
The film proposes potential solutions to these problems by calling for restorative action by the reshaping and rethinking of global human activity through technology, social responsibility and conservation.

story_text_a: Trevor is a former soldier who survived the war in Afghanistan. Because of the cruel images he has witnessed, Trevor cannot sleep and is still faced with the terror of war. When his car breaks down while traveling through Texas, he ends up with the sadistic Brodrick family. She keeps passersby and captured tourists as slaves to force them to work on her farm. A wrong question or answer is punishable by death. Trevor himself suffered severe trauma through torture and interrogation behind enemy lines. When they remind him of it, he freaks out. Trevor breaks free and takes up the fight.
story_text_b:
Miner Taura is arrested on the planet Arous (known from The Eyes of Satan, 1957) for scorching the hand of Captain Bantor with hot lava during an attack. She is sentenced to an extended stay on the prison spaceship Vehemence. It's ruled by the sadistic prison guard Exene. Bantor will also be assigned to the ship. He's there to develop a mind-control machine that turns humans into mindless zombies.
Taura gains the trust of her fellow prisoners and rebels against the sadistic guards. Together, the women manage to escape. In a space battle, they can finally defeat their former oppressors.

story_text_a:
Matt Hunter was one of the best men in the Secret Service until a bomb meant for him killed his parents. He then left the service and retired to his grandfather Jimmy's ranch to care for his younger sister, Sarah. Larry Richards, a successful black politician from New Orleans who is running for the Senate seat, is Matt Hunter's best friend. Because of his skin color and political ambitions, Richards has been targeted by Pentangle, an elite, racist fraternity of politicians and businessmen who want to get rid of him.
When Richards is attacked during Mardi Gras and his son is killed, Hunter, who happened to be visiting him at the same time, has him taken to his grandfather's farm. But the Pentangle is already lurking here, too. Members of the Association kill Richards and his entire family and kidnap Matt's sister. To save his sister, Hunter must now face a life-and-death battle in the swamps of Louisiana with the leaders of Pentangle. Little by little, Hunter finally manages to defeat the four leaders of Pentangle and rescue his sister.
story_text_b: The film tells the story of a pensioner Ivan Fёdorovič, who lives with his niece, who is raped by three young boys, after which they are arrested, but soon released. Ivan Fedorovich will do everything he can to take revenge on them.

story_text_a:
Dmitry "Dima" Maykov (Grigoriy Dobrygin) is a student at Moscow State University. For his birthday, his father (Sergei Garmash), gives him a black '66 Volga. In the glove compartment, Dima finds an old photo of three scientists and an old audio record, but he gives them no mind.
Dima is in love with his classmate Nastya Svetlova (Yekaterina Vilkova). Dima believes that the only way to her heart lies through money and status, which in turn are only attainable through ambitiousness and egoism. This belief is strengthened when Dima sees the success of Nastya's friend, Max (Ivan Zhidkov), who also happens to have a Mercedes.
Dima begins working as a flower delivery boy. During one of the runs, he gets into trouble with Kuptsov's men, and while being chased by them, accidentally engages the car's flight system. Losing control of the flying car, Dima crash lands into an abandoned building. With Max's help, Dima is able to play the record from the glove box which helps him track down two of the scientists in the photo, Pavel Perepelkin and Olga Romantseva, who turn out to be husband and wife. Dima, pretending to be a newspaper reporter, asks them about the car. The Volga is revealed to be a product of a Soviet black project, equipped with multiple rocket engines allowing supermaneuverable flight, as well as a device called "nano-catalyzer" which transmutes ordinary gasoline into high-yield nanofuel to power them. Romantsova gives Dima the car's manual, which the third scientist, Mikhail Yelizarov, wrote. At first, Dima enjoys the flights and makes decent money delivering flowers while avoiding the infamous Moscow traffic jams. But his egotism leads Dima to leave a stabbed man on the street instead of helping him, and that man later turns out to be his own father.
The death of his father changes Dima's outlook on life. He decides to use his car to help people in need. He rapidly gains many fans among the city dwellers, and newspapers grant him the nickname "Black Lightning."
Meanwhile, Kuptsov starts a hunt for the nano-catalyzer, which can produce fuel needed to power his tectonic drill concealed within one of the Moscow City skyscrapers. The drill will allow Kuptsov to reach a layer of diamonds located beneath the tectonic plate, but will likely destroy the city in the process. Kuptsov finds the scientists who worked on the flying Volga and forces them to build the same kind of flight system for his Mercedes, as well as outfit it with weaponry and armor shielding. Kuptsov lures Dima out by letting Perepelkin, one of the scientists, escape to the roof of the skyscraper. Kuptsov then ambushes "Black Lightning" with rocket fire from his Mercedes, stealing the nano-catalyzer and sending the Volga falling down, crashing into the ice and sinking to the bottom of the Moscow River.
A call from his girlfriend, Nastya, that says that she really loves him, brings the hero back to his senses. Dima remembers the emergency backup tank with 30 minutes' worth of nanofuel, bursts out from under the ice, and rushes into Kuptsov's lair, freeing the scientists and recapturing the nano-catalyzer. He then flies to pick up Nastya, but Kuptsov beats him to her, taking her as a hostage and offering to trade her for the nano-catalyzer. Dima and Kuptsov confront each other over the Red Square. Dima flashes his headlights and honks the horn in a special signal that Nastya knows about. Nastya jumps out of Kuptsov's car and Dima grabs her in midair, safely landing her to the earth below. The final battle between the flying cars in the sky above Moscow ends with Dima luring Kuptsov's car to the outer reaches of the atmosphere, where the Mercedes runs out of nanofuel. Kuptsov floats in the Earth's orbit, left for dead.
Dima and Nastya meet on the ground and celebrate the New Year together.
story_text_b:
George Armstrong Custer (Flynn) arrives at West Point in an outlandish uniform he had designed himself, which makes him appear to be a visiting foreign general. Following the misunderstanding, he signs as a cadet and begins to stack up demerits for pranks and a general disregard for rules while at the Point. When the Civil War breaks out, Custer is at the bottom of his class.
Custer is walking a silent punishment tour when he is approached by Libbie Bacon who asks him for directions. Shortly thereafter, his punishment ends, and he runs after her, explaining his rude silence, and asking if he may come to call that evening. Later, Custer and other members of his class are graduated early and ordered to report immediately to Washington, D.C., for assignment. As a result, Custer misses his appointment with Libbie.
Custer makes the acquaintance of Gen. Winfield Scott (Sydney Greenstreet), who aids him in getting placed with the 2nd U.S. Cavalry. He becomes a war hero after disregarding a superior's orders during a crucial battle, successfully defending a bridge for the Union infantry. Awarded a medal, he gets leave to return home to Monroe, Michigan. He meets Libbie at her home, but her father, who has been the butt of Custer's joke earlier that day, orders him to leave. Custer returns to his regiment. Due to a miscommunication from the Department of War, he is promoted by mistake to the rank of brigadier general and takes command of the Michigan Brigade at the Battle of Gettysburg. He wins the day, and many victories follow thereafter.
Upon returning home to Monroe as a Union war hero, Custer marries Libbie in a lavish ceremony with a full honor guard, but soon grows bored with civilian life and begins drinking too much. Libbie visits Custer's old friend Gen. Scott and begs him to assign Custer to a regiment again. He agrees, and Custer is given a lieutenant colonel's commission out west in the Dakota Territory.
When Custer and Libbie arrive at Fort Lincoln, Custer finds the soldiers a drunken, rowdy, and undisciplined lot in need of firm leadership. His old West Point enemy, Ned Sharp (Arthur Kennedy), who has a government license to run the fort's trading post and saloon, is providing Winchester repeating rifles to the local Native Americans. Furious, Custer stops the rifle sales and permanently closes the saloon. He then instills proper military discipline in his men and introduces a regimental song, "Garryowen", both of which quickly bring fame to the U.S. 7th Cavalry under Custer's command. The 7th has many engagements with Lakota tribal chief Crazy Horse (Anthony Quinn), who eventually offers peace, wanting a treaty that will protect the sacred Black Hills; Custer and Washington sign the treaty, but soon it is bankrupting Sharp's trading posts. Sharp and several others spread a rumor that large gold deposits have been discovered in the Black Hills. American settlers stream into the area in violation of the treaty, but Custer and his troops permit no infractions. To embarrass Custer, Sharp passes out free bottles of liquor to Custer's men hours before they drunkenly pass in revue, in complete disarray, before Commissioner Taipe, a politician in league with Sharp. Custer punches both Sharp and the commissioner in anger, and he is quickly relieved of his command.
On the way to Washington for his Court martial Custer hears from Libbie about attempts to start the gold rush in the Black Hills and realizes from the timing that it has been fabricated, a plan that would bring much business and large profits to a select group. Outraged, Custer takes the information to the U.S. Congress, but they only ridicule him, refusing to hear his evidence. When news arrives that the presence of gold miners has led to open conflict between the Lakota and U.S. troops, Custer appeals in person to President Ulysses S. Grant, one soldier to another, who restores him to command.
Upon returning to Fort Lincoln, Custer comes to realize that his band of cavalry are the only chance at rescuing a force of U.S. infantry from the Lakota. He also knows full well that he and his men have little chance of survival against their force. Custer has a final, emotion-filled goodbye with Libbie, after which he leads his cavalry into battle. An even greater number of Native American tribes, numbering 6000, have come together and joined the conflict. Quickly surrounded, Custer and his meagre forces are killed.
A few corrupt politicians have now goaded the western tribes into war for personal profit, threatening the survival of all white settlers in the Dakota Territories. Custer and his men have given their lives at the Battle of the Little Bighorn in order to slow the Native American advance. A letter left behind by Custer with Libbie, now considered his dying declaration, names the culprits and absolves the Native Americans of all responsibility; Custer wins his final campaign.

story_text_a:
After a three-month mission off the coast of Africa, the aircraft carrier Clemenceau returns to the arsenal at Brest. Suddenly, he is ordered to turn around and make preparations for the attack. No one knows exactly what it is. There is vague talk of a new East-West tension. Ship Lieutenant Gaillac and his Étendard IV pilots rally the aircraft carrier they had left a few hours earlier, but Majo, the burned head of the group, invokes a personal problem and misses the start. Meanwhile, aboard, the maximum alert is triggered with aircraft of nuclear weapons. Tension and nervousness mount until Ravesne, the building's commander, finally learns from his friend Bricourt what it's all about: a satellite of unknown nationality and technology has suddenly appeared in the sky and is baffling the staffs of all major nations.
This is the beginning of 48 hours of anxiety and suspense as the United States and the Soviet Union attempt to destroy the craft stationed above the aircraft carrier.
story_text_b:
The sighting of an unidentified flying object puts the French maritime unit on alert, with the dispatch of fighter planes to intercept it, a task made impossible by the strong radioactivity emitted. Involved in the operations is a national submarine equipped with missile weapons, assisted by a Soviet counterpart named космос (Cosmo).
Overcoming the skepticism about the alien origin, hypothesis endorsed by a pilot tested in a previous mission, it will be possible to avoid the danger of the alien mothership, equipped with a superior and unknown technology, from which disc-shaped objects were leaking that countered the Earth forces.

story_text_a:
Amidst a storm, Captain John Finnegan and his crew, Joey Pantucci, and Leila are hired by mercenaries Hanover, Mulligan, Mason, Billy, T-Ray, Mamooli, and Vivo to pilot their boat across the South China Sea to an undisclosed rendezvous point. Meanwhile, the Argonautica, a luxury cruise ship built and owned by Simon Canton, is undertaking its maiden voyage when a saboteur disables the ship's navigation and communication systems. A large object rises from beneath and rams the vessel, leaving it dead in the water, and the panicking passengers are attacked and slaughtered by unseen creatures.
Finnegan's boat collides with a speedboat shaken loose from the Argonautica (named after a Greek epic poem), during the collision, prompting Finnegan to exasperatedly ask "Now what?" (a catchphrase Finnegan repeats throughout the whole film). It is at this point that the mercenaries take over and reveal they intend to rob the Argonautica's passengers and vault, before sinking the ship with torpedoes stowed aboard the boat. The group boards the ship, leaving Leila and Billy behind to repair the boat, where they are both killed by the creatures. The group reaches the ballroom only to find blood and no sign of the passengers. Finnegan and Joey go to the ship's workshop to scavenge parts to repair the boat. Meanwhile, T-Ray goes off to investigate strange noises and is torn to shreds by the creatures. Mamooli contacts Hanover but is dragged off by the unseen creatures, forcing Finnegan and Joey to flee. They run into a woman named Trillian, a passenger who was imprisoned for stealing. Meanwhile, Hanover's group reaches the vault and Vivo opens it, only to be mistakenly killed by Canton, who was hiding inside the vault along with Captain Atherton and three other passengers. Mason and Mulligan panic and accidentally kill the passengers.
Canton and Atherton explain to the mercenaries that the ship has been attacked by unknown creatures that killed everyone else on board. Under questioning, Canton is found to be the saboteur, having hired the mercenaries to sink the unprofitable ship so that he could collect on the insurance. The group is attacked by creatures resembling giant spike-covered tentacles, which eat Atherton. Canton theorizes that the creatures are an extreme evolution of the Ottoia, which drain their victims of their bodily fluids and then eject the carcasses. The survivors flee, but Mason is grabbed by a creature and kills himself by detonating a grenade. Mulligan elects to stay behind in the crew's galley until a rescue party can arrive. While arguing with the others, as the creature slips in through the range hood; Mulligan scares it off with fire but is ambushed and devoured by another.
In a running battle, the survivors find themselves being herded towards the bow of the ship, where they find a "feeding ground" full of bloody skeletal remains. Attempting to rid himself of any witnesses to his insurance scam, Canton misleads the others to the bow while he moves towards an exit route. The creatures break through the hull, flooding the lower decks and separating the survivors. Hanover wounds Joey in an attempt to slow the creatures, but Joey escapes. Joey later finds Hanover being devoured by one of the creatures. As an act of mercy, he leaves Hanover a gun, but Hanover wastes his only shot trying to kill Joey and is consumed.
Finnegan and Trillian spot an island and return to Finnegan's boat, but—having lost the engine parts—find it useless as a means of escape. Joey returns and begins improvised repairs, and Finnegan sets the boat's autopilot to crash into the Argonautica and detonate the torpedoes. Trillian returns to the cruise ship and locates a jet ski with the fuel they can use to reach the island, but Canton arrives armed with a flare gun. Canton asks Trillian to join him or hand over the keys, but she flees and he chases her. Finnegan pursues Canton to the ballroom on the main deck, saving Trillian. The creatures smash through the main deck and are revealed to be tentacles of a vast deep-sea monster—the Octalus—rather than individual entities. The Octalus grabs hold of Finnegan, who shoots it in the eye, blinding it and freeing himself, and he and Trillian escape on a jet ski. Canton flees the Argonautica by jumping onto Finnegan's boat, but he breaks his leg doing so. Crippled, he is unable to disable the autopilot and dies as the boat crashes into the Argonautica, detonating the torpedoes and destroying both ships and the Octalus.
Finnegan and Trillian reach the island, where they find and reunite with Joey, whom they thought had died. As the three are catching their breath, a loud roar echoes from the jungle; the camera pulls back, revealing the island to have an active volcano in the distance as something big comes crashing through the trees towards the beach. Finnegan is then heard saying "Now what?" one last time.
story_text_b: The film tells the allegorical story of a Russian peasant, as well as his wife and their neighbor. He traces their various living conditions under tsarism, as well as under Communist rule.

story_text_a: Ivan Warding is a thief who specializes in stealing art from the elite of Los Angeles.  He is obliged to a crime boss and wants to get out of the art heist business.  Elyse Tibaldi is an in-debt aspiring actress who is also a con-woman.  Together they plot one last heist and con that will set both free from their obligations.
story_text_b: In Los Angeles, Ivan Warding, on behalf of a dealer, steals art from the homes of the wealthy. He sneaks into their parties and meets Elyse Tibaldi. Together, they take revenge on the dealer who tried to kill Ivan.

story_text_a: In 1880, rancher Pop Jones, along with his daughter Sierra Nevada and cowboy Nat Collins, drove his huge herd of cattle from Texas to new pastures in Montana. On their way north, they're ambushed by Indians and Pop is killed. Sierra and cowboy Nat come to a village of Blackfoot Indians. But the chief of Colorado lets the two whites go free. The peaceful leader of the Blackfoot is convinced of the peaceful coexistence of Indians and whites. Sierra can make her way back to her late father's new pastures. There, however, she learns that wealthy rancher Tom McCord has illegally taken over the land. But Sierra can't prove that she's the rightful heir to the land. But cowboy Farrell comes to her rescue. Farrell's working undercover as a cowboy for McCord, but he's investigating McCord.
story_text_b: The first human mission is about to land on Mars but something goes wrong: the lander crashes on the ground, while the crew members are saved by a miracle. The situation is dramatic, the resources are barely enough for two people waiting for a rescue ship to arrive, so the commander decides that those who are not of vital importance, including him, will go for a walk. The end of the walk will lead them to an incredible discovery.

story_text_a:
Hilary O'Neil (Julia Roberts), who comes from a poor background, is hired to care for a wealthy young man, Victor Gaddes (Campbell Scott), who is suffering from cancer. She moves into a one-bedroom apartment in Victor's mansion in an upscale neighborhood of San Francisco. At first, she is often overwhelmed by work, studying the disease in public libraries.
Hilary becomes a friend and companion to Victor, whose father spends most of his time away on business. The two of them rent a cottage and become a couple. Suddenly, Victor's condition deteriorates drastically, which he initially tries to hide from Hilary, but fails. She discovers Victor's empty syringes for pain and confronts him with having lied to her, as he had previously claimed not to need such medication.
Victor confesses to her that he stopped chemotherapy prematurely so he could live alone with her. Hilary, who realizes that everything she experienced at the cottage was based on a lie (including her love for Victor), breaks down in tears and explains to him that they must return immediately because she could not watch him die before her eyes. Then she calls Victor's father and asks him to pick up his son, no matter what he does.
Victor asks his father to allow him to go to a Christmas party that he and Hilary have been invited to by a friend before their departure, which he assures him. Mr. Gaddes will let him.
At the party, Victor has to witness Hilary lying in the arms of said friend, which breaks his heart. He drives back to the cottage and packs his things to sneak out, only to be caught by Hilary.
She begs him not to give up yet and at the same time promises to accompany him to the bitter end because she loves him. Victor agrees.
The next morning, Hilary and Victor go back to the clinic. Whether Victor recovers or dies remains open.
story_text_b: Hillary O'Neil is a 23-year-old young woman, very beautiful, ambitious but unemployed. She just broke up with her boyfriend who cheated on her. Looking for a job, she responded to a small ad in the newspaper for a job at the home of a person requiring a little experience as a nurse. Going to the address, she entered the home of a very wealthy businessman seeking permanent help for his 28-year-old son, who had been suffering from leukemia for more than a decade. The father refuses the job to the young woman, estimating that she lacks the necessary experience and that she has no recommendations. But the son, Victor, immediately recalls her from the street by his butler as she returns home, immediately reveals her illness, and decides to offer her the job without hiding from her that she will necessarily have to experience extremely trying times in her supporting role, especially during the terrible side effects of chemotherapy. Then begins a poignant story in which the young woman's feelings progress from compassion to a true deep love shared between her and the young man.

story_text_a: Hercule Poirot and Captain Hastings have barely found each other when they are confronted by an international criminal organization, called  the Four. Number one is the Chinese Li Chang Yen, number two a wealthy American, number three a French woman; of number four, only the nickname is known:  the Destroyer. It is in the course of various investigations, in which the sign of the Four appears, that Poirot manages to understand the workings of his opponents. To thwart the plot, he will have to make great sacrifices. However, he will succeed in unraveling this mysterious story.
story_text_b:
This time the opponents of the famous Belgian detective Hercule Poirot are not ordinary murderers or common criminals, but even an organization headed by the four greatest criminal minds in the world. Led by a diabolical and enigmatic Chinese mandarin, they want to take over the world using powerful means of destruction. Helping the investigator is not only his loyal friend and companion Captain Arthur Hastings, but also a twin brother unknown to all. The novel consists of a series of episodes that see Poirot facing and solving from time to time different criminal puzzles, until the final clash against the four bosses.
The conclusion of the novel is set in the "Labyrinth", at the foot of the Latemar Dolomite group in Trentino-Alto Adige.

story_text_a:
After separating from his wife Véronique, the Parisian illustrator Robert moves back to Vichy. There he lives in an anonymous development. He's very reserved with his colleagues. In the evenings, he observes the young Juliette, who spends her holidays in the house of her aunt-in-law. When Robert decides to reveal himself to Juliette, she discovers a passion for him that is not familiar to him. He doesn't want to get involved with the woman of his dreams.
Meanwhile, Juliette rejects her plan to marry Patrick, a research pharmaceutical representative who travels frequently. Patrick doesn't want to accept Juliette's decision. Furious, he fights for her and challenges Robert, whom he suspects to be responsible for the breakup. In the process, he escalates into increasingly savage threats until the conflict finally escalates. He's on the phone with Véronique, who advises him to use physical force. He then cuts off Robert, who is on his way to Juliette's house, and hits him with his car. During the fight, Patrick falls into a river, from which Robert pulls him out. Patrick now devises a plan of revenge: he hides in a Paris hotel to expose Robert to suspicion of his murder; he is supported by Robert's intriguing ex-wife Véronique, who considers this a game and a belated revenge on Robert.
With the police, Robert is becoming increasingly suspicious, especially as intimacy from his failed marriage and the closer circumstances of getting to know him and Juliette come to light. Even when Robert is shot one night in his home, it does little to change the Commissioner's attitude at first. Robert is further targeted when Juliette commits suicide out of despair over unrequited love and against the backdrop of her special relationship with death. Finally, Robert is shot in Patrick's arm in the second attack and ends up with the old doctor who has been called to his aid. When Patrick launches a third attack on Robert there, the doctor crashes heavily and falls into a coma in the hospital.
Meanwhile, Véronique's partner Marcello, who can no longer bear to watch the atrocities, has betrayed Patrick's hiding place in a Paris hotel to Robert. Robert immediately notifies the police, but they seem to take no action. Eventually, Patrick surrenders to the police without confessing. Soon after his arrest, he's on the loose again thanks to his father's connections. In his distress, he seeks out Véronique, from whom he hopes for help, but she asks him to keep her out of the police, and incites him in a treacherous game to an ultimate revenge.
Together, they drive to Robert's, Patrick smashes his dishes, and they provoke him. The situation escalates when Robert receives a phone call informing him of the doctor's death. When Patrick realizes he's a murderer, he completely loses control and attacks Robert with a knife. Robert is able to repel him and Véronique tries to take the knife from Patrick, but is fatally wounded in the neck.
At the end you see Robert's bloodstained hand reaching for the knife that Patrick had in his hand, telling himself "Don't touch!"
story_text_b:
The saga, said to have taken place around the introduction of Christianity in Iceland, tells the story of two Icelandic poets, Gunnlaugr Ormstunga and Hrafn Önundarson, and their love of Helga the Fair, granddaughter of Egill Skallagrímsson, which results in a competition leading to a deadly duel of honor.
The story opens with a prophetic dream of two eagles who fight over a swan before killing each other. A hawk then arrives to comfort the swan, foreshadowing the rest of the saga and the love triangle element of the story.
The saga then transitions to Gunnlaugr and his upbringing.  After Gunnlaugr has an altercation with his father, Illugi the Black, Gunnlaugr rides away to Borg where he meets a farmer, Thorstein, son of Egil Skallagrímsson. Gunnlaugr accepts Thorstein's gracious invitation to stay with him, and he spends a year there studying law. During this year, Gunnlaugr and Helga, Thorstein's daughter, begin a friendship which culminates in them taking a liking for one another. Gunnlaugr then decides to travel abroad, but first asks Thorstein for Helga's hand in marriage—a customary practice in that day. Thorstein quickly rejects Gunnlaugr's proposal because of his decision to travel abroad, but after he and Illugi discuss the matter further they agree that if Gunnlaugr returns in 3 years he can have Helga as his wife.
Despite his feelings for Helga, Gunnlaugr travels to the courts of Northern kings to recite his poetry. He first visits Norway and earl Eric Haakonsson, where his initial poem is received indifferently. Gunnlaugr eventually is banished from the country after Gunnlaugr replies to the Earl's followers with disrespect, further cementing his nickname of "Serpent-Tongue". Gunnlaugr quickly leaves Norway and heads to England, where King Æthelred rewards Gunnlaugr handsomely for his poem with a cloak of scarlet and requests that he return next autumn. After this, Gunnlaugr travels to Ireland and the court of Sigtrygg Silkbeard. The king has no idea what the proper reward for a poem is, and initially offers a lavish prize before he is counseled to give a more reasonable gift of scarlet clothes, an embroidered tunic, a cloak lined with exquisite furs, and a gold bracelet. Next to be visited is the Orkneys, where Gunnlaugr receives an axe from Earl Sigurd Hlodvirsson. After this comes Sweden, where Gunnlaugr recites a poem in praise of the Norwegian earl Eiríkr, who finally appreciates Gunnlaugr's verses.
To cement his relationship with Æthelred Gunnlaugr returns to England. He is delayed for the winter before heading to Sweden to visit King Óláfr Skötkonung. Here Gunnlaugr meets Hrafn Önundarson—the antagonist of the saga.  Each of them recites a poem for the king. and is told to discuss the other's poem. They both respond by making back-handed comments, resulting in a falling out. Hrafn then returns to Iceland, where he discusses with Skafti the Lawspeaker the possibility of asking Thorstein for Helga's hand in marriage. Skafti references the agreement between Gunnlaugr and Thorstein previously made, but Hrafn ignores the objection and says that Gunnlaug is so proud these days that he "won’t take any notice of this or care about it at all". After Hrafn and Skafti discuss the issue with Illugi and Thorstein, they agree that if Gunnlaugr breaks his vow of returning after three years to claim his wife, Hrafn then has permission to marry Helga.
The story then transitions back to Gunnlaugr and his adventures abroad, where he fulfills his oath to King Æthelred and returns to England.
