At the king's insistence, Gunnlaugr stays an extra summer in England, which ultimately causes his original agreement with Thorstein to be void. Gunnlaugr returns to Iceland too late to stop the marriage, and consequently Gunnlaugr and Hrafn become embroiled in a bitter rivalry. It is apparent throughout the wedding that Helga still possesses feelings for Gunnlaugr. After the ceremony, Gunnlaugr approaches Helga and they talk for a while. Their talk concludes with Gunnlaugr giving the cloak King Æthelred gave to him to his beloved Helga.
With Gunnlaugr returning to Iceland, Helga loses all interest in Hrafn, causing him increasing disdain for the tragic hero. They first compete in verse and later in battle. After their first altercation ends anticlimactically, Hrafn and Gunnlaugr agree to travel to Norway to end their dispute once and for all. Dueling became outlawed after their first physical altercation. Their feud in Norway continues, with Gunnlaugr cutting off Hrafn's leg. Hrafn, in one final act of spite, tricks Gunnlaugr into lowering his guard and mortally wounds Gunnlaugr before he is ultimately defeated. Gunnlaugr dies a short time later and Helga is married off to another poet named Thorkel, fulfilling the prophecy. Helga dies a little later, gazing at the cloak that Gunnlaugr gave her.

story_text_a:
In 1900, a couple is murdered in Paris. The masked killer had a metal hand and ripped the couple's heart out. The murder was witnessed by Sonja, the couple's daughter, who was in hiding.
Twelve years later, a new wax museum opens in Rome. The main attractions are depictions of historical murders that are designed to look realistic. A young man is supposed to spend the night there as part of a bet, but is found dead in the museum the next morning. The cause of death is believed to have been a heart attack, and rumor has it that he was frightened to death.
The same day, Sonia applied for a job as a costume designer at the museum and was hired directly by Boris Volkoff, the director of the museum, much to the surprise of his assistant Alex. As she leaves the museum, she meets Andrea, a journalist who wants to investigate the death of the young man. He suspects there's something strange going on in the museum. Sonia also notes that her own story and that of the museum seem to be connected. As more and more people disappear around the museum, the two bond. You suspect Boris Volkoff is behind this, waxing these real corpses to make them look more alive.
Through her blind aunt, Sonia finds out that Boris Volkoff is Sonia's father. He was obsessed with creating living wax figures as early as 1900, and neglected his marriage, so that Sonia's mother obtained a lover. He surprised and murdered the couple in 1900. Subsequently, his laboratory caught fire and he was presumed dead. Sonia wants to bring him to justice, but she's kidnapped instead. Boris reveals that he covers his burned face and hand with real skin to hide his scars. She must also discover that the wax figures are actually still living people, kept alive artificially with chemicals but unable to move.
Andrea rescues Sonia, and it's the fight that ignites the wax museum. Boris attacks the two, but is apparently killed by his assistant Alex, who no longer wants to participate in his treacherous plans. While Sonia and Andrea escape into the open, Alex sneaks into the basement. He peels off his skin, revealing a metal skeleton beneath it. Looks like Boris traded skin with his assistant. He changes his skin and becomes Boris again. Undetected, he leaves the museum and disappears into the crowd.
story_text_b:
Thomas Abernathy has been commissioned by Filadyne to carry out experiments aimed at improving energy supplies. He wants to create a black hole. Trained as a physicist, Eva Soderstrom works on the Abernathy team and has a relationship with her colleague Steven Price.
Soderstrom's father died a few years earlier in a similar attempt. She's convinced the experiment is dangerous. Soderstrom is trying to stop Abernathy.

story_text_a:
Professional bull rider Luke Collins meets Sophia Danko, an art student at Wake Forest University, after she attends a PBR event. On the way home from their first date, they spot a car crash in the woods and help rescue an elderly man from the vehicle, along with a box full of letters.
In the hospital, Sophia visits the 91-year old man she rescued, Ira Levinson. He explains the letters are what he wrote as a teenager to his late wife, Ruth, and she offers to read them to him, which tell the story of how they met and fell in love in 1940.
In flashbacks, Ruth tells a young Ira that she wants a big family, and he eventually proposes to her before leaving to fight in World War II. However, Ira is shot during an attack and is later informed that he can no longer have children, news that causes distance between Ruth and him when he returns. Regardless, they decide to make it work and move in together, decorating the house with many paintings that Ruth and he love.
Back in the present day, Ira is moved to a nursing home where Sophia continues to visit. Luke continues bull riding as Sophia and he fall in love. He attends an art exhibit with her, which he finds uninteresting, and they realize how different their two worlds are; Luke says he does not feel their relationship will work.
Sophia goes to Ira for advice, who tells her how he and Ruth made it work. In flashbacks, it is revealed that Ruth, a school teacher, became attached to a young student named Daniel McDonald after finding out she and Ira wouldn't have children of their own. They wanted to adopt him but Daniel's uncaring relatives wouldn't allow it.
Luke is injured while riding and is rushed to hospital. He is advised not to ride again but he refuses to accept that his career is over. Following an argument, Luke and Sophia break up. In flashbacks, Ira and Ruth break up because she cannot see a life without children in their future. However, weeks later, Ruth returns as she cannot live without Ira. Decades later, now 80 years old, Ira wakes up to find Ruth has died in her sleep.
One night, a woman knocks on his door, claiming to be the wife of Daniel McDonald, the child they almost adopted when they were younger, and informs Ira that Daniel, who later became a professor of physics and astronomy, has died. She gives him a portrait of Ruth that he had painted, with a message on the back that reads: "Ruth Levinson, third grade teacher. She told me I could be anything I wanted to be when I grew up".
Sophia and Luke are contacted by Ira's attorney who tells them that he has died and an auction will be held for his collection of paintings. Meanwhile, Luke wins his last ride, and the event championship, but feels disappointed because Sophia is not there to share it with him.
Going to the auction, Luke buys the first piece of art, a simple painting by Daniel "Portrait of Ruth". He and Sophia reconcile with a kiss after he tells her he will not ride anymore because what he really wants is to be with her for the rest of his life. The auctioneer then reveals Ira's clause in the auction rules was: whoever buys Daniel's portrait will receive the entire collection, worth almost $200 million, as it is the piece of art that meant the most to him.
A year later, Luke and Sophia, now married, have built an art gallery dedicated to Ira and Ruth and their paintings. He takes her to Black Mountain College where Ira and Ruth used to spend their wedding anniversary. They sit under the same tree and read Ira's letters together.
story_text_b:
Luke Collins is a North Carolina bull rider who is seriously injured during a race.
Returning to the competition after more than a year, he accidentally meets Sophia Danko, an art history student from New Jersey with whom he immediately has a special attraction. She's about to graduate and already has professional contacts that could lead to her moving to New York soon. The prospect of having to separate within a few months ruins the good atmosphere that had been created on their first date, in which both had already understood that a lasting relationship could be born. That same evening, while escorting Sophia home, Luke runs into an elderly gentleman who crashed his car, taking him to safety. Sophia rescues from the burning car a box that turns out to be very valuable to the man: it contains the correspondence of a life with his wife, who died a few years ago. Sophia soon becomes attached to elder Ira, a Jewish gentleman who visits regularly, and to whom she reads the letters she wrote to her Ruth, thus tracing a long love affair that began in 1940.
Thanks to Ira, Luke and Sophia, who haven't seen each other since that date, are getting closer by getting together. The differences between the two seem to create the conditions for a shaky union but Ira's deep feeling and stories convince the girl to put aside the misunderstandings. Luke, meanwhile, has a new accident during a rodeo that warns him that his health could be seriously compromised by further trauma. The obstinacy to continue against the opinion of the doctors, as well as the will of the mother and her own, convince Sophia to leave him.
Ira dies and his attorney separately summons Sophia and Luke to the auction of Ruth and Ira Levinson's art collection, held in accordance with the deceased's will. Ruth was a great art enthusiast and from a young age, with great flair, had bought works by emerging artists with the consent of her husband who also did not have the same sensitivity. The two, because of Ira's war wound, knew they could never have children, but they remained united. Actually with a little crisis, when Ruth, after raising for months little Daniel McDonald, her gifted but neglected and parentless pupil, was forced to leave him to his estranged relatives. A foolish thing for her to do, which resulted in an estrangement even from Ira, then returned. With Ruth already gone, Ira learned from Daniel McDonald's widow that he had become a professor of astronomy and physics, and that he owed everything to his teacher to whom he dedicated a portrait that Ira accepted as a gift, moved.
So in an auction full of museum pieces, the very first painting to be sold is Ruth's portrait, which is almost worthless. Luke, present without Sophia's knowledge, wins it in the general indifference. While finalizing the purchase, Luke explains to Sophia that he has retired from competition, having "tamed" the bull that nearly killed him the previous year. She hugs him back and then they both learn that by Ira's will the auction has ended with the purchase of the first painting. In fact, Ira had decided that whoever bought that painting would take possession of the entire collection.
With this unexpected fortune Luke can keep the ranch and Sophia can stay in North Carolina where she will run the prestigious gallery-museum dedicated to the two benefactors whose great love is also a role model for the two young people who can now only be optimistic.

story_text_a:
A group of scientists finds a wreckage of an old aircraft in the ice of the North Pole. Two explorers manage to penetrate the carcass and find a mysterious blue, white and red circular object.
In 1942, in Norway, Johann Schmidt, head of Hydra (a secret Nazi scientific division), breaks into a castle to take possession of the Tesseract, a powerful artifact created by the ancient Norse gods. Meanwhile, in New York, Steve Rogers, a frail and frail young man, attempts to enlist in the army, but is rejected because of his physical defects. One night, Steve visits the Stark Expo with his best friend, Sergeant James "Bucky" Barnes. Abraham Erskine, a German-born scientist working for the government, is impressed by Rogers' patriotic motivations and decides to enlist him. The young man is thus transferred to a special section of the army, under the command of Colonel Chester Phillips and Agent Peggy Carter. In this ward, a recruit will be selected, on whom the super-soldier serum will be tested. Erskine chooses Rogers because of his loyal, fair, and selfless nature, revealing to the young man that the serum had been administered to Schmidt himself, causing him severe collateral damage.
Meanwhile, Schmidt, intent on conquering the entire world, uses the Tesseract to power the innovative weapons designed by Arnim Zola. Rogers and Agent Carter travel to Erskine's secret laboratory, which is aided by Howard Stark, a wealthy inventor and weapons manufacturer. Rogers is injected with the super soldier serum, causing him to grow much taller and develop his muscles incredibly. However, an undercover Hydra agent kills Erskine and escapes with the last remaining vial of the serum. Rogers pursues and captures Kruger, who kills himself with cyanide. The last vial of the serum was destroyed in the fight, and with Dr. Erskine dead, it can't be replicated. So Rogers is the world's only super soldier, too valuable to be exposed in battle. Becoming a popular phenomenon after the city chase, he is promoted to the rank of captain and participates in various shows and performances, during which he is nicknamed Captain America.
In November 1943, in Italy, Rogers learns that an entire division of the army has been taken prisoner by Hydra; among the captured soldiers is Bucky. Despite Colonel Phillips believing a rescue mission inappropriate, Rogers decides to personally go to the rescue of his friend, aided by Peggy and Stark. After flying over enemy defenses, Rogers parachuted alone and managed to penetrate the Hydra base. Here he frees Bucky and the other soldiers, who take down the Nazi base with the help of Tesseract-powered weapons stolen from the Germans. Rogers and Bucky have a face-to-face encounter with Schmidt, who turns out to be Red Skull, so named for the terrible face he used to hide behind a mask. Red Skull and Zola escape with the Tesseract and American soldiers raze the base to the ground.
Back at camp, Rogers is rewarded by Phillips with a new suit and a shield made of indestructible vibranium provided by Stark, and continues to fight the Hydra, flanked by an army of loyal fighters, destroying all enemy bases one by one. During a raid on a Hydra armored train, Steve and Bucky manage to capture Zola, but Bucky falls off a cliff. Phillips extracts from Zola the location of Hydra's last base, which is located in the Alps and is attacked with all available forces. Red Skull manages to take off aboard a Flying Wing, but is caught by Captain America. Red Skull intends to bomb the major U.S. cities, but the captain reaches the cockpit and fights with Schmidt. Eventually Red Skull grabs the Tesseract, being sucked into it and disappearing into thin air. Rogers realizes that the controls are jammed to New York, deciding to sacrifice himself to avoid catastrophe. Last words with beloved Peggy, the captain crashes in the Arctic.
After a long search, Howard Stark retrieves the Tesseract from the bottom of the ocean, but finds no trace of Captain America, who remains so hibernated in the ice for almost seventy years, until his discovery. Waking up in a hospital in present-day New York, the captain escapes through the streets, but is caught by Nick Fury, who provides him with explanations. Eventually, Rogers is intent on training in a gym when he is joined by Fury, who proposes a mission to save the world from a new threat.
story_text_b:
Set in the universe of The Hunger Games, 64 years before the first installment, the book follows young Coriolanus Snow, who is far from the cold, calculating dictator seen during the events of the original trilogy.
Following a long and costly war with the Districts, in which the Capitol was under direct siege for several months, the Capitol remains heavily damaged and is only beginning to recover after victory. The once-wealthy and powerful Snow family has fallen on hard times, mainly due to their munitions factory in District 13 being destroyed. The family patriarch, General Crassus Xanthos Snow, led the Capitol's forces as a key strategist and war hero until he was killed in action. While determined to keep up appearances, 18-year-old Coriolanus Snow, his cousin Tigris Snow and their paternal grandmother (nicknamed "Grandma’am") are running out of options and resources. Faced with the imminent loss of both their grand apartment and the family's great social prestige, Coriolanus remains determined to restore his family to prosperity, taking pride and assurance in the family saying, "Snow Lands On Top."
Based on his academic excellence at the Academy, the Capitol's most prestigious high school, Coriolanus is chosen to mentor a tribute in the upcoming tenth Hunger Games. This will mark the first time the Games have mentors, and the first time there will be tribute interviews and a host, Lucky Flickerman. Coriolanus is assigned the District 12 female tribute, Lucy Gray Baird. She is a member of a traveling musician group/family known as the Covey, who were forced into settling in District 12 once the war began. Lucy Gray sparks the Capitol's attention after singing during the reaping, as well as slipping a hidden snake into the clothing of the mayor's cruel daughter Mayfair, who had arranged for her to be reaped over jealousy about a boy named Billy Taupe. Coriolanus is determined to make a good impression, since his success in the games will most likely guarantee he will win the monetary prize he needs in order to save his apartment and attend University.
Coriolanus decides to meet Lucy Gray at the train station where the tributes are set to arrive, but accidentally ends up locked with them in their transport vehicle. Some of the tributes consider killing him, but are dissuaded by Lucy Gray when she warns them that their families would likely be punished. The transport vehicle drops a stunned Coriolanus and the tributes inside a cage in the Capitol Zoo. He and Lucy Gray seize the opportunity to put on a show and continue earning the sympathy of the Capitol's citizens.
Coriolanus starts gifting Lucy Gray food, since the Capitol is not feeding the tributes, often giving her his only meal for the day. The other mentors follow suit, including Sejanus Plinth, the only child of Strabo Plinth, whose ingenuity constructing a munitions empire in District 2 brought him considerable wealth and political favor, allowing him to buy his family's way into the Capitol after the war. Sejanus gets nowhere trying to use food to build a rapport with his tribute, Marcus, a former classmate of his from District 2. Another mentor, Arachne Crane, mocks and taunts her tribute, leading to her being attacked and killed when she gets too close to the cage bars. The tribute, Brandy, is then shot by the Peacekeepers, and her body is hanged and paraded during Arachne's funeral procession.
Clemensia Dovecote, Coriolanus's classmate, is distraught by the murder, leaving him to complete an essay on ways to increase viewership for the games – which they were supposed to do together – by himself. He presents the essay to the Head Gamemaker, Dr. Volumnia Gaul, proposing a betting scheme and sponsorship of the tributes to engage the people of the Capitol in the outcome of the Games. Dr. Gaul drops the essay into a tank of genetically modified snakes. Coriolanus is forced to retrieve a few pages of the essay from the enclosure and is ignored by the snakes. However, they attack Clemensia when she reaches in, since they did not recognize her scent in the paper, thus proving that Coriolanus was the sole author. Clemensia is severely envenomated and hospitalized, though Gaul brushes this off, only concerned with learning what she had wanted to. Clemensia survives, but with severe mental and physical side effects, and the true cause of her condition is hidden from her family and friends, who are simply told she was ill.
Coriolanus and Lucy Gray start getting close, after bonding over their respective struggles growing up. During a tour of the arena – implied to be a former football stadium – undetected rebel bombs explode and kill several tributes and mentors. Lucy Gray considers escaping in the chaos, but decides to help an injured Snow, saving his life. They share a kiss the last time the mentors get to see their tributes. Despite the bad publicity generated from the various Capitol deaths, the Games begin, with many tributes quickly dying from starvation, disease, or injuries, including Sejanus' tribute, Marcus, who tried to escape when the bombs went off and was punished by being beaten, chained in the arena and left to be killed by the other tributes. Meanwhile, Dr. Gaul enacts Coriolanus's proposals for the Games, successfully increasing Capitol viewership. Sejanus, resentful of both the Capitol and the Games, enters the Arena at night intending to die as a martyr; Dr. Gaul orders Coriolanus to extract him. He convinces Sejanus, explaining his death would be meaningless and he could do more to help if he lives. As they leave, they are attacked by a group of tributes who had noticed them. In the ensuing chase, Coriolanus is forced to bludgeon one of the tributes to death in self-defense. The footage of the Games is altered to hide their presence in the arena.
While in Dr. Gaul's lab, Coriolanus notices a tank of the same genetically modified snakes he and Clemensia encountered being transported. Deducing that they are going to be released in the Games, he drops a handkerchief with Lucy Gray's scent inside the tank to accustom them to her. As Coriolanus predicted, the genetically modified snakes are sent into the arena. They attack and kill several tributes but not Lucy Gray, merely surrounding her and climbing inside her dress, but not biting. After several days, Lucy Gray wins the Games thanks to the snakes and a compact Coriolanus had given her earlier that belonged to his late mother, which she filled with rat poison. At a celebration party at the Academy, Coriolanus is smugly confronted by the academic dean, Casca Highbottom, with evidence implicating him in cheating in the Games and stealing food from the Academy. Dean Highbottom is credited as the intellectual author of the Games, but is now heavily addicted to a drug called morphling, and has always hated Coriolanus. Threatened with being publicly disgraced, Coriolanus reluctantly joins the Peacekeepers and is sent to the garrison in District 12.
Coriolanus reunites with Lucy Gray in District 12, and they continue their romantic relationship. Sejanus, who was forced into the Peacekeepers due to trouble of his own, has grown further opposed to the Capitol's authoritarianism and soon plans to help a group of rebels escape to a place north of the district, rumored to be beyond the Capitol's control. Coriolanus surreptitiously sends word to Dr. Gaul using a jabberjay, a genetically modified bird capable of recording and replaying human voices. Lucy Gray's former lover, Billy Taupe, and Mayfair overhear a conversation between Sejanus and a rebel named Spruce, and are subsequently shot dead by Spruce and Coriolanus (who stumbled upon the meeting with Lucy Gray) to prevent them from blowing their cover. A few days later, Spruce is found severely injured and eventually dies, while Sejanus is arrested because of Coriolanus' recording and hanged for treason. Lucy Gray tells Coriolanus that she is going to escape to the North and he decides to leave with her, despite being offered a spot in officer training school in District 2, because he fears being found out for Billy and Mayfair's murders and hanged like Sejanus.
On their way to the North, Coriolanus accidentally finds the hidden guns used to shoot Billy Taupe and Mayfair. Coriolanus realizes that with the evidence in hand, he could bury what had happened and make a new life for himself. Worried that Lucy Gray had discerned that he was responsible for Sejanus's death after he made an incriminating comment, Coriolanus goes after her with a rifle. He is bitten by a snake and, after expending his ammunition and hyperventilating due to the bite, is unable to discern whether he killed her or she managed to get away. After dumping the incriminating weapons into a lake, Coriolanus returns to the base and is sent back to the Capitol, where Dr. Gaul explains that she had arranged for him to be sent to District 12 so he could obtain more experience and ultimately come to terms with her view of human nature as inherently violent, and the need for an authoritarian government to keep this nature in check. Coriolanus is given a spot at the University under her tutelage and is effectively adopted by Sejanus's parents as their heir, with neither knowing the central role he played in their son's death.
Coriolanus pays a visit to Dean Highbottom at the Academy. There he learns that, while Highbottom did indeed come up with the Hunger Games, he never intended for them to become a reality. While he and Crassus Snow were classmates and friends at the University, they got drunk one night and Highbottom told Crassus of his idea for the Games, but as a simple, theoretical experiment. Seeking to gain favor, Crassus took the idea and submitted it to Dr. Gaul, who made the Games a reality after the war. Highbottom never forgave Crassus for this and adds that he sees much of Crassus' deceitful, manipulative nature in his son. Thoroughly tired of Highbottom's obstructive actions and antagonism towards him, Coriolanus slips rat poison into Highbottom's drug stash, marking the first of the trademark killings that would fuel his rise to power. In the meantime, Coriolanus implements many of his ideas into future Hunger Games as a Gamemaker. All footage from the 10th Hunger Games is permanently erased and, having either died or successfully escaped the country of Panem, Lucy Gray is never seen or heard from again.

story_text_a:
The film tells the story of two people against the backdrop of the public unrest that followed the 2007/2008 Kenyan presidential elections. Anne lost everything in a gang attack: her husband is dead, her son is in a coma, she was raped, and her farm, the home of her small family, was ransacked and burned to the ground. The widowed nurse tries to cope with the traumatic events and piece by piece and against all odds to rebuild her existence. She tries to forgive and is determined to give her son a new perspective.
In parallel, the film portrays a young man who was a member of the gang that night. Joseph is aware of the consequences of his action  How do you find peace as a perpetrator? Both Joseph and Anne are looking for something that only the other can give them to help them process the painful experiences of the past and look forward to the future. But which one will succeed?
story_text_b: Set in a rural Galician environment, the plot follows a French couple who settle in a small town and seek to connect with nature. However, his presence arouses hostility and violence from a couple of neighbors.[6]

story_text_a: The naughty girl Zazie (about ten years old, with a baby's head) is visiting Paris with her mother from the provinces. So that the mother can visit her lover, she leaves Zazie with her uncle for two days. Zazie desperately wants to take the subway, but to her great disappointment, it is denied. The next day, she explores Paris on her own. When her uncle's friend, the bistro owner Turandot, who is supposed to look after her, tries to recapture her, Zazie provokes a commotion by loudly accusing him of harassment. At the flea market, she is actually approached by a snotty-bearded "nice uncle" named Pedro Surplus, who promises to buy her a pair of blue jeans. Zazie rips off his pants and flees to her uncle, pursued by Trouscaillon (Pedro very similar). Then her uncle, who is driven by taxi driver Charles (who then leaves the two but annoyed by Zazies drawings), shows her the city of Paris, first the Eiffel Tower, where the two are separated by a swarm of tourists, in whose "Cityrama" bus Gabriel lands. A fierce chase unfolds with the widow Mouaque pursuing Gabriel's bus in her open car with Trouscaillon and Zazie. The climax is then a brawl in a brewery, which is broken up by police officers, led by Aroun Arachide (Pedro is also very similar). Finally, everyone is invited to the cabaret, where the uncle has a performance as a transvestite. Zazie is now so exhausted that she falls asleep. The next day, Zazie, still asleep, is returned to her mother.
story_text_b:
A ten-year-old girl named Zazie is brought to Paris by her widowed mother (who must meet her lover) and entrusted to a strange uncle, Gabriel (who makes a living as a drag queen in a nightclub), and his wife for a couple of days. Throughout the film, Zazie tries unsuccessfully to take the train station, since it is closed for a strike; in this continuous wandering, she meets the strangest characters, thus showing us a varied Paris, made of appearance and in constant transformation.
Among the various bizarre figures we meet a satyr (i.e. a pedophile) who tries to seduce Zazie, without success: the girl will take advantage of him by getting American jeans (for her a true myth) and eating potatoes and mussels in abnormal quantities, all while telling about the death of her father. She will be able to take the subway only at the end of the film (but, fate beckons, when she has fallen asleep, so she will not notice anything): to her mother's question "What have you done these days?" she answers seraphically "I have aged".

story_text_a:
Brothers Becky and Cal DeMuth are on their way to San Diego to give pregnant Becky a fresh start. On their way to California, they drive along a country road in Kansas. They stop at a creepy abandoned church because Becky is getting over the morning sickness, and from the tall grass that surrounds the area, they hear a little boy crying for help.
When they both go into the grass, they quickly lose each other. There seems to be no way out of this wide grass. Time and space seem to behave there in ways that defy logic. Voices are coming from all directions, and the place they're in right now is a different place the next second. Tobin Humboldt, the little boy who called for help, is not the only person who got lost in that grass. There's also Tobin's father, Ross, who Becky and Cal initially believe can help them, but gradually transforms into a sinister figure. They all seem to be attracted to and influenced by a black monolith that sits in the middle of the grass field. When they all meet at the monolith, Ross kills Natalie. Tobin, Becky and Cal and escaped with Becky's ex-boyfriend, who also turned up in the field, to an abandoned gas station. Because Travis and Becky seem to be getting along again, Cal dropping Travis off the roof of the gas station. Ross shows up and kills Cal. When he tries to overpower Becky, she stabs him in the eye with a pair of scissors and escapes, all the while having disturbing visions. When she wakes up, Ross has delivered her child and is feeding her his flesh. Tobin and Travis show up, and Travis finally kills Ross after Becky gouges out his other eye as well. Travis touches the monolith and leads Tobin out of the field, shakes his hand with Becky's chain and tells him to stop her from going into the field. Tobin finds himself in the church, as he leaves it he sees Cal and Becky, as at the beginning of the film, wanting to enter the field. He manages to convince her to flee in the car by showing her Becky's necklace.
story_text_b:
Becky DeMuth and her brother Cal travel to San Diego so Becky, who is six months pregnant, can give her child up for adoption. As they stop outside an old church, they hear the distressed cries of a young boy named Tobin, coming from a field of tall grass across from the church. Then they hear his mother, Natalie, begging him not to call anyone. Worried, Becky and Cal enter the field but are soon separated and discover that the distance between them is changing strangely. Increasingly panicked, they try to leave but are unable to find their way back. Night falls and Cal stumbles upon Tobin, injured and dirty, holding a dead crow, who tells him that the field cannot move dead things, before burying the crow. Becky meets Tobin's father, Ross, but they are later separated by the field. Tobin takes Cal to an ancient rock located in the field and encourages him to touch it, but they are interrupted by the screams of Becky, who is attacked by an unknown figure.
Travis, the father of Becky's child, arrives at the church looking for Becky and Cal. He finds their car parked outside the church and decides to venture into the field of tall grass, and meets Tobin who leads him to Becky's corpse. Travis, in his grief, loses sight of Tobin. At the same time, an obviously older version of Tobin arrives at the church accompanied by Natalie and Ross. Hearing Travis call Tobin, their dog, Freddy, runs into the tall grass, followed by the family. Travis hears Tobin and starts looking for him. The family panics and splits, and Ross falls on the rock and touches it as night falls. The next morning, Becky and Cal are back in the field when they hear Tobin screaming. Tobin says Freddy was killed. Knowing that the field cannot move dead things, Travis tells Becky and Cal to walk towards Tobin, and the four characters are reunited. Travis tells Becky and Cal that they've been missing for two months.
The group sees a building in the distance and decides to walk in that direction. On the way, Becky gets a call from someone who appears to be in great distress. As she walks, the grass begins to penetrate Becky's uterus and she passes out, then is awakened by Ross, who finds Tobin. The night is falling. Ross takes them to the rock where they find Natalie, panicked, who assures them that she saw Becky's body earlier in the day. She warns them not to touch the rock. Ross's behavior becomes increasingly bizarre as the other characters decide to leave. Ross wounds Travis and kills Natalie before going after the others, stating that the rock showed him the truth and the way to the exit, but that he does not want to leave the field.
Becky, Cal, Travis, and Tobin arrive at the abandoned building and, while doing some reconnaissance, Travis and Cal discover that Freddy has managed to escape through a "hole" that leads to the road. Cal, jealous, who seems to have incestuous feelings for Becky, dumps Travis as he slides off the roof. Tobin witnesses this, and flees into the field when Ross manages to access the roof of the building. Becky refuses to leave Travis and returns to the building as Cal escapes into the field. Cal is strangled to death by Ross, and it is discovered that the characters are in a time rift, haunted again and again in the field of tall grass by Ross gone mad. Travis survived the fall and started looking for Becky. They come to an agreement in the field and Becky confesses that she was going to give the baby up for adoption.
Becky is attacked by Ross but manages to escape by piercing his eye with a pair of scissors as a storm brews. Becky encounters fantastical creatures who take her to the rock, which is engraved with prophetic drawings of Becky's birth. After seeing a horrific vision under the rock, Becky calls a number on her phone, warning her past self to stop Cal from hurting Travis, then passes out. She wakes up to find Cal taking care of her and feeding her, which is revealed to be her baby. Becky slowly realizes that she's hallucinating and that "Cal" is actually Ross. Moments later, Travis stumbles across the unconscious body of Becky. Tobin finds them and they are then confronted by Ross, who fatally wounds Travis. As Ross tries to force Tobin to touch the rock, Becky attacks Ross and pierces his other eye with her necklace, before dying from her injuries. Travis kills Ross, and then realizes that the only way to understand the tall grass is to touch the rock. Travis touches the rock and sees a series of strange visions. He then grabs Tobin's hand and guides him to an exit, asking him to stop Becky and Cal from entering the tall grass.
Tobin is transported into the church while across the road, Becky and Cal are about to enter the tall grass. Tobin manages to stop them by showing Becky his necklace, which Travis had given him, thus closing the time rift. So Becky decides to keep the baby and they head back. Travis hears them leave and dies peacefully in the grass.

story_text_b:
Berlin in 1944: Three German-Americans, who have been in the German Reich since the beginning of World War II, are drafted into military service for a special task: Ferdinand Steinbichler, whose mother lives in New Orleans, came to Berlin for the 1936 Summer Olympics and got stuck there. Paul Blümel once ran a trucking company in Canada with his brother. He was surprised by the beginning of the war, when he wanted to bring his mother to the American continent. Third in line is Berliner Willi Kuhlke, who lived with his wife and father-in-law in Los Angeles until just before the war. He actually came back to Berlin to visit his sick aunt. He has never seen his son, Pietro, who was born in the meantime. Because of their knowledge of American life, the three are given the task of running the "Wheat Mouse Company". Behind the alias is nothing less than an order to land a submarine on the American coast and blow up Lockheed's airframes.

Despite the FBI's intense surveillance of the coast, stone beetles, blister beetles, and puffins are able to break through the barrier undetected and hide in Los Angeles. There, Willi sees his son Pietro for the first time and learns that his wife Anna performs as a singer with the American troops.

The police are so closely following them that they prefer to retire as seasonal workers on the ranch of George Dalton and his lovely daughter Suzy. Old Dalton finally arranges for Ferdinand Steinbichler to be drafted into the U.S. Army under his false name. Suzy Dalton arrives just in time to warn Ferdinand of the numerous leaflets the FBI has distributed in the area. So the three of them have to go underground again.
The three Germans are becoming increasingly aware that they will end up on the gallows if they are arrested as disguised civilians. Angelo Pirrone, whose daughter is now on camera in Hollywood, has the saving idea. In the film studio, he hands over to the wanted a few costumes from the fund of an anti-German film, first party uniforms with the wrong order of the badges of honor and bracelets, which they loudly criticize in front of the investigators. These reveal themselves, the three Germans flee to another room in the costume found and lock the door. When the FBI investigators finally reach their goal after breaking down the door, they are met by Steinbichler, Blümel and Kuhlke in impeccable Army uniforms, reporting properly. Instead of the dreaded death penalty, she now faces being a prisoner of war.

story_text_a:

Malony's father is dead, and his stepfather, who adopted him, has left the family. Sévérine admits to being overwhelmed by Malony's outbursts. She leaves him with the juvenile judge, who arranges for him to be placed in a home.
Years pass, and Malony is finally 15 years old. He's barely been to school in two years, and he's regularly in the police's sights. His child welfare supervisor gives up and Malony gets a new  Yann, who himself was once in prison. When Malony steals a car and endangers the public with rabies, he is sentenced by Florence Blaque to a six-month stay in a Centre éducatif fermé (CEF). This type of closed rehabilitation facility is designed to pave the way for him to return to school. Malony improves slightly and learns to write, but fails at the school performance, during which he has an uncontrollable tantrum. At CEF, he meets Tess, the daughter of a counselor. He sleeps with her, which is tantamount to rape, after which they both cry. To his mother, he can then open up on the phone and confess that he misses her. At the CEF, Malony is about to celebrate his 16th birthday.

Yann forces him to go to work, is attacked by him with scissors and beats him. For this Yann is warned by Florence Blaque. He's close to giving up, he doesn't see any progress with Malony, and he thinks the situation is hopeless. Florence Blaque is encouraging him.
It's just before Christmas when Malony gets a visit from his mother at work. She confesses that her son Toni was taken away by the authorities because she smoked joints with a friend in the presence of the child and Toni suffered smoke poisoning in the process. Malony is furious, steals a car on December 24th, breaks into the foster home and takes Toni. When he tries to call his mother, Malony tries to stop him. The car overturns. Malony is taken into custody shortly thereafter by Florence Blaque. Malony says thank you. Yann's out of his mind. In prison, Malony gets a visit from his mother. Tess confesses to him that she's pregnant, but Malony doesn't want the child. At the court hearing about the accident and the theft of the car, Malony apologizes to those who were injured. Florence Blaque sentences him to six months in prison, five of them on probation, followed by six months in another CEF. Since Malony has already spent a month in pre-trial detention, he will be taken directly to the CEF. He freaks out when he finds out Tess is in the hospital having an abortion. He commits himself to her and the child and prevents the abortion. Because of his escape, he is not allowed to take a trip with his mother as planned shortly thereafter. He wounds the heavily pregnant head of the CEF, causing Sévérine to lash out and Malony to speak harshly. For the first time, she's assuming responsibility as a mother. As a result, Maloney's behavior is improving. He works in the timber industry as part of the CEF and drives a forklift truck. He develops trust in Yann and plans to be there for his child. He's celebrating his 17th birthday at the CEF. Soon after, he's going to be a father. With the baby in his arms, he goes to Florence Blaque. She's going into retirement, ten years of her working life spent, among other things, taking care of Malony. Malony is slowly leaving the courthouse with his child.
story_text_b:
Malony is 11 years old. His young mother Séverine, irresponsible, drug addict and unstable, does not provide a satisfactory emotional and educational environment. He was placed by children's judge Florence Blaque in several increasingly restrictive institutions. His disastrous schooling is interrupted, he is prone to violent outbursts that he cannot control, and crime increases. However, the magistrate persists in trying to help him in spite of the little results she achieves and despite the often hostile, but sometimes affectionate, behavior of the young boy, who is attached more than anything to his mother and younger brother.
When he's 16, Malony is taken in by Yann, a forensic educator determined to save him, protected by this judge who believes in him, he oscillates between progress and relapse but lifts his head up to what may be a fulfilled life expectancy.

story_text_a:
The narrator of the story, the historian Dietrich Knickerbocker, first introduces the scene of the action, the so-called "sleepy canyon". The small side valley of the Hudson River near Tarrytown, where the customs of the Dutch colonists have remained almost unchanged, is popularly believed to be an enchanted place; it is perpetually under the control of some magic power which exercises its dominion over the minds of good people and causes them to wander about in a perpetual dream. They believe in all kinds of miracles, are subject to spells and faces, often see all kinds of strange apparitions, and hear music and strange voices in the air. The most terrifying of these apparitions is a "Headless Horseman", the ghost of a Hessian mercenary from the American Revolutionary War, who is reputed to ride at night to the former battlefield to look for his severed head.
"About thirty years ago" Ichabod Crane, a scholarly but superstitious rural schoolmaster from Connecticut, disappeared into this peaceful corner. In the schoolhouse, he teaches the "small, tough, stubborn, broad-shouldered Dutch boys" and teaches the peasants to sing psalms. He especially enjoys the Dutch cuisine and soon catches the eye of Katrina van Tassel, a farmer's daughter with a particularly lavishly filled pantry, on whose hand Abraham van Brunt, called "Brom Bones", also puts his hopes. One autumn day, Crane is invited to a banquet at the van Tassels'. After the elaborately described meal and the ensuing dancing pleasure, a social round of shocking stories is told; Brom Bones claims to have met the headless rider himself and won a horse race with him.
As night falls, Crane makes his way home. Again and again, he is startled by eerie noises and strange shapes in the ghost as he rides. Suddenly, he sees a "great horseman" riding a black horse of powerful form. The figure rides alongside him without saying a word, and as the light briefly lights up, Crane sees that the figure had no head! but his horror grows as he realizes that he is carrying the head that should have been on his shoulders on the saddle button in front of him. Terrified, he drives his horse, but the figure sets off in pursuit. Just before Crane reaches the saving church bridge, the ghostly rider rises, throws his head at the fleeing schoolmaster, and throws Crane off his horse.
The next morning, Ichabod Crane was gone. A search party found only his horse and a crushed pumpkin on the bridge. At least the old women of the valley are convinced that Ichabod was led away by the galloping Hesse. However, according to Knickerbocker, a traveler later brought news from New York that Crane was still alive and had tried his luck elsewhere. Katharina van Tassel, meanwhile, was married to Brom Bones. The latter was always seen making a very sarcastic face when Ichabod's story was told.
story_text_b:

She's chaotic but beautiful and always happy. She's flooded with men as soon as they find out she's divorced her husband. Only her dentist Dr. Agartz shows himself distracted during the treatment, does not recognize her and reveals to her that Robert will marry again and that it was only his ex who caused the separation anyway. Thesi is displeased. Memories of her marriage to Robert lead to the realization that the two were always arguing over small things. It's her fault, for example, that he was never home and that she'd redecorated the apartment in the meantime. At one point, Thesi got fed up and spontaneously packed her things.
She's going out on her own. The writer Niki Springer and the German consul in Mexico Georg Lindberg notice her in a cafe. Betsy, who loves them both unsuccessfully, brings Thesi to her table; she had met Thesi when she was preparing her German visa. Niki and Georg fall in love with Thesi, who engages with both of them to annoy Robert. At her engagement party, she appears unexpectedly in a boldly cut dress, introduces the two men as her lovers, smokes a cigarette and leaves after a short time. The audience and Karin, Robert's fiancée, are left in shock.
Thesi and Georg are a couple. Although Thesi has repeatedly spoken out against the marriage, she becomes romantic when Robert's marriage to Karin approaches and Georg has to return to Mexico. She agrees to Georg's fourth request, and the two plan to sail to Mexico together in a few days. Thesi already feels sick during the celebration. The next day, she's in the hospital for scarlet fever. Thesi is only slowly improving. She's using the time to think about her feelings. In the end, it's clear to her that she loves Robert more than Georg. Georg returns to Mexico alone, but thanks Thesi for the most beautiful summer months he has ever spent. Meanwhile, Robert broke up with Karin, who realized he could never escape her ex. When Thesi enters her penthouse apartment, all the furniture is gone. Before she can call the police, Robert is standing in front of her. He brought her furniture back to her apartment while she was in the hospital, where most of it was also before the divorce. He's taking Thesi home with him. Just after he left for work, Thesi spontaneously rearranged the apartment. This time, Robert jokingly asks her to marry him, which she accepts.

She felt that they had treated her in a way that was shameful and that made her feel exploited. Karl Marx and his Theories of Surplus Value accompanied her in her approach to "putting things in order", as she said: a writer is a productive worker, not because he produces ideas, but because he enriches his publisher when he exploits his writings. The writer thus becomes the wage-earner of a capitalist. She specifically confronted three publishers: the very important Paul Cassirer, the publisher and art dealer, Alfred Flechtheim and the publisher Kurt Wolff. story_text_a:
Jennifer Brea is a Harvard PhD student about to marry the love of her life, when she is struck down by a fever that leaves her bedridden. Months before her wedding, she becomes progressively more ill, eventually losing the ability even to sit in a wheelchair. When doctors tell her it's "all in her head", she goes online and finds a hidden world of millions confined to their homes and bedrooms by myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME), also commonly called chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS).
Unrest tells the story of Jennifer and her husband Omar Wasow, as newlyweds grappling with how to live in the face of a lifelong illness. In search of answers and initially bedbound, Jennifer sets off on a virtual voyage around the world, meeting four extraordinary ME patients in the US, UK, and Denmark. Their bedrooms connected by Skype and Facebook, these patients teach Jen how to make a life of meaning when everything changes.
story_text_b:
Jennifer Brea is a Harvard student about to marry the love of her life, when she is attacked by a fever that leaves her bedridden. Months before the wedding, she does not recover but her health worsens, reaching the point where she cannot even sit in a wheelchair. When doctors tell you "it's all in your head", you find a hidden world of thousands of people with the same symptoms, via the Internet. These people, unable to leave their homes, and in the most severe cases in bed, suffer from myalgic encephalomyelitis or chronic fatigue syndrome.
Unrest tells the story of Jennifer and her husband Omar, in which as newlyweds they have to face living together when one person suffers from a severe and chronic illness. In search of answers, initially bedridden, Jennifer embarks on a virtual journey around the world, meeting four extraordinary people suffering from CFS from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Denmark. In their separate rooms, connected via Skype and Facebook, these patients will teach Jennifer how to find meaning in her life when everything changes.
Unrest is an autobiographical story of resistance after the change of a life that is deeply altered after being attacked by CFS, showing how people are treated who suffer from this disease that is not yet fully understood, as well as how it happens that, realizing the extreme fragility of life as everything changes, this fact ends up showing us its crudeness as well as the value of it. It also makes a review of how all people need to find a community where there is a real connection within it.[14]

story_text_a:
Snow-White and Rose-Red are two little girls living with their mother, a poor widow, in a small cottage by the woods. Snow-White is quiet and shy and prefers to spend her time indoors, doing housework and reading. Rose-Red is outspoken, lively and cheerful, and prefers to be outside. They are both very good girls who love each other and their mother dearly, and their mother is very fond of them as well.
One winter night, there is a knock at the door. Rose-Red opens the door to find a bear. At first, she is terrified, but the bear tells her not to be afraid. "I'm half frozen and I merely want to warm up a little at your place," he says. They let the bear in, and he lies down in front of the fire. Snow-White and Rose-Red beat the snow off the bear, and they quickly become quite friendly with him. They play with the bear and roll him around playfully. They let the bear spend the night in front of the fire. In the morning, he leaves trotting out into the woods. The bear comes back every night for the rest of that winter and the family grows used to him.
When summer comes, the bear tells them that he must go away for a while to guard his treasure from a wicked dwarf. During the summer, when the girls are walking through the forest, they find a dwarf whose beard is stuck in a tree. The girls rescue him by cutting his beard free, but the dwarf is ungrateful and yells at them for cutting his beautiful beard. The girls encounter the dwarf several times that summer and rescue him from some peril each time, for which he is ungrateful.
Then one day, they meet the dwarf once again. This time, he is terrified because the bear is about to kill him. The dwarf pleads with the bear and begs it to eat the girls. Instead, the bear pays no heed to his plea and kills the dwarf with one swipe of his paw. Instantly, the bear turns into a prince. The dwarf had previously put a spell on the prince by stealing his precious stones and turning him into a bear. The curse is broken with the death of the dwarf. Snow-White marries the prince and Rose-Red marries the prince's brother.

story_text_a:
A mysterious, white-clad man drops a long-haired woman into a well. The well is full of women, all with long hair, all dressed in night-dresses.
Thirteen years after the original film, two suicides prompt Detective Koiso and his partner to investigate a string of mysterious deaths. The deaths involve video played on devices; just before the deaths, a voice says, "You're not the one". While Koiso is unconvinced, his partner deduces that the deaths are the result of a cursed video that online artist Seiji Kashiwada created.
Akane Ayukawa, teacher of a schoolgirl who died, discovers the schoolgirl's best friend Risa had been looking into the cursed video. The video had been deleted, but the Error 404 message in its wake prompts the video to play when the viewer is alone. In it, Kashiwada allows himself to be killed by a long-haired woman. When the video ends, Risa is attacked; Akane arrives just in time to save her. The ghost tells Akane that she is "the one". Akane screams, and the computer is destroyed. Meanwhile, Koiso and his partner scout Kashiwada's apartment, noting the furniture and decorative wallpaper, which look like a set. The landlady notes that everything is superficial.
Akane is a telekinetic who displayed her power years ago when a maniac attacked her high school. Though she saved the school, she was branded a freak. Takanori Andō, son of Mitsuo Andō from the previous film, and a boy who appreciates her abilities, grows up to be her boyfriend. She soon realizes the video is targeted at her when, at their home, the video plays and the woman appears. Multiple screens show the woman attacking. Takanori and Akane run to a street, where they believe themselves safe, but a large LCD display truck shows a giant version of the ghost, who snatches Takanori away.
Until his partner commits suicide in front of him, Detective Koiso continues to doubt the existence of the film, even when it is revealed that the original broadcast of the online video killed its initial viewers and employees of the site where it was uploaded. Koiso makes his way to Kashiwada's apartment, eager to find answers. He discovers the wallpaper is a horde of white butterflies hiding notes and history. Kashiwada had been attempting to resurrect Sadako Yamamura, as revenge against the human populace for persecuting him. He initially kidnapped long-haired women and threw them down the well, alive. However, when it was revealed that a body could not be found that way, he orchestrated the "cursed video" so that the video would find the perfect host for her.
Koiso finds Akane, whom he'd interrogated previously, and the two of them journey to the old Yamamura household. It no longer has the inn, and a "new" decrepit mall was beside the well. Upon approach to the well, a freakish-looking Sadako facsimile appears and attacks Koiso, biting his neck. The women that had been thrown into the well had become imperfect versions of Sadako. They attack Akane, but with stealth and resistance, Akane prevails against the imperfect Sadakos.
When she arrives at the center of the derelict building, she discovers Takanori had been trapped in a mobile phone at the center of the room. A legion of imperfect Sadakos arrive, but her fear triggers her telekinetic powers, which decimates them. Akane is transported to the roof where the "real" Sadako has been waiting. Sadako says they are exactly the same, which Akane denies; Sadako uses her powers to destroy, while she helps people. Seeing Takanori with a knife to his throat, Akane trades herself for his life. Sadako agrees and goes into her. Akane is overlain with a large amount of the ghost's hair and is buried inside it.
Takanori, now free from Sadako's thrall, destroys the phone. The roof gives and Akane drops to the floor below covered in Sadako's hair, but she escapes alive. In a mid-credits scene, it was shown that just outside the building beside the well, Kashiwada's landlord moves away and her words, "Isn't it all artificial?" echo. In the post-credits scene, the intro to Kashiwada's video plays again, but his introduction changes: "Here we go again".
story_text_b:
It's the Soviet Union during perestroika. Drug trafficking there has begun to appear on a large scale. Ivan Danko, a captain in the Soviet militia, sets a trap for Viktor Rostavili, a major Georgian drug lord. The ambush fails and Viktor escapes from the Soviet Union to the United States, after killing several Moscow police officers including Danko's partner.
Once in the United States, Viktor is arrested for a traffic violation and his arrest is reported to Moscow. Danko is therefore sent to Chicago to carry out Viktor's extradition. There, Art Ridzik, a pompous detective-sergeant from the Chicago Police Department, is assigned as Danko's bodyguard and guide. On the way to the airport, Danko is attacked by a clan of local African-American drug dealers, who are allies of Viktor and in the subsequent shootout Ridžić's partner is killed and Viktor is freed.
In charge of catching him, Danko and Ridžić chase Viktor and his henchmen all over Chicago. Eventually, Danko and Viktor commandeer some buses and engage in a chase until Viktor crashes into a train, after which a shootout between them begins. Danko, carrying an S&W Model 29.44 Magnum given to him by Ridžić, confronts Viktor with the weapon with which he killed his partner in Moscow. Finally Viktor is shot by Danko, who concludes that "he likes the Soviet model better", referring to the revolver that was confiscated from him. Danko returns to Moscow after having exchanged the wristwatch with Ridžić as a sign of friendship.

story_text_a:
In 1936, archaeology professor and adventurer Dr. Jones, nicknamed "Indiana Jones" or "Indy", discovers a temple dotted with traps in the Peruvian jungle and steals a golden idol. Leaving the temple, his French rival Belloq waits for him with warriors of the natives and takes the figure back, Indy escapes at the last second with a seaplane.
Back at his university, he and Brody, the university curator, receive a visit from two representatives of American military intelligence. They instruct Indy to secure the Ark of the Covenant before it falls into Hitler's hands, who also sends for it. There are many myths surrounding the Ark, so an army with the Ark at its head is said to be invincible.
After initial skepticism, Indy takes the job. First, he needs the head of Re's staff, a kind of amulet that can help him locate the Ark's whereabouts. It's owned by Marion Ravenwood, the daughter of Indy's former mentor and his estranged love, who lives as a bar owner in Nepal. Indy flies there, but Marion resents him for ditching her years ago, and doesn't hand him the head piece. As soon as Indy leaves her bar, the Nazi thugs appear around Gestapo Major Toht, who also covets the head. Before Toht can torture Marion, Indy shows up and a fight breaks out, leading to a fire. The head falls into the flame, and when Toht tries to take it, the blazing metal burns into his hand. He escapes and Indy is able to defeat the remaining attackers, but Marion's bar burns down.
With the rescued head piece, the two of them will travel to Cairo. With Belloc's help, the Nazis under Colonel Dietrich have found the ancient city of Tanis and are digging for the Ark. Indy's old friend Sallah has insight into the Germans' excavation work. The Nazis, however, are on their trail. Marion is kidnapped and apparently killed in an explosion, while Indy and Sallah escape multiple assassination attempts. Sallah tells that the Nazis are using a replica of the head to dig for a hall called the "Fountain of Souls" where the Ark is supposed to be located. Indy has the inscription of his headpiece translated and learns that the staff for the headpiece must be six kadams long. But on the back of the headpiece, it says that you must wear a kadam in honor of the Hebrew god. Since the Nazis with the burn scar on Toht's hand only have the front of the headpiece, they miscalculated the length and dug in the wrong place.
After reuniting with Indy Belloq in a bar, Sallah helps him into the so-called card room, a hall with a model of Tanis and a hole in the ceiling. Indy puts a stick of the right length, with the headpiece at the top, in a certain spot, and as the sun shines through the ceiling opening at the right angle, the crystal in the center of the headpiece concentrates the sun's rays and illuminates in the model of the city the building where the box is supposed to be.
With some workers at night, Indy finds the opening to the "Fountain of Souls" and the box, but they are surprised by Belloq and Dietrich. They transport the crate and lock Indy and Marion in the building, the floor of which is covered with hundreds of snakes. Indy finds an exit and pursues Dietrich's wagon column on horseback. After a chase, he can take the truck with the trunk. Sallah arranges for him, Marion and the box to board a cargo ship, but it is picked up on the high seas by a German submarine. Dietrich and Belloq take over the cargo and put Marion on the sub, but Indy manages to sneak aboard before it sinks.
On an island north of Crete, the submarine, commanded by Oskar Schomburg, is stuck in a camouflaged submarine harbor. Inside the island, Belloq and Dietrich want to open the box. Indy tries to free Marion by threatening to destroy the crate with a tank fist. But Belloq realizes that Indy is bluffing and can't destroy this precious historical artifact, and has him arrested. In the evening, Belloq celebrates a ritual in which, in addition to Dietrich and Toht, numerous soldiers also participate, as well as Indy and Marion, who are tied to a pole. Belloq, in the garb of a high priest, utters an incantation, and two soldiers lift the lid of the ark. This, however, contains only the dust of the shattered tablets of the Law of Moses. Suddenly, all the electrical appliances explode, and supernatural, ghostly lights float out of the box and surround those present. Indy begs Marion not to look under any circumstances. Finally, lightning strikes the box and melts everyone in it except Indy and Marion, who survive the inferno with their eyes closed. Finally, the lid of the ark is hurled upward by a huge pillar of fire, landing back on the ark and closing it.
Back home, Indy and Brody will be denied any further access to the federal vault. Government officials assure them that the box is currently being investigated by "absolute specialists". In reality, however, the box is stored in a wooden box labeled "Top Secret" and housed in a huge government storage facility with thousands of other similar wooden boxes. Finally, Indy and Marion are reunited.
story_text_b:
This is Peru, 1936. Professor Henry Walton Jones Jr. (pronounced  Indiana, or  Indy ), a prominent American archaeologist and expert in the occult, is about to get his hands on a Chachapoyan idol. After escaping a series of deadly traps in an ancient temple, he is dishonestly robbed of the relic by his main rival, a French archaeologist, René Belloq. Indy manages to get rid of the Hovito Indians aboard a seaplane but returns empty-handed to the United States.
Returning from his trip to Marshall College in Bedford, Connecticut, Jones was ordered by U.S. Secret Service agents seeking to decrypt a cable from supporters of the Third Reich. The Nazis seem to be on the trail of the Ark of the Covenant, containing the Tablets of the Law, from the site of Tanis in Egypt. Since the Ark is supposed to confer the power to lead any army to victory, it must under no circumstances fall into the hands of Adolf Hitler. In their quest for occult power, the Nazis sought out Abner Ravenwood, Jones' former mentor and expert on the subject. Ravenwood possesses the medallion of Ra, an artifact that according to legend allows for the precise location of the holy relic in the  Well of Souls.
Indiana Jones flies to Nepal to find Ravenwood, who he hasn't spoken to in years. He learns from Marion, the daughter of his mentor and former love with a temper, that the old man is dead. Marion has the medallion so coveted that Indy offers to buy it for $3,000, plus $2,000 to allow her to return to the United States. Marion accepts the sale but the tavern is stormed by bandits led by Gestapo officer Arnold Toht. During the altercation, the establishment caught fire and Toht burned his hand trying to grab the medallion. Indy and Marion escape with the artifact and head for Egypt.
Arriving in Cairo, the couple reunited with Sallah, an iconic figure in the city and an old friend of Jones. The latter informs Indy that Belloq allied himself with the Nazis, under the orders of Colonel Dietrich, to excavate the Tanis site thanks to the medallion inscriptions embedded in Toht's burned palm. In the town's souk, Marion is kidnapped and forcibly taken away in a truck that Jones accidentally blows up. The adventurer is devastated by the death of his former love, but decides with the help of Sallah to continue the search. They realize that the Nazis are digging in the wrong place because the other side of the coin provides crucial precision that Toht lacks. Indiana infiltrates the excavation site and discovers that Marion is not dead but held captive by Belloq. The Ark of the Covenant is soon discovered in the heart of the  Well of Souls  teeming with serpents. The Nazis seize the sacred artifact and seal the well, leaving Indy and Marion behind.
The couple escape and discover that the Ark is about to be transported to Berlin aboard a flying wing, an experimental aircraft. Indy attempts to sabotage the operation by destroying the device, after a fistfight with one of the mechanics that results in the death of the latter, shredded by a propeller. Dietrich, Toht and Belloq boarded with the Ark and their troops aboard a convoy of trucks. After a frantic pursuit through the desert, Jones succeeded in capturing the truck containing the Ark, but at the cost of multiple injuries and bruises. Marion treats him, and they resume their romantic relationship.
Indiana and Marion leave Egypt aboard a cargo ship commanded by Captain Katanga. But just when they thought they were safe out of territorial waters, they are caught by a German submarine. Dietrich once again takes possession of the Ark and Belloq kidnaps Marion. Jones manages to elude and hide outside the submarine to an island in the Aegean Sea where Belloq plans to open the golden chest. The archaeologist stops the Nazis by threatening to destroy everything with a rocket launcher. But he is reasoned by Belloq who thinks he is incapable of destroying such a testimony of history. In fact, Jones doesn't have the guts. He is disarmed, captured, and nailed to a stake with Marion. Belloq performs an ancient ceremony to open the Ark and it turns out it contains nothing but sand... But suddenly, spirits resembling the seraphs of the Old Testament emerge from the ark. Indiana, knowing the danger from studying the relic with her mentor, orders Marion to close her eyes and not look at it. The spirits took on the terrifying appearance of angels of death, and blinding rays began to strike the Nazis. Belloq, Dietrich, and Toht die a horrible death because of the ghostly gaze.
In the epilogue, set in Washington, D.C., government officials assure Indy that the Ark is being studied in a secure location by experts and will not be accessible to researchers. The archaeologist is furious. The Ark is actually labeled  Top Secret  and commonly stored in a giant dusty hangar filled with hundreds of boxes with uncertain contents. We'll learn in the movie Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull that this hangar is in Area 51 in Nevada and, much to the delight of the archaeologist, it will not be studied...

story_text_a:
Winfried Conradi, a retired music teacher from Aachen who lives alone, is prone to quirky jokes. The 68-year-old also runs courses at the school and maintains an apparently relaxed relationship with the mother of his daughter Ines and the mother's partner. Ines, on the other hand, has become a stranger to him, work dominates her life even in the family circle, and she is working on a career as a business consultant in Bucharest.
After his beloved dog Willi dies, Winfried takes a vacation to surprise Ines. She's looking forward to a presentation for client Henneberg from the petroleum industry, and she's not very happy about it. But she's taking her father to a reception where she wants to meet Henneberg. He first leaves Ines with his young, blonde, Ukrainian girlfriend Natalya, talks to others and then turns to Winfried, who jokes that he has hired a "substitute daughter" for lack of his own, who also cuts his toenails. To Ines' horror, Henneberg finds this amusing and invites Winfried against Ines' plan with a late-night round at a club. There, Ines makes a faux pas: she speaks openly about staff reductions and is reprimanded by Henneberg. Winfried immediately tries to protect her in his own way.
On the next Saturday, Winfried has again little of Ines, who decide to focus on supporting Natalja in the "shopping". When she falls asleep on Sundays and misses Henneberg's calls, all her frustration is directed at the unsuspecting and guiltless father, who finally seems to leave in the evening. On the Monday before the presentation, Ines surprises Gerald's supervisor with a change of tactics discussed, as the exchange with Henneberg did not go as desired. She rejects her colleague Tim, who happens to be her lover. The presentation, however, is not entirely satisfactory.
When she finally wants to relax with two friends in the evening, Winfried suddenly reappears: With a dark wig and protruding teeth, recognized only by Ines, he pushes himself with champagne and as Toni Erdmann, with Ion Țiriac known as Businessman, the irritated but amused women. In this disguise, he interferes in her daily life from now on.
After some irritation, she finally takes her father to a meeting with Illiescu, head of the affected local oil department, and introduces him, to her own surprise, as an experienced consultant. Winfred's conversation with oil workers unintentionally ends fatally when Illiescu fires one of the workers on the spot. To her father's horror, Ines responds sarcastically by denying herself a discharge. When Winfried is also grateful for the hospitality of the workers, Ines attacks him on the way back, his "green mentality" is opposed to a "modernization" and thus her work.
When she finally falls asleep in the car, Winfried follows the invitation of the fleeting Flavia to the traditional Easter egg dyeing. Ines, waking up, follows him and sees him introduce himself as the "German Ambassador" and her as the secretary "Miss Schnuck". Only reluctantly, she finally agrees to perform the song Greatest Love of All accompanied by her father on the keyboard as "fabulous Whitney Schnuck". Despite the applause, she leaves the apartment without saying a word. Winfried, perplexed, descends the stairs in the hallway of the house, with a Kukeri costume in the background. He reveals himself to Flavia, who turns to him, but has already seen through him, and stays for dinner.
Meanwhile, the catering service is waiting outside Ine's apartment for her birthday brunch, which, to Gerald's delight, will also serve as team building. The next day everything is ready when Ines wants to change her painstakingly made, tight outfit and the doorbell rings in the middle of the equally difficult undressing. Spontaneously, she opens Steph intentionally almost naked, refuses their help in getting dressed, and declares the brunch a naked party. Steph refuses, as does Tim, and they both leave. On the other hand, Anca and Gerald, Tim's informants, assistant and boss, come undressed in spite of their discomfort. In front of Gerald, however, a silent, long-haired cookie monster appears, which frightens Anca as much as Gerald, who finds it "cool". Using a pretext, Ines follows the costumed man into a park, wearing only a thin bathing suit, and finally calls out, "Daddy!" After a warm embrace, they part without saying a word.
Some time later, Ines comes to the funeral of her grandmother, Winfred's mother. By changing jobs, however, she was able to reach her goal and leave Romania for Singapore. In a belated response to her question in Bucharest, Winfried explains that important moments in life cannot be captured and understood only afterwards. So she puts on his prank bite and grandma's hat, which encourages Winfried to go get the camera. With her thoughts alone, she stays behind in the garden.
story_text_b:
Orphan Max Brinkley and his friends Scott Sanders and Jessica Taylor stick together like peas in a pod. They have all kinds of pranks on their minds with their teachers and all other fellow humans. Max's uncle, Rick, raises him and owns Brinkley Technologies, a company that develops cutting-edge technology for the intelligence community. Thus the three children always have the latest inventions at their disposal.
What they don't know is that a secret agency is already secretly watching and admiring their abilities. In school, everything is interesting except the subject matter. However, Principal Henderson is keeping a close eye on all three. Above all, he must repeatedly pronounce punishments. One of them is the interesting job of helping Game Inc. develop new video games.
There, she receives a DVD that reveals the exact location of a stolen top-secret FBI microchip. At night, they break into the warehouse and actually take possession of the chip. However, during their escape, they are discovered and tied up by the criminal Daniels and his accomplice Jeff. The children alert the police, who can arrest both criminals. Max, Scott and Jessica are getting an offer from the Secret Service. They're supposed to do undercover work that adult agents aren't cut out for.
During the senior prom, where Max dances happily with his beloved Nicole, Uncle Rick picks the four of them up in a helicopter and hands Max a thank-you letter from the President of the United States.

story_text_a:
In the final weeks of World War II, a bandage-wrapped man awakens with amnesia in a U.S. military field hospital in Okinawa. Over the course of his long recovery, he learns that he is George W. Taylor, a marine who was severely wounded by an enemy grenade. Among Taylor's personal items is an unsigned letter that vehemently curses him for an unspecified wrong he committed against the writer. Mortified at the letter and the possibility that he is a bad person, Taylor resolves to hide his amnesia and uncover his original identity without anyone's help.
Taylor begins his investigation in Los Angeles, his registered place of residence. He finds a note in an old briefcase of his advising him that an account had been opened in his name at a local bank by an apparent friend named Larry Cravat. In the course of Taylor's search for Cravat, he ends up in a nightclub called The Cellar. As Taylor asks around for anyone who might know Cravat, the bartender alerts two thugs about his inquiry. To evade the thugs, Taylor slips into the dressing room of singer Christy Smith, where he finds an old postcard directed to Christy from a woman named Mary announcing her impending marriage to Larry Cravat. He takes the postcard and leaves as Christy summons the nightclub's bouncer.
Taylor later returns to The Cellar at the request of the bartender, who called claiming to have information about Larry Cravat, but it is a trap and he is seized by the thugs, who are henchmen of the gangster Anzelmo. Taylor is brutally interrogated to give up Cravat's whereabouts, and then dumped at the address on the postcard, Christy's apartment. Upon being revived by Christy's care, Taylor asks her about Mary, who he assumes is Cravat's wife. Christy relates that Cravat left Mary at the altar, and she subsequently died in a pedestrian accident. Taylor decides to confide in Christy about his amnesia.
Christy introduces Taylor to Mel Phillips, the genial proprietor of The Cellar, who in turn arranges a meeting with LAPD Lieutenant Donald Kendall to shed some light on the mysterious Larry Cravat. Taylor uses the alias Tom Carter during the meeting to protect himself. Kendall reveals that years ago, a Nazi official who planned to defect sent his nest egg of $2 million in cash to America for safekeeping, but was executed before he could make his escape from Germany. The money, which was in $1,000 bills that could not be spent or exchanged without attracting government attention, changed hands many times until it was brought to Los Angeles in December 1942. Cravat, a private detective at the time, is alleged to have stolen the money and murdered its carrier before vanishing. As he leaves, Kendall notes that the police want to question George Taylor, since his recent activities have stirred up the Cravat case.
A message signed "L.C." is found on Christy's car, which eventually leads Taylor to Terminal Dock and the office of the fortune teller Dr. Oracle, who Taylor recognizes as Anzelmo. Explaining that he is also hunting for Cravat to obtain the $2 million, Anzelmo divulges that the money's original carrier was a man named Steele, and Steele's murder took place at Terminal Dock. The crime was witnessed by a dockworker named Michael Conroy, who saw an unidentified third man in the area with Cravat and Steele. Anzelmo accuses Taylor of being the third man, and warns him that if he does not help him contact Cravat, he will use his detailed knowledge of Steele's murder to frame Taylor as the killer. Taylor tracks Michael Conroy to Lambeth Sanatorium, narrowly avoiding being hit by a speeding truck in the process, only to find Michael dying of a recent stab wound. In his last moments, Michael shares that after the Steele murder, he found a suitcase that had been left behind and hid it under Terminal Dock; Michael dies before he can name the suitcase's owner and Steele's killer.
Lt. Kendall visits Christy's apartment in search of Taylor, having determined that her friend "Tom Carter" was Taylor by planting the "L.C." note as bait, and warns that he is now wanted for the murder of Michael Conroy.
